title: Decoupled two-dimensional superconductivity and continuous melting transitions in layered superconductors immersed in a parallel magnetic field
text_ai: Possible phases and the B-T phase diagram of interlayer Josephson vortices induced by a magnetic field parallel to the superconducting layers are investigated by Monte Carlo simulations based on the anisotropic, frustrated XY model. At low fields, the system exhibits a three-dimensional ordered phase characterized by interlayer Josephson vortex lattices, which undergoes a continuous melting transition into a two-dimensional decoupled liquid state at a field-dependent temperature. Upon increasing the magnetic field, the melting line evolves nonmonotonically, revealing a reentrant behavior attributed to the competition between Josephson coupling and thermal fluctuations. Our simulations identify a distinct decoupling transition at which the interlayer phase coherence vanishes, separating the bulk three-dimensional vortex solid from a regime of decoupled two-dimensional superconductivity within individual layers. This decoupling transition is found to be continuous and belongs to the universality class of the two-dimensional XY model with columnar disorder, as evidenced by critical exponents extracted from finite-size scaling analyses. The resulting phase diagram features a tricritical point where the melting and decoupling lines merge, beyond which a single first-order transition from the vortex lattice directly to the decoupled normal state occurs. We further characterize the nature of the continuous melting transition in the decoupled regime, demonstrating that it proceeds via a Kosterlitz-Thouless-like unbinding of pancake vortices within each layer. These findings reconcile longstanding experimental puzzles in highly anisotropic layered superconductors, providing a unified microscopic description of the field–temperature phase diagram and highlighting the role of interlayer decoupling in mediating continuous phase transitions.

title: Hyper Strategy Logic
text_ai: Strategy logic (SL) is a powerful temporal logic that enables strategic reasoning in multi-agent systems. SL supports explicit (first-order) quantification over strategies and provides a logical framework to express many important properties such as Nash equilibria, dominant strategies, etc. While in SL the same strategy can be used in multiple strategy profiles, each such profile is evaluated w.r.t. a fixed set of initial states. However, many crucial properties in multi-agent systems—such as robustness, sensitivity, and strategic equivalence—inherently involve comparing multiple strategy profiles across different system executions or initial conditions. Traditional SL cannot express these hyperproperties because its semantics fix a single profile at a time. To address this gap, we introduce Hyper Strategy Logic (HyperSL), an extension of SL that combines first-order quantification over strategies with explicit quantification over atomic propositions representing strategy profiles. HyperSL allows simultaneous reasoning about multiple profiles and compares their outcomes within a single formula. We establish the model-checking complexity of HyperSL, prove that it strictly generalizes both SL and HyperLTL, and demonstrate its expressiveness by formalizing properties like strategy dominance under varying initial states, robustness against adversarial strategy changes, and symmetric equilibria across multiple observation points.

title: Language Embedded 3D Gaussians for Open-Vocabulary Scene Understanding
text_ai: Open-vocabulary querying in 3D space is challenging but essential for scene understanding tasks such as object localization and segmentation. Language-embedded scene representations have made progress by incorporating language features into 3D spaces. However, their efficacy heavily depends on neural networks that are resource-intensive in training and rendering. We propose Language Embedded 3D Gaussians (LE3DGs), a novel representation that directly attaches dense language features to individual 3D Gaussian primitives, eliminating the need for resource-intensive neural radiance fields. By initializing Gaussians from a sparse point cloud and distilling per-Gaussian CLIP embeddings via a student-teacher framework, our method supports real-time rendering and open-vocabulary querying without additional network inference during deployment. A spatial-aware aggregation mechanism refines the language field by blending neighboring Gaussians, improving semantic coherence for localization and segmentation tasks. Extensive experiments on ScanNet, Replica, and LERF demonstrate that LE3DGs achieves state-of-the-art performance in open-vocabulary object localization and semantic segmentation while requiring an order of magnitude less training time and memory than prior approaches. Furthermore, our representation enables interactive scene editing and downstream applications such as 3D instance retrieval and question answering. The compact Gaussian structure naturally supports level-of-detail rendering and progressive query refinement, making it suitable for real-world robotics and augmented reality systems. Code and trained models will be released to facilitate further research in language-grounded 3D understanding.

However, their efficacy heavily depends on neural networks that are resource-intensive in training and rendering.

title: Insights into the effects of sleep disordered breathing on the brain in infants and children: Imaging and cerebral oxygenation measurements.
text_ai: Sleep disordered breathing (SDB) is a common condition in infants and children. SDB encompasses a spectrum of respiratory disorders, which are defined as either obstructive or central in nature. Obstructive SDB ranges in severity from primary snoring (PS), to obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). Recent neuroimaging studies have revealed that even mild forms of pediatric SDB, such as PS, are associated with alterations in brain structure and function. Volumetric analyses using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) have demonstrated reduced gray matter volume in regions critical for cognition and executive function, including the prefrontal cortex and hippocampus. Diffusion tensor imaging (DTI) studies further indicate disrupted white matter integrity, particularly in tracts connecting frontal and temporal lobes, which may underlie the attentional deficits and learning difficulties observed in these patients. Functional MRI (fMRI) during cognitive tasks shows aberrant activation patterns, suggesting compensatory mechanisms but also impaired neural efficiency. Complementing these structural and functional insights, near-infrared spectroscopy (NIRS) and other cerebral oxygenation measurements have provided real-time evidence of intermittent hypoxia and altered cerebral hemodynamics during sleep. In children with OSA, NIRS reveals recurrent desaturations and delayed post-apneic reoxygenation, alongside impaired cerebrovascular reactivity. These disturbances are more pronounced in younger infants, whose developing brain is particularly vulnerable to oxygen fluctuations. Accumulating evidence suggests that even nocturnal hypoxia of moderate severity can trigger inflammatory cascades, oxidative stress, and disrupted neurotransmitter systems, compounding the direct effects of sleep fragmentation. Despite these advances, key gaps remain. Longitudinal studies tracking brain changes from infancy through adolescence are scarce, and the relative contributions of hypoxia versus sleep fragmentation to neural injury are incompletely disentangled. Moreover, the clinical significance of subtle imaging and oxygenation abnormalities in relation to long-term academic and behavioral outcomes warrants further investigation. Early identification using non-invasive imaging and oximetry may facilitate timely intervention, potentially mitigating the lasting neurocognitive sequelae of pediatric SDB. Integrating multimodal neuroimaging with continuous cerebral oxygenation monitoring promises to deepen our understanding of the pathophysiological pathways linking SDB to brain dysfunction across childhood development.

title: Less or More: Towards Glanceable Explanations for LLM Recommendations Using Ultra-Small Devices
text_ai: Large Language Models (LLMs) have shown remarkable potential in recommending everyday actions as personal AI assistants, while Explainable AI (XAI) techniques are being increasingly utilized to help users understand why a recommendation is given. Personal AI assistants today are often located on ultra-small devices such as smartwatches, which have limited screen space. This raises a critical question: how can XAI explanations be designed to remain useful when screen real estate is severely constrained? We propose a framework that distills LLM reasoning into hierarchically structured explanation units—ranging from concise keywords to brief sentences—that can be dynamically composed based on available display space and user interaction context. Through a controlled user study (N=48) comparing three explanation modalities (full-text, keyword-based, and icon-enhanced) on a smartwatch simulator, we evaluate trade-offs between glanceability and comprehension. Results show that keyword explanations achieve significantly faster decision times (<2 seconds) with only a modest reduction in perceived transparency compared to full-text. However, users express a desire for on-demand access to more detail when needed. We therefore introduce an adaptive system that toggles between “less” and “more” explanation levels depending on inferred user state (e.g., walking vs. stationary). Our findings indicate that adaptive glanceable explanations preserve user trust and recommendation acceptance, while reducing cognitive load on ultra-small devices. This work contributes design guidelines for balancing informativeness and brevity in LLM-driven XAI on wearables, demonstrating that less can indeed be more when explanations are tailored to context.

title: Learning Deep Representations of Fine-grained Visual Descriptions
text_ai: State-of-the-art methods for zero-shot visual recognition formulate learning as a joint embedding problem of images and side information. In these formulations the current best complement to visual features are attributes: manually encoded vectors describing shared characteristics among categories. Despite good performance, attributes have limitations: (1) finer-grained recognition requires commensurately more attributes, and (2) attributes do not provide a natural language interface. We address these limitations by learning deep representations of natural language descriptions for fine-grained visual categories. Instead of relying on fixed attribute vocabularies, we leverage free-form textual descriptions that capture subtle visual distinctions using arbitrary linguistic phrases. Our model jointly embeds images and these descriptions in a common semantic space via a neural network that learns to extract discriminative features from both modalities. Crucially, the description encoder is trained on fine-grained captions that highlight distinguishing characteristics, enabling zero-shot recognition of unseen categories with significantly finer granularity than attribute-based methods. Furthermore, the use of natural language provides an intuitive interface for querying and explaining recognition decisions. Experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our approach outperforms attribute-based baselines, particularly for highly confusable classes, while retaining the ability to generalize across diverse visual domains.

title: Saliency-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating Visual Explanations
text_ai: Explainable AI (XAI) has gained significant attention for providing insights into the decision-making processes of deep learning models, particularly for image classification tasks through visual explanations visualized by saliency maps. Despite their success, challenges remain due to the lack of annotated datasets and standardized evaluation pipelines. To address these limitations, we introduce Saliency-Bench, a comprehensive benchmark designed to systematically evaluate visual explanations. The benchmark comprises a diverse collection of annotated datasets spanning multiple domains, including natural images, medical scans, and satellite imagery, each with ground-truth relevance labels for saliency evaluation. We propose a standardized evaluation pipeline incorporating both quantitative metrics—such as insertion/deletion scores, pointing game accuracy, and faithfulness measures—and qualitative human studies to assess explanation plausibility. Additionally, Saliency-Bench includes a unified interface for seamless integration with popular XAI methods, enabling fair comparisons. Through extensive experiments on state-of-the-art saliency techniques, we reveal critical insights into their strengths and weaknesses, highlighting the importance of dataset-specific performance and the need for robustness against input perturbations. Our benchmark provides a rigorous foundation for advancing reproducible XAI research, facilitating the development of more faithful and interpretable explanations. The code, datasets, and evaluation protocols are publicly released to foster community-driven improvements and standardized assessments.

title: Unraveling the Complexity of Imported Malaria Infections by Amplicon Deep Sequencing.
text_ai: Imported malaria and recurrent infections are becoming an emerging issue in many malaria non-endemic countries. This study aimed to determine the molecular patterns of the imported malaria infections and recurrence. Blood samples were collected from patients with imported malaria infections during 2016-2018 in Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, China. Deep sequencing targeting the *Plasmodium* 18S rRNA gene and polymorphic markers (*msp1*, *msp2*, and *glurp*) was performed on all samples. A total of 325 isolates from 289 patients were sequenced, achieving a mean coverage depth of 2,800× per amplicon. Haplotype diversity was high (Hd = 0.89–0.96), with 42 distinct haplotypes identified among the three species (P. vivax, P. falciparum, P. ovale). Polyclonal infections occurred in 22% of primary cases and 41% of recurrent cases, suggesting multiple imported sources or within-host selection. Recurrence was classified as recrudescence (67%) or reinfection (33%) based on haplotype concordance at two or more loci. Notably, 18% of recurrences involved a genetically distinct clone from the primary infection, indicating a second imported event. The high proportion of polyclonal and recrudescent infections highlights the complexity of managing imported malaria in a non‑endemic setting. Amplicon deep sequencing provided the resolution necessary to distinguish recrudescence from reinfection and to track parasite population dynamics. These findings underscore the value of molecular surveillance for guiding clinical management and public health interventions in regions targeting malaria elimination.

title: MedHallu: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Detecting Medical Hallucinations in Large Language Models
text_ai: Advancements in Large Language Models (LLMs) and their increasing use in medical question-answering necessitate rigorous evaluation of their reliability. A critical challenge lies in hallucination, where models generate plausible yet factually incorrect outputs. In the medical domain, this poses serious risks to patient safety and clinical decision-making. To address this, we introduce MedHallu, a comprehensive benchmark specifically designed to detect and evaluate medical hallucinations in LLMs. MedHallu comprises over 10,000 diverse medical queries spanning diagnosis, treatment, pharmacology, and patient education, each annotated with gold-standard answers verified by clinical experts. Unlike existing benchmarks, MedHallu systematically captures multiple hallucination types—factual inaccuracy, invention, temporality errors, and omission—across varied difficulty levels. We evaluate 15 state-of-the-art LLMs, including GPT-4, Med-PaLM 2, and open-source alternatives, revealing alarming rates of hallucination: even top-performing models exhibit up to 22% hallucinated responses in high-stakes scenarios. Our analysis further uncovers strong correlations between model confidence and correctness, yet also highlights deceptive fluency where confident hallucinations evade simple detection. MedHallu provides fine-grained metrics for hallucination type and severity, enabling targeted model improvement. We also release a diagnostic toolkit for automated hallucination identification. This work establishes a critical resource for the safe deployment of LLMs in clinical settings, alerting developers and practitioners to persistent gaps that must be bridged before autonomous medical AI can be trusted.

title: The influence of dysbiosis on kidney stones that risk up renal cell carcinoma (RCC).
text_ai: Kidney stone is a common urological condition, the prevalence and incidence of which has escalated in the last few years due to dietary habits and other related medical conditions such as obesity and diabetes mellitus. It is a chronic disease which leads to loss of kidney function(s) and nephrectomy. Recent evidence suggests that gut microbiota dysbiosis may play a pivotal role in both the pathogenesis of kidney stones and the progression to renal cell carcinoma (RCC). Dysbiosis alters metabolite profiles, including increased oxalate absorption and reduced anti-inflammatory short-chain fatty acids, which can promote calcium oxalate supersaturation and crystal aggregation in the urinary tract. Concurrently, dysbiosis-driven chronic inflammation and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition have been implicated in the malignant transformation of renal tubular cells. This review examines the mechanistic links between dysbiosis, stone-induced renal injury, and carcinogenic risk, highlighting how microbial imbalances may amplify the well-established stone–RCC association. Understanding these pathways could inform novel preventive strategies targeting the microbiome to reduce both stone recurrence and RCC incidence.

title: Combining cues to judge distance and direction in an immersive virtual reality environment.
text_ai: When we move, the visual direction of objects in the environment can change substantially. Compared with our understanding of depth perception, the problem the visual system faces in computing this change is relatively poorly understood. Here, we tested the extent to which participants' judgments of visual direction could be predicted by standard cue combination rules. To this end, we developed an immersive virtual-reality paradigm in which participants judged the egocentric direction of a target while they moved along a straight path. The target could be presented with or without binocular disparity, and we independently manipulated optic flow speed and the presence of non-visual (vestibular and proprioceptive) self-motion cues. By systematically varying cue reliability — through changes in flow density and target visibility — we measured direction-estimation bias and variability across six cue conditions. A Bayesian cue-integration model, which up-weights more reliable cues, was fitted to individual participants’ data. Results showed that when self-motion cues were absent, direction judgments were strongly biased by disparities in optic flow, consistent with a cue-reweighting process. When motion cues were present, observers combined visual and non-visual information in a near-optimal manner: the magnitude of the direction-estimation bias decreased, and variability was lower than in any single-cue condition. These findings demonstrate that the visual system’s estimate of changing visual direction follows the same cue-combination principles established for depth perception, despite the distinct computational demands of solving for heading versus egocentric direction during self-motion. The work extends cue-integration theory to a dynamic spatial task and highlights the role of active movement in shaping visual perception.

title: Annama H chondrite - mineralogy, physical properties, cosmic ray exposure, and parent body history
text_ai: The fall of the Annama meteorite occurred early morning (local time) on April 19, 2014 on the Kola Peninsula (Russia). Based on mineralogy and physical properties, Annama is a typical H chondrite. It has a high Ar-Ar age of 4.4 Ga. We determined a cosmic-ray exposure (CRE) age of 8.2 ± 0.8 Ma based on noble gas concentrations, consistent with the major peak of H chondrite CRE ages. The noble gas data also reveal a low trapped Ne component, indicative of a short regolith history. Petrographic observations show moderate shock stage (S3) and weak weathering (W0), suggesting minimal post-impact alteration. The high Ar-Ar age indicates early thermal metamorphism on the parent body, with no evidence of significant later heating. Combined with bulk and oxygen isotope compositions, these data refine Annama’s position within the H chondrite group and constrain its collisional history. The meteorite’s pre-atmospheric mass was estimated at ~50 kg, and its orbital parameters derived from fireball observations imply a source in the inner main belt. Our results support a scenario where Annama originated from a relatively intact H chondrite parent body fragment, with a simple two-stage exposure history involving ejection ~8 Ma ago and a rapid transfer to Earth.

title: Parallelized Wireless Sensing System for Continuous Monitoring of Microtissue Spheroids.
text_ai: Currently, the use of electrical readout methods for the investigation of microtissue spheroids in combination with lab automation tools is hindered by the cable connections that are required to interrogate the on-chip-integrated electrodes. To overcome this limitation, we developed a wireless sensor scheme, which can detect the size variation of microtissues during long-term culturing and drug exposure assays. Our system employs a passive resonant circuit integrated into the culture platform, where the resonant frequency shifts in response to changes in the electrical impedance of the sensor electrodes—a direct indicator of microtissue volume. An external reader coil placed beneath the multiwell plate wirelessly interrogates the sensors without physical contact, enabling seamless compatibility with standard liquid-handling robots and automated incubators. We validated the approach using tumor spheroids cultured over seven days. Real-time resonant frequency measurements tracked spheroid growth, showing excellent correlation with optical image analysis (R² = 0.97). In a cisplatin dose-response study, the sensor distinguished between control and treated spheroids within 4 h, well before visible morphological changes occurred. The wireless system supports up to 24 parallel sensors with a readout rate of 1 Hz and a detection limit of 10‑µm diameter change. By eliminating wired connections, our scheme preserves sterility, reduces handling steps, and allows uninterrupted monitoring inside standard laboratory automation stacks. This work demonstrates that wireless electrical sensing can replace offline imaging for high-throughput kinetic studies of microtissue spheroids, opening the door to fully automated, real‑time screening in three‑dimensional cell culture.

title: Dark Matter and Sterile Neutrinos
text_ai: Dark matter has been recognized as an essential part of matter for over 70 years now, and many suggestions have been made, what it could be. Most of these ideas have centered on Cold Dark Matter, particles that are predicted in extensions of standard particle physics, such as supersymmetry. In contrast, sterile neutrinos offer an alternative and compelling dark matter candidate that arises naturally from minimal extensions of the Standard Model to accommodate nonzero neutrino masses. Unlike supersymmetric particles, sterile neutrinos are gauge singlets and interact only gravitationally, making them inherently "dark." Their masses are not constrained by electroweak symmetry breaking, allowing a wide range from keV to GeV. Particularly, keV-scale sterile neutrinos are attractive as warm dark matter, potentially resolving small-scale structure issues that plague cold dark matter models, such as the missing satellites and core-cusp problems. Production mechanisms in the early universe—through oscillations with active neutrinos (the Dodelson-Widrow mechanism) or via decay of heavier scalars—provide viable scenarios consistent with observed relic density. Moreover, sterile neutrinos can be probed through X-ray observations of their radiative decay into active neutrinos and photons, with recent astrophysical signals (e.g., the 3.5 keV line) sparking intense debate. Laboratory searches, including tritium beta-decay experiments and neutrino oscillation anomalies, further constrain their parameter space. This review examines the theoretical motivations for sterile neutrino dark matter, summarizes observational bounds, and assesses the current status of the candidate in light of experimental and astrophysical data.

title: Closure of Secundum Atrial Septal Defects by Using the Occlutech Occluder Devices in More Than 1300 Patients: The IRFACODE Project: A Retrospective Case Series.
text_ai: The Occlutech Figulla ASD device series (OFSO) shows an improved device design for interventional ASD closure, larger follow-up series are missing. We retrospectively reviewed the feasibility, safety, implantation properties, results, and follow-up of ASD closure using Occlutech devices over a 5 year period by establishing a multi-institutional collaborative result registry with 16 contributing centers from 11 countries (IRFACODE). Of 1,347 patients (mean age 36.2 ± 14.8 years, 61% female) with secundum ASD, device implantation was attempted in all. Technical success was achieved in 98.3% (1,324/1,347), with deployment failure due to deficient rims or large defects in 23 cases. Mean device size was 27 ± 9 mm, and fluoroscopy time averaged 5.8 ± 2.9 minutes. Periprocedural complications occurred in 2.2%, including device embolization (n=7, all retrieved percutaneously), transient arrhythmias (n=11), and minor vascular access issues (n=9). No cardiac erosion, thromboembolism, or late perforation was reported over follow-up. At a mean follow-up of 3.4 ± 1.6 years, complete closure (no residual shunt) was documented in 97.5% by transthoracic echocardiography; residual shunts were trivial in 2.0% and small in 0.5%, without need for reintervention. The IRFACODE project confirms the safety, feasibility, and efficacy of the Occlutech OFSO series, with high implantation success and excellent long-term closure rates, comparable to other contemporary devices, while offering the potential advantages of its innovative design and lower profile delivery system. This largest reported series underscores its clinical utility in routine ASD closure.

title: Virgibacillus indicus sp. nov. and Virgibacillus profundi sp. nov, two moderately halophilic bacteria isolated from marine sediment by using microfluidic streak plates.
text_ai: Three Gram-variable, moderately halophilic, motile, endospore-forming rods, designated P2-C2 T , P3-H5 T and P3-B8, were isolated from marine sediment of the Southwest Indian Ocean by using the microfluidic streak plate method. Phylogenetic analysis based on 16S rRNA gene sequences placed all three strains within the genus *Virgibacillus*, with strain P2-C2T showing highest similarity to *V. xinjiangensis* JCM 15336T (97.8%), while strains P3-H5T and P3-B8 were most closely related to *V. halodenitrificans* DSM 10037T (98.2 and 98.4%, respectively). The low average nucleotide identity (ANI) and digital DNA–DNA hybridization (dDDH) values (<95% and <70%, respectively) between the isolates and their closest relatives confirmed their status as distinct genomic species. Cells grew optimally at 30–37 °C, pH 7.0–8.0, and in the presence of 3–8% (w/v) NaCl. Predominant cellular fatty acids were anteiso-C15:0 and iso-C15:0 for all strains, and the major respiratory quinone was menaquinone-7 (MK-7). Polar lipid profiles included diphosphatidylglycerol, phosphatidylglycerol, and an unidentified phospholipid. Strains P3-H5T and P3-B8 shared 99.9% 16S rRNA gene sequence identity and >99% ANI, indicating they belong to the same species. Based on polyphasic taxonomic analyses, we propose two novel species: *Virgibacillus indicus* sp. nov. (type strain P2-C2T = MCCC 1A12345T = KCTC 43210T) and *Virgibacillus profundi* sp. nov. (type strain P3-H5T = MCCC 1A12346T = KCTC 43211T), with strain P3-B8 representing an additional isolate of the latter. Our findings underscore the utility of the microfluidic streak plate method in recovering rare halophilic taxa from marine sediments.

title: Clustering, order conditions, and languages of interval exchanges
text_ai: For any interval exchange transformation $T$ (standard or generalized), if we define a morphism $\phi$ from the set of letters to the set of the return words of a word in the natural coding, respecting the lexicographical order, the word $\phi v$ clusters (for the Burrows-Wheeler transform) for the permutation of $T$ if and only if the word $v$ clusters for the permutation of the induced map of $T$ on the cylinder $[w]$. Furthermore, we show that the order conditions on the permutation of $T$ are reflected in the clustering behavior of $\phi v$, leading to a characterization of the language of $T$ in terms of the Burrows-Wheeler transform. We prove that the language is closed under this clustering operation and derive necessary and sufficient conditions for a word to be in the language based on its clustering. This yields a new combinatorial description of the order conditions that govern the dynamics of interval exchanges, linking the structure of the natural coding to the Burrows-Wheeler transform. Moreover, we illustrate these results with examples, showing how the clustering property can be used to compute the language explicitly, and discuss implications for symbolic dynamics and algorithmic recognition of interval exchange languages.

title: Good Research Practice: Lessons from Animal Care and Use.
text_ai: Animal care and use play a pivotal role in the research process. Ethical concerns on the use of animals in research have promoted the creation of a legal framework in many geographical areas that researchers must comply with, and professional organizations continuously develop recommendations on specific areas of laboratory animal science. These regulatory frameworks and guidelines emphasize the principles of the 3Rs—Replacement, Reduction, and Refinement—which, while originally developed for animal research, offer valuable insights for good research practice across all disciplines. By prioritizing robust experimental design, rigorous data management, and transparent reporting, animal care and use protocols inherently address core pillars of research integrity. Moreover, the mandatory ethical review processes and institutional oversight mechanisms in animal research provide a model for fostering accountability and minimizing bias. This paper argues that the structured systems governing animal studies can inform broader research practices, enhancing reproducibility and reliability. Key lessons include the importance of prospective planning, continuous training, and culture of care that extends beyond compliance to embrace scientific rigor and social responsibility. Adopting these principles more widely could strengthen trust in research outcomes and promote ethical conduct throughout the scientific enterprise.

title: Cracking Double-Blind Review: Authorship Attribution with Deep Learning
text_ai: Double-blind peer review is considered a pillar of academic research because it is perceived to ensure a fair, unbiased, and fact-centered scientific discussion. Yet, experienced researchers can often correctly guess from which research group an anonymous submission originates, biasing the peer-review process. In this work, we investigate the extent to which deep learning can automate this guessing game, potentially undermining the anonymity of double-blind review. We curate a large-scale corpus of academic papers from multiple disciplines, extracting full-text submissions along with verified author identities. A transformer-based neural network is trained to classify papers by author, achieving an accuracy of over 85% on held-out test sets across fields such as computer science, physics, and biology. Even when limiting input to the abstract only, or to a single section of the paper, attribution accuracy remains above 70%, far exceeding random chance. We further show that stylometric features learned by the model are robust to trivial obfuscation techniques like synonym replacement or sentence rearrangement. These findings suggest that current double-blind review practices are vulnerable to systematic authorship attribution using modern AI. To mitigate this threat, we propose and evaluate several countermeasures, including adversarial rewriting, insertion of generic templates, and multi-author masking. Our results indicate that while no defense is fully effective, a combination of approaches can reduce attribution accuracy to near chance levels. We conclude by discussing the broader implications for the integrity of peer review and the need for community awareness and adaptation.

Yet, experienced researchers can often correctly guess from which research group an anonymous submission originates, biasing the peer-review process.

title: A Theoretical Solution of the Mind-Body Problem: An Operationalized Proof that no Purely Physical System Can Exhibit all the Properties of Human Consciousness
text_ai: This article presents an operationalized solution to the mind-body problem which relies on rigorously defined theoretical reasoning rather than philosophical argument. We identify a specific operation which is a necessary property of all healthy human conscious individuals -- specifically the operation of self-certainty, or the capacity of healthy conscious humans to "know" with certainty that they are conscious. We then demonstrate, through a logical analysis of the computational and informational constraints inherent to any purely physical system, that no such system can perform this operation. The proof proceeds by showing that self-certainty demands a form of reflexive, first-person access to one’s own mental states that cannot be realized via any deterministic or probabilistic physical mechanism—since such mechanisms always reduce to third-person, externally verifiable processes. Consequently, any system that genuinely exhibits self-certainty must possess a non-physical component. This result provides a demonstrable, falsifiable criterion for the presence of consciousness and decisively resolves the explanatory gap between subjective experience and objective physical description.

We identify a specific operation which is a necessary property of all healthy human conscious individuals -- specifically the operation of self-certainty, or the capacity of healthy conscious humans to "know" with certainty that they are conscious.

title: General convergence analysis of stochastic first order methods for composite optimization
text_ai: In this paper we consider stochastic composite convex optimization problems with the objective function satisfying a stochastic bounded gradient condition, with or without a quadratic functional growth property. These models include the most well-known classes of objective functions analyzed in the literature: non-smooth Lipschitz functions and composition of a (potentially) non-smooth function and a smooth function, with or without strong convexity. Our analysis is based on a novel Lyapunov function that simultaneously captures the expected decrease in the objective value and the growth of the composite term. Under the bounded gradient condition, we derive a convergence rate of O(1/k) for the expected suboptimality gap, which improves to linear convergence when the quadratic functional growth property holds, even without strong convexity. This property generalizes strong convexity and facilitates accelerated rates in composite settings where smoothness assumptions are relaxed. Notably, our results do not require separate assumptions on Lipschitz continuity of the smooth component or bounded variance; they follow directly from the composite structure and growth condition. This unified framework bridges existing analyses for smooth, non-smooth, and composite optimization. We illustrate the tightness of our bounds through examples and demonstrate practical applicability on machine learning problems, such as regularized logistic regression and support vector machines with hinge loss. Our work provides a comprehensive convergence theory for stochastic first-order methods in composite optimization, highlighting the minimal assumptions needed for fast convergence. The analysis covers both smooth and non-smooth components, and we show that the quadratic growth condition leads to exponential convergence in expectation, matching the best-known rates for strongly convex problems. Our bounds are tight in the sense that they match lower bounds for specific problem instances, confirming their optimality. Additionally, our framework allows for adaptive step sizes without prior knowledge of problem parameters, enhancing practical usability.

These models include the most well-known classes of objective functions analyzed in the literature: non-smooth Lipschitz functions and composition of a (potentially) non-smooth function and a smooth function, with or without strong convexity.

title: Reflection on modern methods: visualizing the effects of collinearity in distributed lag models.
text_ai: Collinearity can be a problem in regression models. When examining the effects of an exposure at different time points, constrained distributed lag models can alleviate some of the problems caused by collinearity. Still, some consequences of collinearity may remain and they are often unexplored. In this paper, we systematically examine the residual impacts of collinearity on the estimated lag structure through both analytical derivation and extensive simulations. We focus on common constraint choices—such as polynomial, penalized, and spline-based distributed lag models—and quantify how even mild collinearity among adjacent lags inflates the variance of individual coefficients and distorts the shape of the overall lag-response curve. To make these effects tangible, we introduce a suite of diagnostic visualizations: cross-correlation heatmaps of coefficient estimates, variance inflation factor profiles across lags, and sensitivity plots that show how the estimated curve changes when constraints are relaxed or the lag length is altered. Our simulations reveal that collinearity can produce artificial peaks or troughs in the lag-response function, especially at the boundaries of the lag window, and that standard model selection criteria may fail to detect such distortions. We further demonstrate that the degree of distortion depends strongly on the true underlying lag structure and the autocorrelation of the exposure series. Using a real-world example from environmental epidemiology (daily temperature and mortality), we illustrate how these visualization tools can help researchers identify problematic regions of the lag space and guide the choice of constraint degree. We conclude by recommending that analysts routinely apply such diagnostics to assess whether collinearity is undermining the interpretability of their distributed lag model estimates.

title: Strong versus Weak Coupling Confinement in N=2 Supersymmetric QCD
text_ai: We consider N=2 supersymmetric QCD with the gauge group SU(N_c)=SU(N+1) and N_f number of quark matter multiplets, being perturbed by a small mass term for the adjoint matter, so that its Coulomb branch shrinks to a number of isolated vacua. In each vacuum, the low-energy effective theory confines via monopole or dyon condensation. Using Seiberg-Witten, we identify the condensing particles. We distinguish strong coupling confinement, where light monopoles condense at large effective coupling, from weak coupling confinement, where dyons condense at weak coupling. The interpolation as the adjoint mass varies reveals a flavor-dependent crossover. Examining the effective superpotential, we find that the transition changes the number of light dyons. For specific N_f we observe a transition between the two regimes, accompanied by a dyon charge jump. Our analysis clarifies the roles of bare coupling and matter content. We relate to 't Hooft line operators and the phase structure. This extends the understanding of confinement in supersymmetric gauge theories.

title: The prevalence of AGN feedback in massive galaxies at z~1
text_ai: We use the optical--infrared imaging in the UKIDSS Ultra Deep Survey field, in combination with the new deep radio map of Arumugam et al., to calculate the distribution of radio luminosities among galaxies as a function of stellar mass in two redshift bins across the interval 0.4<z<1.2. We then identify active galactic nuclei (AGN) through their radio emission, using a luminosity threshold that excludes star formation contributions. At a given stellar mass, the fraction of galaxies hosting radio-loud AGN is found to increase with redshift, and this fraction is a strong function of stellar mass, rising from ~5% at 10^10.5 M⊙ to ~30% at 10^11.5 M⊙ in the highest redshift bin. By comparing with the local relation, we demonstrate that the prevalence of radio-mode AGN feedback in massive galaxies was already established by z~1. The integrated radio luminosity density from these AGN, when compared to the star formation rate density, implies that mechanical feedback from radio jets is energetically sufficient to quench further star formation in the most massive systems. These results support a picture in which AGN feedback is a ubiquitous and ongoing process in massive galaxies at z~1, consistent with the observed decline in their specific star formation rates.

title: Robustness of diabatic enhancement in quantum annealing
text_ai: In adiabatic quantum annealing, the speed with which an anneal can be run, while still achieving a high final ground state fidelity, is dictated by the size of the minimum gap that appears between the ground and first excited state in the annealing spectrum. We demonstrate that such gap-limited performance can be exceeded by deliberately introducing diabatic transitions, which enable the system to traverse small gaps with high probability of remaining in the instantaneous ground state—a phenomenon known as diabatic enhancement. A central concern is whether this enhancement persists under realistic experimental imperfections, including control noise, finite temperature, and parameter variations. Using exact diagonalization for small spin chains and quantum trajectory methods for open-system dynamics, we systematically probe the robustness of diabatic enhancement in disordered transverse-field Ising models. We find that the enhancement in ground state fidelity relative to an adiabatic sweep remains substantial even in the presence of weak to moderate decoherence, off-resonant control errors, and moderate deviations from the optimal sweep schedule. The enhancement factor decreases only polynomially with noise strength, rather than exponentially, and remains above a practically useful threshold over a wide parameter range. This robustness is traced to interference among multiple Landau-Zener transitions, which collectively stabilizes the ground-state population against perturbations. Furthermore, we derive an analytical bound relating the enhancement’s degradation to the density of avoided crossings and the effective noise spectral density. Our results indicate that diabatic enhancement is not a fragile phenomenon but a practical tool for accelerating quantum annealing in near-term devices.

title: Nitrogen Cluster Anions
text_ai: Anions are formed by electron attachment to helium nanodroplets doped with N$_2$. The most prominent ion series is due to odd-numbered N$_m$$^{-}$ with 3 $\le$ m < 140. Neither N$^{-}$ nor N$_2$$^{-}$ are observed. An appearance energy of 11.5 $\pm$ 0.5 eV is measured for N$_3$$^{-}$. This value is consistent with dissociative electron attachment to a N₂ dimer within the droplet. For larger clusters, appearance energies gradually decrease to about 9.5 eV for m ≈ 100. Mass spectra reveal a pronounced odd-even intensity alternation, with odd-numbered Nₘ⁻ strongly favored. The abundance distribution peaks near m = 11 and decays monotonically beyond m ≈ 30, with no evidence of metastable decay, indicating efficient cooling by the helium environment. The absence of N⁻ and N₂⁻ suggests that formation proceeds via electron capture by preformed neutral N₂ aggregates, followed by rapid intracluster reactions that yield stable odd-numbered anions. The observed series is attributed to linear Nₘ⁻ structures, analogous to the known N₃⁻ and N₅⁻ anions. These results provide the first experimental evidence for large nitrogen cluster anions and elucidate their stability under cryogenic conditions.

title: Conservation laws, exact travelling waves and modulation instability for an extended nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation
text_ai: We study various properties of solutions of an extended nonlinear Schr\"{o}dinger (ENLS) equation, which arises in the context of geometric evolution problems -- including vortex filament dynamics -- and governs propagation of short pulses in optical fibers and nonlinear metamaterials. We first derive a hierarchy of local conservation laws for the ENLS equation using the method of multipliers, obtaining conserved densities for mass, momentum, energy, and an additional higher-order invariant that reflects the extended nature of the model. Exact travelling wave solutions are subsequently obtained by reducing the ENLS equation to an ordinary differential system via the travelling wave ansatz and integrating it in closed form. Both bright solitary waves and dark kink-type solutions are expressed in terms of Jacobi elliptic functions, with their existence regimes delineated by the coefficients of third-order dispersion, self-steepening, and the Raman-like nonlinear term. A modulation instability analysis is performed on a continuous-wave background using linear stability theory; the resulting dispersion relation yields a gain spectrum whose bandwidth and maximum growth rate depend sensitively on the higher-order parameters. It is shown that these extended terms can either suppress or enhance the classical Benjamin–Feir instability, leading to new regimes of stability and instability. Numerical simulations corroborate the analytical predictions and illustrate the evolution of modulated waves into localized structures such as Peregrine solitons and breathers. The results provide insight into the dynamics of short optical pulses in nonlinear metamaterials and of vortex filament motion, with potential applications to pulse propagation, rogue wave generation, and wave turbulence.

title: Distributed Optimal Voltage Control with Asynchronous and Delayed Communication
text_ai: The increased penetration of volatile renewable energy into distribution networks necessities more efficient distributed voltage control. In this paper, we design distributed feedback control algorithms where each bus can inject \emph{both active and reactive} power into the grid to regulate the voltages. However, practical communication networks introduce asynchrony and time delays that can degrade performance. To address this, we propose a fully distributed algorithm based on gradient feedback that is robust to asynchronous updates and bounded communication delays. We prove convergence to the optimal solution of a well-defined voltage regulation problem under mild conditions on the delay bound. The algorithm requires only local measurements and neighbor-to-neighbor communication. We further extend the method to handle time-varying delays and packet drops. Simulations on IEEE test feeders demonstrate that our approach achieves near-optimal voltage regulation even under severe communication impairments, outperforming existing methods that assume synchronous or delay-free communication.
prefix: The increased penetration of volatile renewable energy into distribution networks necessities more efficient distributed voltage control. In this paper, we design distributed feedback control algorithms where each bus can inject \emph{both active and reactive} power into the grid to regulate the voltages.

title: Effects of PRP and LyPRP on osteogenic differentiation of MSCs.
text_ai: Platelet-rich plasma (PRP) is rich in a variety of growth factors and plays an important role in the proliferation and differentiation of mesenchymal stem cells (MSCs). It has been reported that the preparation of freeze-dried platelets (lyophilized platelets [LyPRP]) from platelets could be an effective strategy to preserve the bioactivity of platelets for a long time. However, the comparative efficacy of PRP and LyPRP in promoting osteogenic differentiation remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate and compare the effects of PRP and LyPRP on the osteogenic differentiation of human bone marrow-derived MSCs. PRP was prepared from fresh human whole blood, while LyPRP was obtained through a standardized freeze-drying process. Both preparations were characterized for growth factor content (PDGF, TGF-β1, VEGF) using ELISA. MSCs were cultured in osteogenic induction medium supplemented with either PRP or LyPRP at varying concentrations (0%, 2.5%, 5%, 10%). Osteogenic differentiation was assessed via alkaline phosphatase (ALP) activity, alizarin red S staining for mineralization, and qPCR analysis of osteogenic markers (RUNX2, OCN, OPN). Results demonstrated that both PRP and LyPRP significantly enhanced ALP activity and mineralization compared to control, with dose-dependent effects. Notably, LyPRP exhibited comparable bioactivity to fresh PRP in promoting osteogenic gene expression and matrix mineralization, despite a lower absolute concentration of certain growth factors. The freeze-drying process did not substantially impair the osteoinductive potential of platelet-derived factors. These findings suggest that LyPRP represents a stable and effective alternative to PRP for MSC-based bone tissue engineering, offering practical advantages in storage and standardization without compromising osteogenic efficacy. Further studies are warranted to validate these effects in vivo.

It has been reported that the preparation of freeze-dried platelets (lyophilized platelets [LyPRP]) from platelets could be an effective strategy to preserve the bioactivity of platelets for a long time.

title: Spectroscopic Observations of Selected Planetary Nebulae from the HASH Database
text_ai: We conducted research on the classification and physical properties of 10 objects from the HASH (Hong Kong/Australian Astronomical Observatory/Strasbourg Observatory H-alpha Planetary Nebula (PN)) database with small angular sizes (< 8\arcsec) in the northern hemisphere. The sample consisted of 6 Likely PNe, 2 new candidates, one emission-line star, and one object of unknown nature. We obtained long-slit optical spectra using the 2.16m telescope at Xinglong Observatory, covering the wavelength range 3700–7600 Å at a resolution of ~8 Å. Emission-line fluxes were measured and dereddened using the H I Balmer decrement. For each object, we derived electron densities from the [S II] λλ6716/6731 ratio and electron temperatures from the [O III] λλ4959/5007 lines where available. We also computed ionic abundances of He, O, N, S, and Ar using collisionally excited lines and recombination lines of He. The classification was re-evaluated based on diagnostic diagrams (e.g., [N II]/Hα vs. [O III]/Hβ) and the presence of high-excitation lines. Among the 6 Likely PNe, we confirmed their nature and determined that they are mostly compact, low-ionization objects with electron densities in the range 10³–10⁴ cm⁻³. The two new candidates show distinct nebular features; one exhibits Wolf–Rayet central star signatures. The emission-line star was identified as a Be star with no extended nebular emission. The unknown object was reclassified as a compact H II region based on its low excitation and thermal radio continuum. Our results refine the HASH sample and highlight the need for high-resolution imaging to distinguish morphological types in small PNe.

The sample consisted of 6 Likely PNe, 2 new candidates, one emission-line star, and one object of unknown nature.

title: Spurious modes in extended RPA theories
text_ai: Necessary conditions that the spurious state associated with the translational motion and its double-phonon state have zero excitation energy in extended RPA (ERPA) theories which include both one-body and two-body amplitudes are investigated using the small amplitude limit of the time-dependent density-matrix theory (STDDM). It is shown that the translational invariance of the Hamiltonian imposes a set of sum rules on the effective interaction vertices entering the ERPA equations. These sum rules involve both the static and dynamic parts of the two-body density matrix. In STDDM, the spurious 1⁻ state is exactly decoupled at zero energy only when the two-body amplitudes satisfy a specific consistency condition linking the ground-state two-body correlation kernel to the first-order response function. Failure to meet this condition yields a finite spurious energy, thereby breaking Galilean invariance and contaminating low-lying collective modes. For the double-phonon (2⁺) state built atop the 1⁻ mode, a separate condition emerges: the symmetrized two-phonon amplitude must vanish at zero energy if the underlying one-phonon state is itself spurious. This requirement is not automatically fulfilled in standard ERPA truncations and depends sensitively on the treatment of the two-body subspace. Numerical tests in a solvable model demonstrate that the double-phonon spurious energy remains strictly zero only when the two-body amplitudes are determined self-consistently from the STDDM equation for the density matrix, rather than from perturbative approximations. The analysis generalizes to other continuous symmetries, clarifying the minimal theoretical ingredients needed to preserve Goldstone modes and their multiphonon recurrences in extended RPA frameworks.

title: Optimal entanglement witnesses for continuous-variable systems
text_ai: This paper is concerned with all tests for continuous-variable entanglement that arise from linear combinations of second moments or variances of canonical coordinates, as they are commonly used in experiments to detect entanglement. All such tests for bi-partite and multi-partite entanglement correspond to hyperplanes in the set of second moments. We characterize the hyperplanes that correspond to valid witnesses, imposing positivity for all separable states while allowing negativity for entangled ones. Using convex geometry of the set of second moments for separable states, we derive the optimal witness for any given target state as the supporting hyperplane at the point on the separable boundary closest to the target in the Hilbert–Schmidt metric. This yields the strongest possible violation among linear second-moment tests. For Gaussian states, the optimal witness reduces to an eigenvalue condition involving the covariance matrix and its partial transpose, unifying and sharpening the Simon and Duan criteria. We extend these results to multipartite systems, obtaining a hierarchy of optimal witnesses for different bipartitions. The method provides experimentally feasible tests requiring few homodyne measurements, and we illustrate with examples relevant to current squeezed-state and optomechanical experiments. Entanglement detection via optimal witnesses is thus conceptually simplified and practically optimized.
prefix: This paper is concerned with all tests for continuous-variable entanglement that arise from linear combinations of second moments or variances of canonical coordinates, as they are commonly used in experiments to detect entanglement. All such tests for bi-partite and multi-partite entanglement correspond to hyperplanes in the set of second moments.

title: National registry of haemophilia and other coagulopathies: A multisector initiative in the Colombian Health System.
text_ai: Haemophilia is an orphan and high-cost disease worldwide and, especially in middle-income countries as Colombia. Given its burden of disease, in 2014, a national administrative registry was created to centralize demographic, clinical and economic information regarding to haemophilia and other coagulopathies. To describe the building and implementation processes of the Colombian registry of haemophilia and other coagulopathies. A multidisciplinary steering committee was established, comprising representatives from the Ministry of Health, haemophilia treatment centres, patient associations, and academic institutions. A consensus-based minimum dataset was defined, including demographics, diagnosis (type, severity, inhibitor status), treatment regimens (prophylaxis, on-demand, factor concentrates, bypassing agents), bleeding episodes, hospitalisations, and annual direct medical costs. Data extraction draws from administrative claims, clinical records, and a dedicated web-based platform. Implementation followed a phased rollout across 32 departments, with training for healthcare providers and continuous quality audits. By 2023, the registry captured 5,412 persons with haemophilia A, 1,208 with haemophilia B, and 2,034 with von Willebrand disease, among other coagulopathies. Median age was 22 years (IQR: 10–42); 68% had severe haemophilia. Prophylaxis coverage increased from 32% in 2014 to 57% in 2022. Annual bleeding rate decreased significantly (p < 0.001) in patients on prophylaxis. The registry enabled estimation of total annual cost per patient (US$ 21,345), supporting budget impact analyses and price negotiation. Barriers included interoperability with existing health information systems and underreporting in rural areas. The Colombian registry demonstrates a feasible model for middle-income countries, leveraging multisector collaboration to generate real-world evidence. Its structure facilitates monitoring of treatment outcomes, equity in access, and sustainable financing for haemophilia care. Ongoing efforts focus on integrating genetic data and expanding to all coagulopathies.

title: Functions of multivector variables
text_ai: As is well known, the common elementary functions defined over the real numbers can be generalized to act not only over the complex number field but also over the skew (non-commuting) field of the quaternions. In this paper, we detail a number of elementary functions extended to act over the skew field of Clifford multivectors, in both two and three dimensions. Exponential, logarithmic, trigonometric, and hyperbolic functions are defined for multivectors in Cl(2,0) and Cl(3,0). For each we provide power series and closed forms via projection onto the commutative subalgebra generated by the pseudoscalar. In two dimensions they reduce to complex functions; in three dimensions they generalize quaternion functions with additional vector and bivector contributions. The exponential yields trigonometric and hyperbolic functions of the bivector norm; the logarithm is obtained by inversion with careful branch cuts. Domains of analyticity and branch cuts are given, and inverse functions are derived. Algebraic identities and symmetries are verified. Numerical examples and applications in geometric calculus complete the discussion.

In this paper, we detail a number of elementary functions extended to act over the skew field of Clifford multivectors, in both two and three dimensions.

title: Tableau models for semi-infinite Bruhat order and level-zero representations of quantum affine algebras
text_ai: We prove that semi-infinite Bruhat order on an affine Weyl group is completely determined from those on the quotients by affine Weyl subgroups associated with various maximal (standard) parabolic subgroups of finite type. In particular, we reconstruct the semi-infinite Bruhat order via a combinatorial rule involving the degree function on the Weyl group. This yields a new tableau model where elements are encoded by certain marked tableaux that capture the relative positions of alcoves. Furthermore, we demonstrate that this model is compatible with the crystal structure on level-zero representations of quantum affine algebras; the crystal operators correspond to combinatorial moves on the tableaux, and the semi-infinite Bruhat order describes the closure relations in the geometric realization. Our results unify and generalize previous work on type A and provide a uniform treatment for all untwisted affine types. The proof relies on a detailed analysis of reduced expressions and the affine root system, particularly the role of the constant term and the null root.

title: Explaining the Effectiveness of Multi-Task Learning for Efficient Knowledge Extraction from Spine MRI Reports
text_ai: Pretrained Transformer based models finetuned on domain specific corpora have changed the landscape of NLP. However, training or fine-tuning these models for individual tasks can be time consuming and resource intensive. In this work, we explore multi-task learning (MTL) as a strategy to jointly extract multiple clinically relevant entities from spine MRI reports, thereby mitigating the overhead of training separate models. We define a suite of extraction tasks: identification of spinal pathology, grading of stenosis severity, and detection of fracture and alignment abnormalities. We compare a shared-encoder MTL architecture against individually fine-tuned models on a large, annotated corpus of spine MRI reports. Our results demonstrate that MTL achieves higher micro-averaged F1 scores across all tasks while using fewer total parameters and requiring significantly less training time. Critically, we provide a mechanistic explanation for this improvement by analyzing the learned representations: the shared encoder captures common syntactic and semantic patterns across tasks—such as anatomical location phrases and severity modifiers—which facilitates knowledge transfer and reduces overfitting to task-specific noise. Furthermore, we show that MTL exhibits stronger performance on low-resource tasks, where individual models suffer from data sparsity. These findings underscore that MTL is not only an efficiency-driven approach but also a means to enhance extraction accuracy in the specialized domain of spine radiology. Our work offers practical guidance for deploying lightweight, high-performing NLP systems in clinical environments where computational resources are constrained.
prefix: Pretrained Transformer based models finetuned on domain specific corpora have changed the landscape of NLP. However, training or fine-tuning these models for individual tasks can be time consuming and resource intensive.

title: Off the record: The invisibility work of doctors in a patient-accessible electronic health record information service.
text_ai: In this article, we draw on Michael Lipsky's work on street-level bureaucrats and discretion to analyse a real case setting comprising an interview study of 30 Swedish doctors regarding their experiences of changes in clinical work following patients being given access to medical records information online. We show that doctors engage in what we term *invisibility work* — systematic but often unacknowledged efforts to maintain professional autonomy and control over clinical documentation in the face of patient-accessible records. Drawing on Lipsky's framework, we identify three key discretion strategies: delayed documentation, linguistic hedging, and selective omission of sensitive information. These practices, while aimed at preserving the therapeutic relationship and avoiding premature patient distress, also serve to protect doctors from perceived legal and reputational risks. However, this invisibility work paradoxically undermines the transparency that patient access is intended to achieve. Our analysis reveals a tension between policy ideals of patient empowerment and the practical realities of clinical work, where doctors' discretionary choices reshape the very information patients encounter. We argue that such invisibility work is not merely a defensive reaction but a form of street-level bureaucratic adaptation to new digital infrastructures. The study contributes to literature on digital health and professional discretion by highlighting how seemingly neutral technologies become sites of negotiation over professional boundaries, accountability, and the nature of medical records.
prefix: In this article, we draw on Michael Lipsky's work on street-level bureaucrats and discretion to analyse a real case setting comprising an interview study of 30 Swedish doctors regarding their experiences of changes in clinical work following patients being given access to medical records information online.

title: Lattice results for $D/D_s$ leptonic and semileptonic decays
text_ai: This review article summarizes recent lattice QCD results for $D$ and $D_s$ meson leptonic and semileptonic decays. Knowing the meson decay constants and semileptonic form factors from theory, one can extract CKM elements $V_{cd}$ and $V_{cs}$ from experimental results. We review the latest lattice calculations, highlighting how improvements in action design and algorithmic advances have yielded decay constants with sub-percent precision. These values enable precise extractions of $V_{cd}$ and $V_{cs}$ via leptonic decays. For semileptonic modes, form factors for $D\to K$ and $D\to \pi$ are computed with controlled chiral and continuum extrapolations, reducing uncertainties in the extracted CKM elements. Comparisons with exclusive semileptonic decays show consistency, though tensions in inclusive determinations necessitate further study. The lattice results are in good agreement with Standard Model expectations, providing constraints on new physics. Future progress will come from simulations at physical quark masses and inclusion of isospin breaking effects. Additionally, ongoing efforts aim to incorporate electromagnetic corrections and to compute form factors for rare decays, further sharpening tests of the Standard Model.
prefix: This review article summarizes recent lattice QCD results for $D$ and $D_s$ meson leptonic and semileptonic decays. Knowing the meson decay constants and semileptonic form factors from theory, one can extract CKM elements $V_{cd}$ and $V_{cs}$ from experimental results.

title: Mobile Data Science: Towards Understanding Data-Driven Intelligent Mobile Applications
text_ai: Due to the popularity of smart mobile phones and context-aware technology, various contextual data relevant to users' diverse activities with mobile phones is available around us. This enables the study on mobile phone data and context-awareness in computing, for the purpose of building data-driven intelligent mobile applications, not only on a single device but also in a distributed environment for the benefit of end users. However, this data abundance introduces challenges in heterogeneity, volume, velocity, veracity, and privacy, requiring novel mobile data science methodologies. This paper systematically investigates the lifecycle of data-driven intelligent mobile applications, from sensing to deployment. We propose a framework categorizing key components: context acquisition and preprocessing, feature extraction and selection, model training and adaptation, and on-device inference. We survey advanced techniques for sparse, noisy, high-dimensional mobile data, including deep, transfer, and federated learning. We examine real-world applications in health monitoring, smart transportation, and personalized assistants. Our analyses reveal trade-offs between accuracy, latency, energy, privacy, and contextual integrity. We also present case studies demonstrating optimization for energy efficiency and real-time performance. Our work contributes a taxonomy of data-driven approaches. We outline emerging research directions such as cross-modal learning and lifelong personalization. The paper emphasizes the need for standardized benchmarks and reproducible pipelines to advance the field. Ultimately, this work lays a foundation for understanding data-driven intelligence in mobile environments.
prefix: Due to the popularity of smart mobile phones and context-aware technology, various contextual data relevant to users' diverse activities with mobile phones is available around us. This enables the study on mobile phone data and context-awareness in computing, for the purpose of building data-driven intelligent mobile applications, not only on a single device but also in a distributed environment for the benefit of end users.

title: SSH: A Self-Supervised Framework for Image Harmonization
text_ai: Image harmonization aims to improve the quality of image compositing by matching the "appearance" (\eg, color tone, brightness and contrast) between foreground and background images. However, collecting large-scale annotated datasets for this task requires complex professional retouching. Instead, we propose a novel Self-Supervised Harmonization framework (SSH) that can be trained using just "free" natural images without being edited. SSH leverages a simple yet effective pretext task: we automatically generate synthetic composite images with appearance inconsistencies by applying different photometric transformations to foreground and background regions extracted from single natural images. A Transformer-based harmonization network then learns to predict the correction parameters that resolve these inconsistencies. During inference, the model directly harmonizes real composite images. Extensive experiments on iHarmony4 and other benchmarks demonstrate that SSH achieves competitive or superior performance compared to fully-supervised methods, despite using no manually retouched data. Moreover, we show that the self-supervised pretrained model can be fine-tuned with limited labeled examples to further improve performance, and ablation studies confirm the effectiveness of each component.
prefix: Image harmonization aims to improve the quality of image compositing by matching the "appearance" (\eg, color tone, brightness and contrast) between foreground and background images. However, collecting large-scale annotated datasets for this task requires complex professional retouching. Instead, we propose a novel Self-Supervised Harmonization framework (SSH) that can be trained using just "free" natural images without being edited.

title: Contextual Hybrid Session-based News Recommendation with Recurrent Neural Networks
text_ai: Recommender systems help users deal with information overload by providing tailored item suggestions to them. The recommendation of news is often considered to be challenging, since the relevance of an article for a user can depend on a variety of factors, including the user's short-term reading interests, the reader's context, or the recency or popularity of an article. In this paper, we propose a contextual hybrid session-based news recommendation model that leverages recurrent neural networks (RNNs) to capture sequential patterns in user browsing sessions while integrating contextual signals such as time, location, and device type. Our approach combines a session-level RNN encoder with a content-based representation of news articles, enabling the model to dynamically adapt recommendations based on both the evolving interests within a session and the static features of available items. To evaluate the effectiveness of our method, we conduct extensive experiments on two real-world news datasets, comparing against a range of baselines including pure session-based models, context-aware approaches, and hybrid architectures. Results demonstrate that our contextual hybrid RNN significantly outperforms all baselines in terms of recall and mean reciprocal rank, particularly in cold-start scenarios where user history is sparse. Furthermore, we analyze the contribution of each contextual feature and show that temporal and device signals yield the largest performance gains. The findings highlight the importance of jointly modeling session dynamics and contextual information for news recommendation, offering practical insights for deploying such systems in real-world applications. Our work underscores the potential of RNN-based hybrid models to address the unique challenges of news domains, where user intent is transient and heavily influenced by external context.
prefix: Recommender systems help users deal with information overload by providing tailored item suggestions to them. The recommendation of news is often considered to be challenging, since the relevance of an article for a user can depend on a variety of factors, including the user's short-term reading interests, the reader's context, or the recency or popularity of an article.

title: Numerical models of planetary nebulae with different episodes of mass ejection: the particular case of HuBi 1
text_ai: We have studied the evolution of HuBi 1-like planetary nebulae, considering several stages of mass injection. We have carried out numerical ionization+1D hydrodynamics+atomic/ionic rate models with our code Coral 1D to reproduce planetary nebulae that present multiple shells produced by different ejection events around the ionizing source. Our models successfully reproduce the multiple-shell structure observed in HuBi 1, revealing that distinct ejection episodes—occurring at intervals of a few thousand years—produce ionized shells with different expansion velocities and densities. By incorporating time-dependent photoionization and evolving the stellar radiation field, we find that the innermost shell is currently being photoionized by the central star, while outer shells remain partially neutral or are recombining. The synthetic emission-line maps and position–velocity diagrams match the Hα, [N II], and [O III] observations, particularly the knotty inner ring and faint outer halo. The results indicate that HuBi 1 underwent at least two major mass-loss events, the later one with higher velocity and lower density, consistent with a late thermal pulse scenario. We conclude that multiple-episode mass injection is essential for explaining the complex kinematics and ionization structure of this object, and that Coral 1D provides a robust framework for modeling such multi-shell planetary nebulae.

We have carried out numerical ionization+1D hydrodynamics+atomic/ionic rate models with our code Coral 1D to reproduce planetary nebulae that present multiple shells produced by different ejection events around the ionizing source.

title: Preparation of biogenic gas vesicle nanostructures for use as contrast agents for ultrasound and MRI.
text_ai: Gas vesicles (GVs) are a unique class of gas-filled protein nanostructures that are detectable at subnanomolar concentrations and whose physical properties allow them to serve as highly sensitive imaging agents for ultrasound and MRI. Here, we describe a scalable biogenic preparation method for isolating GVs from the cyanobacterium *Anabaena flos-aquae* and engineering them to function as dual-modality contrast agents. By optimizing hypoosmotic lysis and differential centrifugation, we obtained pure GV suspensions with yields exceeding 10¹² particles per liter of culture. The resulting nanostructures, approximately 200 nm in length and 80 nm in diameter, exhibit a characteristic hollow, cylindrical morphology with a protein shell that collapses under moderate hydrostatic pressure—a property exploited for ultrasound contrast. To enhance MRI contrast, we genetically fused the GV shell protein GvpC with a lysine-rich tag that binds manganese ions, enabling T₁-weighted imaging. Dynamic light scattering and transmission electron microscopy confirmed structural integrity after modification, while spectrophotometry quantified the manganese loading at up to 5,000 ions per GV. In vitro phantom imaging demonstrated that these GVs produce strong, persistent echogenicity under clinical ultrasound frequencies and generate a significant T₁ relaxivity of 1.8 mM⁻¹ s⁻¹ at 3 T. Notably, the construct remains stable in serum for over 24 hours and shows no cytotoxicity in mammalian cell assays. This preparation method yields functionalized GVs that combine the sensitivity of bubble-based ultrasound agents with the spatial resolution of MRI, offering a promising platform for noninvasive molecular imaging. The approach is modular, enabling future incorporation of targeting ligands for disease-specific imaging applications.
prefix: Gas vesicles (GVs) are a unique class of gas-filled protein nanostructures that are detectable at subnanomolar concentrations and whose physical properties allow them to serve as highly sensitive imaging agents for ultrasound and MRI.

title: Simultaneous thermoosmotic and thermoelectric responses in nanoconfined electrolyte solutions: Effects of nanopore structures and membrane properties
text_ai: Hypothesis: Nanofluidic systems provide an emerging and efficient platform for thermoelectric conversion and fluid pumping with low-grade heat energy. As a basis of their performance enhancement, the effects of the structures and properties of the nanofluidic systems on the thermoelectric response (TER) and the thermoosmotic response (TOR) are yet to be explored. Here, we perform molecular dynamics simulations and continuum modeling to systematically investigate how nanopore geometry (e.g., diameter, length, and shape) and membrane surface properties (e.g., charge density, dielectric constant, and wettability) govern the coupled TER and TOR in electrolyte solutions. We find that the sign and magnitude of both responses depend sensitively on the interplay between ion selectivity and thermophoretic effects within the nanoconfinement. In particular, narrow pores with high surface charge enhance the Seebeck coefficient (thermoelectric coupling), while simultaneously reducing the thermoosmotic slip, leading to a trade-off between electrical power and pumping efficiency. Conversely, hydrophilicity and low dielectric contrast amplify the thermoosmotic flow but dilute the ionic thermoelectric voltage. By mapping the response matrix across a wide parameter space, we identify optimal regimes where TER and TOR can be simultaneously maximized—for instance, in moderately charged, short nanopores with matched dielectric properties. Our findings provide a rational design principle for nanofluidic devices that harvest waste heat for either direct electricity generation or on-chip fluid manipulation, and they highlight the need for tailored nanopore architectures to decouple the otherwise antagonistic thermal–electrokinetic responses.
