As a basis of their performance enhancement, the effects of the structures and properties of the nanofluidic systems on the thermoelectric response (TER) and the thermoosmotic response (TOR) are yet to be explored.

title: Antimicrobial resistance and use, and rates of hospitalization associated with bacterial infections, including sepsis
text_ai: While the mechanisms and quantitative details are complex, few analysts would doubt that antibiotic use increases the prevalence of drug-resistant bacterial pathogens among all bacteria causing disease in a population. The causal connection between antibiotic use and the total incidence of severe bacterial infections, possibly mediated by antibiotic resistance, is less clearly established. Here, we examine this relationship using national surveillance data on antibiotic consumption, antimicrobial resistance prevalence, and hospital discharge records for bacterial infections and sepsis over a ten-year period. We employ a distributed-lag time-series model to estimate the effect of population-level antibiotic use on subsequent hospitalization rates, while controlling for seasonal and secular trends. Our results indicate that increases in antibiotic consumption are associated with elevated hospitalization rates for resistant infections and sepsis, even after accounting for resistance prevalence. This suggests that antibiotic use may directly impair patient outcomes—for instance, by disrupting the microbiome—independently of its role in selecting for resistant organisms. These findings highlight the need for antibiotic stewardship programs to consider not only resistance mitigation but also the potential for reducing severe infection incidence through judicious prescribing.

The causal connection between antibiotic use and the total incidence of severe bacterial infections, possibly mediated by antibiotic resistance, is less clearly established.

title: MBAPose: Mask and Bounding-Box Aware Pose Estimation of Surgical Instruments with Photorealistic Domain Randomization
text_ai: Surgical robots are usually controlled using a priori models based on the robots' geometric parameters, which are calibrated before the surgical procedure. One of the challenges in using robots in real surgical settings is that those parameters can change over time, consequently deteriorating control accuracy. To address this, we propose MBAPose, a novel framework for estimating the 6-DOF pose of surgical instruments without requiring explicit geometric models or re-calibration. MBAPose leverages both instance segmentation masks and axis-aligned bounding boxes to focus the pose estimation network on instrument-specific features, thereby improving robustness to occlusions and background clutter. To overcome the scarcity of labeled real surgical data, we employ photorealistic domain randomization, generating highly diverse synthetic images that mimic real operating conditions, including varying lighting, textures, and camera perspectives. This training strategy enables the model to generalize effectively to unseen real environments. Extensive experiments on both simulated and real surgical datasets demonstrate that MBAPose achieves mean translation errors below 2 mm and rotation errors under 3°, significantly outperforming prior methods that rely on calibrated models. Furthermore, our approach maintains consistent accuracy even when geometric parameters drift during prolonged procedures, offering a practical solution for long-duration robot-assisted surgery. The code and trained models are made publicly available.
prefix: Surgical robots are usually controlled using a priori models based on the robots' geometric parameters, which are calibrated before the surgical procedure. One of the challenges in using robots in real surgical settings is that those parameters can change over time, consequently deteriorating control accuracy.

title: A Deep Conditioning Treatment of Neural Networks
text_ai: We study the role of depth in training randomly initialized overparameterized neural networks. We give a general result showing that depth improves trainability of neural networks by improving the conditioning of certain kernel matrices of the input data. This result holds for arbitrary non-linear activation functions under a certain normalization. Specifically, we analyze the neural tangent kernel (NTK) and the empirical Gram matrix of the last-layer features, showing that their minimum eigenvalues increase with depth for a fixed dataset and parameter budget. This improved conditioning accelerates gradient descent convergence and enables faster learning of high-frequency components in the target function. We quantify this effect by deriving explicit bounds on the condition number as a function of depth, width, and the activation's curvature. The normalization required is a careful scaling of the pre-activation variances, ensuring that the forward dynamics remain stable across layers. Our results establish a rigorous theoretical foundation for the common intuition that deeper networks are easier to train, independent of any capacity or expressivity gains. Numerical experiments on synthetic and image datasets confirm the theory, demonstrating monotonically improved condition numbers and faster training times as depth increases, even when controlling for total number of parameters.

We give a general result showing that depth improves trainability of neural networks by improving the conditioning of certain kernel matrices of the input data. This result holds for arbitrary non-linear activation functions under a certain normalization.

title: Why Are You Wrong? Counterfactual Explanations for Language Grounding with 3D Objects
text_ai: Combining natural language and geometric shapes is an emerging research area with multiple applications in robotics and language-assisted design. A crucial task in this domain is object referent identification, which involves selecting a 3D object given a textual description of the target. However, existing systems often misidentify objects, especially with ambiguous descriptions or similar candidates. To explain such errors, we propose counterfactual explanations that answer the question: Why did the model choose the wrong object? Our method generates minimal alterations to the input description or object configuration that would flip the prediction to the correct referent. We define a search over candidate modifications—including changes to geometric attributes, spatial relations, or lexical choices—and select those that yield a high‑confidence correct prediction with minimal change. We evaluate on the ReferIt3D dataset, collecting human judgments on plausibility and informativeness. Our counterfactuals highlight model biases like over‑reliance on color or position cues, and are preferred over baselines by annotators who find them more helpful for understanding model decisions. Moreover, using them for targeted data augmentation improves grounding accuracy by up to 5% absolute. Our contributions include a novel task formulation, an efficient search algorithm, empirical evidence of utility for model improvement, and a new benchmark of human‑judged counterfactuals. This work paves the way for transparent human‑robot interaction and interpretable language grounding in physical environments.
prefix: Combining natural language and geometric shapes is an emerging research area with multiple applications in robotics and language-assisted design. A crucial task in this domain is object referent identification, which involves selecting a 3D object given a textual description of the target.

title: Gene-centric gene-gene interaction: A model-based kernel machine method
text_ai: Much of the natural variation for a complex trait can be explained by variation in DNA sequence levels. As part of sequence variation, gene-gene interaction has been ubiquitously observed in nature, where its role in shaping the development of an organism has been broadly recognized. Despite the recognized importance of gene-gene interaction, its detection in genome-wide association studies remains challenging due to statistical and computational burdens. Existing methods often test interactions at the single-marker level, which suffers from low power after multiple-testing correction and fails to capture the joint effect of multiple variants within a gene. To address these limitations, we propose a gene-centric, model-based kernel machine method for testing gene-gene interaction. Our approach first constructs a similarity kernel for each gene using all genetic variants within that gene, thus aggregating information across variants in a biologically meaningful unit. Interaction between two genes is then modeled by including the element-wise product of their respective kernel matrices as an additional variance component in a linear mixed model. This formulation allows for flexible modeling of non-linear and non-additive effects while maintaining computational efficiency through a score test. Importantly, the method naturally conditions on the main effects of both genes, thus avoiding confounding between marginal and interaction signals. We evaluate the proposed method through extensive simulations, demonstrating well-calibrated type I error and substantial power gains over single-marker interaction tests under various epistatic models. Application to a human body mass index study further illustrates the method’s ability to detect novel gene-gene interactions that are replicable across independent cohorts. The gene-centric kernel machine framework provides a powerful and scalable tool for epistasis mapping in complex traits.
prefix: Much of the natural variation for a complex trait can be explained by variation in DNA sequence levels. As part of sequence variation, gene-gene interaction has been ubiquitously observed in nature, where its role in shaping the development of an organism has been broadly recognized.

title: Visual Perception Generalization for Vision-and-Language Navigation via Meta-Learning
text_ai: Vision-and-language navigation (VLN) is a challenging task that requires an agent to navigate in real-world environments by understanding natural language instructions and visual information received in real-time. Prior works have implemented VLN tasks on continuous environments or physical robots, all of which use a fixed camera configuration due to the limitations of datasets, such as 1.5 meters height, 90 degrees horizontal field of view (HFOV), etc. Such rigid visual constraints limit the agent's ability to generalize across varying camera parameters encountered in real-world deployment. To address this, we propose a meta-learning framework that enables the agent to rapidly adapt its visual perception to new camera configurations with minimal fine-tuning. Our approach trains an initial model on a diverse set of simulated camera settings, then leverages meta-gradient updates to learn a robust initialization that captures invariant visual features across different heights, fields of view, and orientations. During navigation, the agent can quickly adapt to the target camera setting using a small number of gradient steps, thereby overcoming the domain gap between training and deployment. We evaluate our method on the VLN-CE benchmark under multiple camera configurations not seen during training. Experimental results show that our meta-learned agent significantly outperforms prior state-of-the-art models in cross-configuration generalization, while maintaining competitive performance on standard fixed-configuration evaluations. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the learned visual representations are transferable to novel environments and instructions, underscoring the effectiveness of meta-learning for visual perception generalization in VLN. This work highlights the importance of addressing visual heterogeneity and provides a scalable solution for deploying VLN agents under realistic, varied camera setups.

Prior works have implemented VLN tasks on continuous environments or physical robots, all of which use a fixed camera configuration due to the limitations of datasets, such as 1.5 meters height, 90 degrees horizontal field of view (HFOV), etc.

title: Nanotechnology approaches in the current therapy of skin cancer.
text_ai: Skin cancer is a high burden disease with a high impact on global health. Conventional therapies have several drawbacks; thus, the development of effective therapies is required. In this context, nanotechnology approaches are an attractive strategy for cancer therapy because they enable the efficient delivery of drugs and other bioactive molecules to target tissues with low toxic effects. This review highlights recent advances in nanoparticle-based systems, including liposomes, polymeric nanoparticles, and metallic nanostructures, which enhance drug stability, solubility, and selective accumulation in cutaneous tumors via passive and active targeting mechanisms. Topical formulations with nanocarriers improve skin penetration and retention, reducing systemic toxicity while enabling photothermal and photodynamic therapies for non-melanoma and melanoma lesions. Furthermore, stimuli-responsive nanoplatforms offer on-demand drug release at the tumor site. Despite challenges such as scalability and clinical translation, nanotechnology remains a transformative approach for improving therapeutic efficacy and patient outcomes in skin cancer management.

In this context, nanotechnology approaches are an attractive strategy for cancer therapy because they enable the efficient delivery of drugs and other bioactive molecules to target tissues with low toxic effects.

title: Diverse tunable dynamics of two quantum random walkers
text_ai: Quantum walk research has mainly focused on evolutions due to repeated applications of time-independent unitary coin operators. However, the idea of controlling the single particle evolution using time-dependent unitary coins has still been a subject of multiple studies as it not only hosts interesting possibilities for quantum information processing but also opens a much richer array of phenomena including static and dynamic localizations. The present work extends this investigation to two interacting quantum walkers, where time-dependent unitary coins enable a rich array of dynamical behaviors. By modulating coin parameters periodically or aperiodically, we demonstrate tunable regimes from ballistic transport to complete dynamical localization, as well as correlated phases like pair localization and separation. The evolution of entanglement is shown to be highly sensitive to the coin's temporal structure, offering a versatile control mechanism for quantum correlations. We derive exact expressions for certain protocols, and numerical simulations provide a comprehensive phase diagram. Our simulations also show that initial states affect dynamics, with coherence tuned by modulation. Additionally, time-dependent coins induce transitions absent in single-walker cases, such as the sudden formation of bound states. These results highlight the utility for achieving diverse dynamics in multispecies settings, with potential applications in quantum simulations and information processing. The tunability opens up new possibilities for designing circuits that leverage two-walker correlations.

However, the idea of controlling the single particle evolution using time-dependent unitary coins has still been a subject of multiple studies as it not only hosts interesting possibilities for quantum information processing but also opens a much richer array of phenomena including static and dynamic localizations.

title: Cognitive system to achieve human-level accuracy in automated assignment of helpdesk email tickets
text_ai: Ticket assignment/dispatch is a crucial part of service delivery business with lot of scope for automation and optimization. In this paper, we present an end-to-end automated helpdesk email ticket assignment system, which is also offered as a service. building on a hybrid cognitive architecture that combines deep learning with rule-based reasoning to interpret ticket content, infer urgency, and route to the most qualified resolver. The system employs a multi-layer attention mechanism to extract context from email threads, handles multi-intent tickets via dynamic goal decomposition, and leverages a knowledge graph of historical resolutions to disambiguate ambiguous requests. To achieve human-level accuracy, we integrate a feedback loop where human supervisors correct misassignments, and the model incrementally updates its embedding space through online learning, reducing drift over time. We evaluate the system on a corpus of 1.2 million real-world helpdesk tickets from a multinational IT service provider, comparing against both rule-based baselines and state-of-the-art text classifiers. Results show a 94.7% first-attempt accuracy (vs. 86.2% for the best baseline), with a 38% reduction in escalation rates and an average assignment latency under 1.2 seconds. Moreover, in a blind A/B test with 15 experienced dispatchers, the system matched or exceeded human performance in 91% of the cases, while processing 300× more tickets per hour. The service architecture is containerized and deployed on Kubernetes, supporting elastic scaling across enterprises with varying data governance requirements. We conclude that a cognitively-inspired, continually learning system can automate ticket assignment at scale without sacrificing precision, thereby freeing human experts for complex, value-adding tasks. This work demonstrates a practical pathway toward human-level automation in knowledge-intensive service operations.
prefix: Ticket assignment/dispatch is a crucial part of service delivery business with lot of scope for automation and optimization. In this paper, we present an end-to-end automated helpdesk email ticket assignment system, which is also offered as a service.

title: Convergence of drift-diffusion PDEs arising as Wasserstein gradient flows of convex functions
text_ai: We study the quantitative convergence of drift-diffusion PDEs that arise as Wasserstein gradient flows of linearly convex functions over the space of probability measures on ${\mathbb R}^d$. In this setting, the objective is in general not displacement convex, so it is not clear a priori whether global convergence even holds. We show that global convergence toward the unique equilibrium is indeed guaranteed, and we quantify the rate in terms of the convexity properties of the functional. The key observation is that linear convexity along generalized geodesics in the Wasserstein space—a condition weaker than displacement convexity—suffices to establish a new entropy–dissipation inequality. This inequality, reminiscent of a modified logarithmic Sobolev inequality, implies exponential decay of the relative entropy along the flow, and consequently exponential convergence in the Wasserstein-2 metric. The rate is determined by the convexity constant of the functional along these generalized geodesics. Our result covers a wide range of drift-diffusion PDEs, including Fokker–Planck equations, porous medium equations, and aggregation–diffusion models with repulsive interaction potentials. For each example we verify the required convexity condition and compute the explicit convergence rate. Moreover, in the degenerate case where the functional is only semiconvex, we derive algebraic (polynomial) rates of convergence. The analysis relies on a careful study of the second variation of the functional along displacement interpolations, combined with a refined estimate of the dissipation of the relative entropy. This approach circumvents the lack of displacement convexity and provides a unified framework for quantitative convergence of Wasserstein gradient flows of convex functions.

title: Generic algebraic properties in spaces of enumerated groups
text_ai: We introduce and study Polish topologies on various spaces of countable enumerated groups, where an enumerated group is simply a group whose underlying set is the set of natural numbers. Using elementary tools and well known examples from combinatorial group theory, combined with the Baire category theorem, we obtain a plethora of results demonstrating that several phenomena in group theory are generic. Specifically, we prove that for many natural Polish spaces of enumerated groups, properties such as being torsion-free, having trivial center, and being residually finite are Baire generically true. We also show that the existence of a solvable word problem is a generic property in the space of recursively presented groups. These results, grounded in elementary combinatorial group theory and the Baire category theorem, unify and extend known observations about the prevalence of certain group-theoretic phenomena. Our approach thus provides a topological lens through which generic algebra can be systematically studied, offering new insights into the structure of the space of all countable groups.

Using elementary tools and well known examples from combinatorial group theory, combined with the Baire category theorem, we obtain a plethora of results demonstrating that several phenomena in group theory are generic.

title: The conundrum of stock versus bond prices
text_ai: In a general way, stock and bond prices do not display any significant correlation. Yet, if we concentrate our attention on specific episodes marked by a crash followed by a rebound, then we observe that stock prices have a strong connection with interest rates on the one hand, and with bond yield spreads on the other hand. This asymmetric pattern suggests that the relationship between equity and fixed-income markets is regime-dependent, governed by shifts in investor sentiment and macroeconomic uncertainty. During crash–rebound episodes, the common driver appears to be a flight-to-quality mechanism: as equity prices plummet, investors simultaneously demand safer assets, compressing risk-free yields while widening credit spreads. Conversely, when a rebound takes hold, the unwinding of risk aversion reverses these movements, tightening spreads and raising interest rates in tandem with rising stock prices. The conundrum lies in reconciling this episodic synchronization with the long-run decoupling observed in tranquil periods. One plausible explanation is that the pricing kernel—the stochastic discount factor—becomes more volatile and more negatively correlated with consumption growth during crises, thereby amplifying the co-movement of discount rates applied to both asset classes. This interpretation implies that standard linear factor models, which assume a stable correlation structure, may miss the latent time variation in risk premia that only manifests during tail events. Future research should explore whether the strength of this episodic link is itself predictable, perhaps by monitoring valuation ratios or volatility indices that flag impending regime shifts.

Yet, if we concentrate our attention on specific episodes marked by a crash followed by a rebound, then we observe that stock prices have a strong connection with interest rates on the one hand, and with bond yield spreads on the other hand.

title: Napoleonic Constructions in the Hyperbolic Plane
text_ai: In the Euclidean setting, Napoleon's Theorem states that if one constructs an equilateral triangle on either the outside or the inside of each side of a given triangle and then connects the barycenters of those three new triangles, the resulting triangle happens to be equilateral. We investigate the extent to which this celebrated result generalizes to the hyperbolic plane, adopting both the Poincaré disk and the upper half‑plane models. Equilateral triangles in hyperbolic geometry are defined by equal side lengths rather than equal angles, and their barycenters are taken as the intersection points of the medians. We show that for an arbitrary hyperbolic triangle, the triangle formed by connecting the barycenters of the three outward (or inward) equilateral triangles constructed on its sides is always equilateral only when the original triangle is itself equilateral. In the general case, the resulting triangle is not equilateral, but we derive explicit formulas for its side lengths and angle defects in terms of the side lengths and area of the original triangle. We also identify a special family of triangles—those with a particular relation among their sides—for which the “Napoleon triangle” remains equilateral. These results highlight the sharp contrast between Euclidean and hyperbolic geometries for this classical construction and offer new insights into the role of curvature in plane geometry.
prefix: In the Euclidean setting, Napoleon's Theorem states that if one constructs an equilateral triangle on either the outside or the inside of each side of a given triangle and then connects the barycenters of those three new triangles, the resulting triangle happens to be equilateral.

title: Derivation and maintenance of mouse haploid embryonic stem cells.
text_ai: Ploidy represents the number of chromosome sets in a cell. Although gametes have a haploid genome (n), most mammalian cells have diploid genomes (2n). The diploid status of most cells correlates with the number of probable alleles for each autosomal gene and makes it difficult to target these genes via mutagenesis techniques. The establishment of haploid embryonic stem cells (haESCs) in mice overcomes this limitation, providing a powerful platform for forward and reverse genetic screens. Here, we describe a robust method for deriving haESCs from parthenogenetic embryos, alongside optimized culture conditions that sustain haploidy through inhibition of endoreduplication. Using FACS-based enrichment for DNA content, we achieve stable haESC lines that maintain a normal karyotype, express pluripotency markers, and contribute to chimeras upon injection into blastocysts. We further demonstrate that these cells can be differentiated into multiple lineages while retaining haploidy, facilitating loss-of-function studies without the need for heterozygosity or RNA interference. Our protocols address critical parameters—including medium composition, passaging density, and cell cycle synchronization—that maximize haploid cell frequency. These findings establish haESCs as a versatile tool for genetic interrogation in mammals.

The diploid status of most cells correlates with the number of probable alleles for each autosomal gene and makes it difficult to target these genes via mutagenesis techniques.

title: Evolution of an N-level system via automated vectorization of the Liouville equations and application to optically controlled polarization rotation
text_ai: The Liouville equation governing the evolution of the density matrix for an atomic/molecular system is expressed in terms of a commutator between the density matrix and the Hamiltonian, along with terms that account for decay and redistribution. We develop an automated vectorization method that maps the density matrix elements into a vector of length N^2, converting the commutator and relaxation terms into a linear system of ordinary differential equations. The method accommodates arbitrary Hamiltonians and decay processes, handling both closed and open systems. It is implemented in a flexible computational framework that generates the system of equations symbolically or numerically. As an application, we study optically controlled polarization rotation in an N-level atomic system. We show that the vectorized Liouville equations capture the evolution of the Stokes parameters and predict a rotation of the polarization axis that depends on the control field intensity and detuning. The results demonstrate the utility of the automated approach for modeling complex multilevel dynamics in quantum optics and atomic physics.

title: Spectral Efficiency Maximization for DMA-enabled Multiuser MISO with Statistical CSI
text_ai: Dynamic metasurface antennas (DMAs) offer the potential to achieve large-scale antenna arrays with low power consumption and reduced hardware costs, making them a promising technology for future communication systems. This paper investigates the spectral efficiency (SE) of DMA-enabled multiuser multiple-input single-output (MISO) systems in both uplink and downlink transmissions, using only statistical channel state information (CSI) to maximize the ergodic sum rate of multiple users. We formulate a weighted sum rate maximization problem that jointly optimizes the DMA’s adjustable weights and the base station’s digital precoder (downlink) or combiner (uplink). The problem is non-convex due to the unit-modulus constraints of the DMA elements and the coupling between analog and digital stages. Using the majorization-minimization (MM) framework and a concave lower bound on the ergodic rate expression, we develop an iterative algorithm that converges to a stationary point. The algorithm exploits the closed-form expressions for the statistical CSI-based rate, which depend only on the channel’s second-order moments. For the downlink, we further propose a low-complexity design that decouples the analog and digital optimization by first maximizing the average signal-to-leakage-plus-noise ratio (SLNR) for the DMA weights and then applying regularized zero-forcing for the digital precoder. Simulation results show that the proposed schemes achieve up to 95% of the ergodic sum rate obtained with full instantaneous CSI, while requiring significantly less feedback overhead. Compared to conventional fully digital arrays with the same number of radio-frequency chains, the DMA architecture yields comparable SE at a fraction of the hardware cost. The findings demonstrate that statistical CSI is sufficient for practical DMA-enabled MISO systems, offering a robust solution for low-complexity, energy-efficient massive MIMO deployments.

This paper investigates the spectral efficiency (SE) of DMA-enabled multiuser multiple-input single-output (MISO) systems in both uplink and downlink transmissions, using only statistical channel state information (CSI) to maximize the ergodic sum rate of multiple users.

title: Are Bitcoins price predictable? Evidence from machine learning techniques using technical indicators
text_ai: The uncertainties in future Bitcoin price make it difficult to accurately predict the price of Bitcoin. Accurately predicting the price for Bitcoin is therefore important for decision-making process of investors and market players in the cryptocurrency market. This study aims to evaluate the predictability of Bitcoin prices by employing a range of machine learning models—including Random Forest, Support Vector Regression, Long Short-Term Memory networks, and Gradient Boosting—trained on a comprehensive set of technical indicators. The dataset spans daily price observations from 2014 to 2023, and the indicators cover momentum, volatility, volume, and trend-following categories such as Relative Strength Index, Moving Average Convergence Divergence, Bollinger Bands, and on-balance volume. Model performance is assessed using mean absolute error, root mean squared error, and directional accuracy, with a walk-forward validation approach to simulate real-time trading decisions. The results reveal that ensemble methods consistently outperform simple benchmarks, achieving directional accuracy rates above 60% in out-of-sample tests, though prediction error remains substantial during periods of extreme volatility. Notably, the inclusion of lagged price returns and volatility measures significantly enhances predictive power, while volume-based indicators contribute marginally. The findings suggest that while Bitcoin price exhibits some degree of short-term predictability driven by technical patterns, the inherent noise and non-stationarity of the market prevent reliable long-term forecasts. These insights have practical implications for algorithmic trading strategies and risk management, highlighting the potential of machine learning to extract predictive signals from technical indicators despite the asset’s notorious unpredictability. Future work could incorporate sentiment data and blockchain fundamentals to further improve forecast accuracy.

title: How Dense is Your Gas? On the recoverability of LVG model parameters
text_ai: We explore the recoverability of gas physical conditions with the Large Velocity Gradient (LVG) model, using the public code RADEX and the molecules HCN and CO. Examining a wide parameter range with a series of models of increasing complexity we use both grid and Monte Carlo Markov Chain (MCMC) methods to recover the input conditions, and quantify the inherent and noise induced uncertainties in the model results. Our analysis reveals that the recoverability of density and temperature is strongly degenerate, particularly for HCN, where likelihood surfaces exhibit multiple minima. Inherent uncertainties dominate at high signal-to-noise, driven by the choice of collisional rate coefficients and the limited number of observable transitions. Noise-induced uncertainties become comparable for low signal-to-noise ratios, especially for subordinate HCN lines. For CO, the larger number of optically thin transitions provides tighter constraints on the kinetic temperature but still leaves the column density poorly constrained. The MCMC posteriors are frequently multimodal, with distinct solutions corresponding to different excitation regimes. We quantify the minimum achievable uncertainties under ideal conditions and demonstrate that grid-based and MCMC methods yield consistent results when the parameter space is adequately sampled. However, the MCMC approach more efficiently reveals degeneracies and allows robust uncertainty propagation. Our results highlight that LVG modeling without prior information on the source’s physical scale or velocity gradient can lead to highly uncertain or misleading parameter estimates. We provide practical guidelines for observers, including recommended line combinations and signal-to-noise thresholds, to improve the reliability of recovered gas conditions.

title: Automated Bridge Component Recognition using Video Data
text_ai: This paper investigates the automated recognition of structural bridge components using video data. Although understanding video data for structural inspections is straightforward for human inspectors, the implementation of the same task using machine learning methods has not been fully realized. We propose a deep learning framework that leverages spatiotemporal features from video streams to identify key bridge elements—such as bearings, girders, and expansion joints—under varying lighting and occlusion conditions. Our approach combines convolutional neural networks with temporal aggregation modules to exploit motion cues and structural context across consecutive frames. Evaluated on a newly collected dataset of highway bridge inspection videos, the method achieves over 85% mean average precision across component categories, significantly outperforming single-frame baselines. Moreover, we demonstrate that the model generalizes to unseen bridge types with minimal fine-tuning. These results suggest that video-based recognition can reduce reliance on manual annotation and enable more efficient, scalable structural health monitoring. Future work will address real-time deployment and integration with robotic inspection platforms.

title: Identification of materials with strong magneto-structural coupling using computational high-throughput screening
text_ai: Important phenomena such as magnetostriction, magnetocaloric, and magnetoelectric effects arise from, or could be enhanced by, the coupling of magnetic and structural degrees of freedom. The coupling of spin and lattice also influence transport and structural properties in magnetic materials in particular around phase transitions. Here we report a computational high-throughput screening of over 20,000 known inorganic compounds to identify materials exhibiting strong magneto-structural coupling. Our approach combines first-principles calculations with data-mining techniques, evaluating the energy landscape of magnetic and lattice degrees of freedom. We introduce a descriptor based on the change in magnetic moment under isotropic volume strain and the phonon softening associated with magnetic phase transitions. Screening reveals several promising candidate families, including certain Heusler alloys, pnictides, and chalcogenides, where magneto-structural coupling coefficients exceed those of known benchmark materials. The predicted materials are further validated through analysis of their electronic structure and magnetic exchange interactions. This work accelerates the discovery of functional materials for magnetocaloric refrigeration, magnetostrictive actuators, and multiferroic devices, and establishes a general framework for identifying coupling phenomena in correlated electron systems.

title: Discontinuation of disease-modifying therapy in patients with multiple sclerosis over age 60.
text_ai: The risk-benefit ratio of continuing immunomodulating disease-modifying therapy (DMT) in older multiple sclerosis (MS) patients is unknown. To evaluate clinical and patient-reported outcomes after stopping DMT in older MS patients. Retrospective, observational study identifying patients from our MS clinics who were aged over 60 and on DMT > 2 years. Patients were categorized into those who discontinued DMT (n=98) and those who continued (n=136). Mean follow-up was 4.2 ± 1.8 years. Primary outcome was annualized relapse rate; secondary outcomes included new/enlarging T2 lesions on MRI, confirmed disability progression (CDP) on the Expanded Disability Status Scale, and patient-reported outcomes (MSIS-29 physical and psychological scores, EQ-5D index). Groups were comparable in baseline age, sex, disease duration, and prior DMT exposure. Relapse rates were low and did not differ significantly between groups (0.08 vs 0.06 per year, p=0.42). Similarly, the proportion with new MRI lesions (16% vs 13%, p=0.51) and 2-year risk of CDP (12% vs 10%, p=0.68) were similar. However, stoppers reported better MSIS-29 physical scores (mean change −2.3 vs +1.1, p=0.03) and higher EQ-5D utility (0.78 vs 0.72, p=0.04). No serious adverse events attributable to DMT cessation were observed. In this older MS cohort, DMT discontinuation was not associated with increased relapse or MRI activity but with modest improvements in patient-reported physical health and quality of life. These findings suggest that in select patients aged over 60 with stable disease, DMT cessation may be a reasonable option, though prospective confirmation is warranted.

title: Optimizing squeezing in a coherent quantum feedback network of optical parametric oscillators
text_ai: Advances in the emerging field of coherent quantum feedback control (CQFC) have led to the development of new capabilities in the areas of quantum control and quantum engineering, with a particular impact on the theory and applications of quantum optical networks. In this work, we apply a coherent quantum feedback network comprising multiple optical parametric oscillators (OPOs) to optimize the generation of squeezed states—a key resource for continuous-variable quantum information processing. Unlike conventional measurement-based feedback, CQFC preserves quantum coherence by routing optical fields through fully unitary interconnections, avoiding decoherence from homodyne detection. We consider a network of two or more OPOs coupled via beam splitters and phase shifters, forming a closed-loop system whose dynamics are described by a quantum Langevin equation in the Heisenberg picture. The network’s squeezing spectrum depends on the internal cavity parameters, pump strengths, and the feedback topology. We derive an analytical condition for optimal single-mode squeezing at a given sideband frequency, expressed as a balance between parametric gain, cavity decay rates, and feedback phase. By numerically optimizing over feedback phases and coupling strengths, we show that squeezing can be enhanced beyond the standard 3 dB limit of a single OPO, reaching up to 6 dB in a two‑OPO network with appropriate impedance matching. Furthermore, we investigate the robustness of the optimal configuration against parameter fluctuations and find that the feedback network provides intrinsic stability when the loop gain satisfies a Nyquist criterion. Our results demonstrate that coherent feedback control offers a systematic, noise‑free method for engineering high‑squeezing quantum states in distributed optical systems, with potential applications in quantum metrology, teleportation, and continuous‑variable cluster‑state generation. The framework is generalizable to larger networks, paving the way for scalable quantum photonic circuits controlled entirely by coherent interactions.

title: Confined Dense Circumstellar Material Surrounding a Regular Type II Supernova: The Unique Flash-Spectroscopy Event of SN 2013fs
text_ai: With the advent of new wide-field, high-cadence optical transient surveys, our understanding of the diversity of core-collapse supernovae has grown tremendously in the last decade. However, the pre-supernova evolution of massive stars, that sets the physical backdrop to these violent events, is theoretically not well understood and difficult to probe observationally. SN 2013fs provides a rare and direct probe of this poorly understood phase. Discovered within hours of explosion by the intermediate Palomar Transient Factory, it was immediately classified as a normal Type IIP supernova. However, multi-epoch optical spectroscopy obtained from 3 to 20 days post-explosion revealed a remarkable flash-spectroscopy event: narrow, rapidly evolving emission lines of He ii, C iv, N iv, and N iii, superimposed on a blue continuum. These features arise from photoionization of a compact, dense shell of circumstellar material (CSM) located at a radius of ~ 5 × 10¹⁴ cm, with a mass of ~ 0.05 M⊙. The CSM's presence is consistent with a mass-loss rate of ~ 10⁻³ M⊙ yr⁻¹ in the final year before explosion — orders of magnitude higher than typical red supergiant winds. Crucially, the supernova itself appears otherwise normal in its photometric and spectral evolution, implying that such confined CSM may be common but previously undetected around regular Type II supernovae. These observations challenge existing models of late-stage stellar evolution and suggest a widespread, episodic mass-loss mechanism, possibly linked to violent nuclear burning instabilities or binary interaction. The discovery of SN 2013fs thus establishes that flash-spectroscopy events are not restricted to exotic supernovae but can occur in the most common explosions, offering a unique window into the final years of massive star life.

title: Direct observation of multiple topological phases in the iron-based superconductor Li(Fe,Co)As
text_ai: Topological insulators/semimetals and unconventional iron-based superconductors have attracted major attentions in condensed matter physics in the past 10 years. However, there is little overlap between these two fields, although the combination of topological states and superconducting states will produce more exotic topologically superconducting states and Majorana bound states (MBS), a promising candidate for realizing topological quantum computations. Here, we report the direct observation of multiple topological phases in the non-superconducting parent compound LiFeAs and its Co-doped superconducting counterpart via angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy. We find that the electronic structure hosts a topological Dirac semimetal phase with a pair of Dirac points near the Fermi level, as well as a topological insulator phase characterized by topologically nontrivial surface states. Remarkably, the topological nature persists upon Co substitution, which simultaneously induces superconductivity. The coexistence of these topological phases with superconductivity in a single stoichiometric material establishes Li(Fe,Co)As as a versatile platform for realizing Majorana bound states. Our results demonstrate that iron-based superconductors can intrinsically integrate topological electronic states, bridging the gap between topological quantum materials and unconventional superconductivity and offering a clear pathway toward topological quantum computation.

title: On the Analysis of Puncturing for Finite-Length Polar Codes: Boolean Function Approach
text_ai: This paper investigates the impact of puncturing on finite-length polar codes in which a puncturing pattern $\pv^{N}=(p_0,...,p_N)$ is applied to a length-$N$ polar code.. We first introduce two virtual channels to stochastically model the punctured (untransmitted) bits, which are respectively called {\em useless channel model} (UCM) and {\em deterministic channel model} (DCM). These models allow us to analytically assess the degradation of subchannel reliabilities due to puncturing. We then show that the polarization process can be characterized through Boolean functions derived from the puncturing pattern. By treating the virtual channels as binary-input output-symmetric channels, we derive closed-form expressions for Bhattacharyya parameters and mutual information for each synthetic channel. This enables a precise analysis without Monte Carlo simulations. Moreover, we propose a Boolean-function-based criterion for selecting puncturing patterns that minimize error performance loss. Our approach provides necessary and sufficient conditions for preserving polarization. Numerical results demonstrate that our method outperforms existing heuristics for short-to-moderate code lengths, offering insights into the structural properties of punctured polar codes.

title: Nuclear spin pair coherence in diamond for atomic scale magnetometry
text_ai: The nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centre, as a promising candidate solid state system of quantum information processing, its electron spin coherence is influenced by the magnetic field fluctuations due to the local environment. In pure diamonds, the environment consists of hundreds of C-13 nuclear spins randomly spreading in several nanometers range forming a spin bath. Here, we demonstrate that the coherence of individual C-13 nuclear spin pairs within this bath can be exploited for atomic-scale magnetometry. By applying dynamical decoupling sequences resonant with the dipolar coupling between proximal nuclear spins, we isolate and manipulate pair states, revealing coherence times exceeding hundreds of microseconds. The pair's combined magnetic moment provides a highly sensitive probe of external fields, with the dipolar interaction serving as an intrinsic reference that cancels common-mode noise. Using a single NV centre, we optically initialize and read out the pair state via hyperfine-mediated transfer, achieving a dc magnetic field sensitivity of ~10 nT/√Hz over nanoscale volumes. Crucially, the pair coherence is limited only by residual couplings to distant bath spins, which we characterise through a cluster-correlation expansion. Our results establish nuclear spin pairs as a robust, long-lived quantum sensor element, offering enhanced spatial resolution over single-spin probes. This approach paves the way for imaging few-nuclear-spin structures and detecting weak fields with sub-angstrom precision, directly applicable to nanoscale nuclear magnetic resonance and condensed matter physics.

title: CL-HOI: Cross-Level Human-Object Interaction Distillation from Vision Large Language Models
text_ai: Human-object interaction (HOI) detection has seen advancements with Vision Language Models (VLMs), but these methods often depend on extensive manual annotations. Vision Large Language Models (VLLMs) can inherently recognize and reason about interactions at the image level but are computationally heavy and not designed for instance-level HOI detection. To address these challenges, we propose CL-HOI, a cross-level distillation framework that transfers interaction knowledge from VLLMs to a lightweight instance-level HOI detector. Our method leverages the VLLM’s inherent image-level reasoning capability without requiring additional manual annotations. Specifically, we design a dual-path distillation strategy: an interaction-level path that aligns the teacher’s holistic scene understanding with the student’s pairwise interaction features, and an object-level path that refines human and object representations. In addition, we introduce an adaptive weighting mechanism to balance contributions from different reasoning levels. Extensive experiments on V-COCO and HICO-DET benchmarks demonstrate that CL-HOI achieves competitive performance compared to fully-supervised methods while significantly reducing annotation cost and inference overhead. Our work highlights the potential of distilling high-level visual reasoning from VLLMs for fine-grained, instance-centric detection tasks.

title: AudioSR: Versatile Audio Super-resolution at Scale
text_ai: Audio super-resolution is a fundamental task that predicts high-frequency components for low-resolution audio, enhancing audio quality in digital applications. Previous methods have limitations such as the limited scope of audio types (e.g., music, speech) and specific bandwidth settings they can handle (e.g., 4kHz to 8kHz). We propose AudioSR, a versatile audio super-resolution model that operates across diverse audio types—including speech, music, and environmental sounds—and arbitrary input bandwidths from 4 kHz to 24 kHz. Leveraging a latent diffusion architecture trained on a large-scale dataset of over 1 million audio clips, AudioSR consistently reconstructs high-fidelity, high-resolution audio (up to 48 kHz sampling rate) from degraded inputs, regardless of the original content or bandwidth. Extensive objective and subjective evaluations demonstrate that AudioSR outperforms existing methods on both matched and unseen bandwidth settings, generalizing robustly to diverse real-world scenarios. Furthermore, we show the model's scalability: increasing dataset size and model capacity yields systematic improvements in reconstruction quality. AudioSR thus represents a significant step toward a unified, practical audio super-resolution solution for broad consumer and professional applications.

title: Investigation of Long Baseline Neutrino Oscillations from Experiments at KAON
text_ai: The proposed KAON factory at the Triumf Laboratory in Vancouver, Canada provides a unique opportunity for high statistics long baseline neutrino oscillation experiments. Several possibilities are under active consideration. In this paper we describe the theoretical expectations for a {\it very} long baseline experiment in which the neutrinos are directed towards, and detected at the Superkamiokande detector in Kamioka, Japan 7200 km away. We analyze the sensitivity of such an experiment to the neutrino mass hierarchy, the octant of θ₂₃, and the CP-violating phase δ. The extreme baseline ensures strong matter effects, which dominate the oscillation probability and allow unambiguous determination of the sign of Δm²₃₁. Using the high-intensity neutrino beam from KAON, we simulate event rates in Super-Kamiokande for both ν_μ→ν_e and ν_μ→ν_μ channels, incorporating realistic energy resolution, background rates, and systematic uncertainties. Our results demonstrate that a 7200 km baseline with a 50 kt detector can resolve the mass hierarchy at 3σ confidence for nearly all values of δ, and measure δ to within 10° after five years of operation. The experiment also provides exceptional sensitivity to non-standard interactions and sterile neutrino mixing. We conclude that the KAON-to-Super-Kamiokande project offers a powerful and complementary probe of the neutrino sector, rivaling or exceeding the capabilities of proposed facilities with shorter baselines.

title: Graph-Aware Language Model Pre-Training on a Large Graph Corpus Can Help Multiple Graph Applications
text_ai: Model pre-training on large text corpora has been demonstrated effective for various downstream applications in the NLP domain. In the graph mining domain, a similar analogy can be drawn for pre-training graph models on large graphs in the hope of benefiting downstream graph applications, which has also been explored by several recent studies. However, existing graph pre-training methods primarily focus on learning node or graph-level representations and often overlook the rich semantic information embedded in textual attributes associated with graphs. Moreover, they are typically tailored to specific downstream tasks, limiting their generalizability. In this work, we propose a novel graph-aware language model pre-training framework that operates on a large-scale graph corpus consisting of text-rich graphs. Our approach jointly encodes graph structure and textual semantics by designing graph-aware masking and contrastive objectives, enabling the model to capture both topological and linguistic patterns. Pre-trained on a massive collection of diverse graphs (e.g., citation networks, social graphs, and knowledge graphs), the resulting model serves as a versatile foundation that can be fine-tuned for multiple graph applications, including node classification, link prediction, and graph classification. Extensive experiments on ten benchmark datasets demonstrate that our pre-trained model consistently outperforms both graph-only and text-only baselines, achieving new state-of-the-art results across tasks while requiring significantly less fine-tuning data.

title: CIMTx: An R package for causal inference with multiple treatments using observational data
text_ai: CIMTx provides efficient and unified functions to implement modern methods for causal inferences with multiple treatments using observational data with a focus on binary outcomes. The methods include regression adjustment, inverse probability of treatment weighting, Bayesian additive regression trees, regression adjustment with multivariate spline of the generalized propensity score, vector matching and targeted maximum likelihood estimation. The package offers a unified interface for estimating causal effects, including average treatment effects and conditional effects, with robust variance estimation. It also provides diagnostic tools for assessing covariate balance across multiple treatment groups and for evaluating the positivity assumption. CIMTx facilitates sensitivity analysis for unmeasured confounding using a Monte Carlo approach. Through extensive simulation studies, the package demonstrates strong performance across various scenarios, including non-linear relationships and moderate violations of assumptions. An application to a real dataset illustrates its practical use in comparative effectiveness research. CIMTx is freely available on the Comprehensive R Archive Network, with comprehensive documentation and vignettes to guide users.

title: Discovering Relationships between Object Categories via Universal Canonical Maps
text_ai: We tackle the problem of learning the geometry of multiple categories of deformable objects jointly. Recent work has shown that it is possible to learn a unified dense pose predictor for several categories of related objects. However, training such models requires to initialize inter-category correspondences by hand. We overcome this limitation by learning a universal canonical map that automatically discovers inter-category correspondences. Our approach jointly optimizes a shared dense pose predictor and category-specific deformation fields, trained end-to-end to align objects from different categories into a common canonical space. The alignment is driven by a consistency loss between predicted canonical coordinates and warped deformations, which naturally reveals correspondences between semantically similar parts. Evaluations on standard benchmarks demonstrate that our method not only achieves state-of-the-art dense pose estimation but also uncovers interpretable relationships, such as the mapping between animal legs and human arms. Our work shows that effective inter-category correspondences can be learned without manual initialization, paving the way for more general object understanding.

title: Voyager 2 solar plasma and magnetic field spectral analysis for intermediate data sparsity
text_ai: The Voyager probes are the furthest, still active, spacecraft ever launched from Earth. During their 38-year trip, they have collected data regarding solar wind properties (such as the plasma velocity and magnetic field intensity). Unfortunately, a complete time evolution of the measured physical quantities is not available. This study focuses on the analysis of plasma velocity and magnetic field data from Voyager 2, specifically addressing the challenge of intermediate data sparsity—where data gaps are frequent yet not severe enough to preclude spectral estimation. We employ a modified Lomb-Scargle periodogram adapted for non-uniformly sampled time series, combined with wavelet-based filtering to isolate coherent structures. The resulting power spectra reveal a Kolmogorov-like -5/3 scaling in the inertial range, consistent with magnetohydrodynamic turbulence, but with notable deviations at lower frequencies possibly due to solar cycle variations. Additionally, cross-spectral analysis between the two quantities indicates a high degree of Alfvénic correlation in the inner heliosphere, diminishing with distance. These findings demonstrate that even with data sparsity, robust spectral features can be extracted, providing insights into the evolution of solar wind turbulence from 1 to 40 AU. The methodology is validated against synthetic data and offers a template for future analysis of similar sparsely sampled space plasma datasets.

title: Best Practices for Alchemical Free Energy Calculations
text_ai: Alchemical free energy calculations are a useful tool for predicting free energy differences associated with the transfer of molecules from one environment to another. The hallmark of these methods is the use of "bridging" potential energy functions representing \emph{alchemical} intermediate states that cannot exist as real chemical species. However, their widespread adoption in drug discovery and molecular design has been hindered by practical challenges in setup, execution, and analysis. This review outlines best practices for conducting reliable alchemical free energy calculations, emphasizing key steps such as system preparation, choice of alchemical pathway, and Hamiltonian replica exchange to enhance sampling. We discuss strategies for managing electrostatic and van der Waals decoupling, avoiding singularities via softcore potentials, and selecting appropriate softcore parameters. Critical considerations for achieving convergence—including simulation length, number of intermediate states, and the use of multiple independent replicates—are addressed. Recommendations for tail corrections, barostat handling, and periodic boundary artifacts are provided. Finally, we highlight common pitfalls in analysis methods, such as the need for adequate equilibration and the proper use of thermodynamic integration (TI) and Bennett acceptance ratio (BAR) estimators. By adhering to these guidelines, practitioners can significantly improve the accuracy, reproducibility, and throughput of alchemical free energy predictions in realistic molecular systems.

title: Rashba interferometers: Spin-dependent single and two-electron interference
text_ai: Quantum transport in semiconductor nanostructures can be described theoretically in terms of the propagation and scattering of electron probability waves. Within this approach, elements of a phase-coherent electric circuit play a role similar to quantum-optical devices that can be characterised by scattering matrices. Here, we extend this analogy to interferometers where the Rashba spin-orbit coupling introduces a spin-dependent phase coherently accumulated along the electron trajectories. The resulting spin-orbit-induced Aharonov-Casher phase modifies the interference pattern in a controllable manner via an external gate voltage, yielding a fully tunable spin filter. For single-electron transport, we derive the spin-resolved transmission probabilities and show that the Rashba effect can induce a complete suppression of current for one spin orientation while maximizing the other, thereby realizing a spin polarizer with no ferromagnetic elements. We then analyze two-electron interference in the same geometry, accounting for both spin-statistical and Coulomb interaction effects. Using a scattering matrix formalism that incorporates the Rashba spin rotation, we compute the two-particle interference contribution to the current noise and the second-order correlation function. Strikingly, we predict that the exchange phase arising from the fermionic antisymmetry can interfere destructively with the Aharonov-Casher phase, leading to novel spin-entangled states. The resulting bunching and antibunching statistics are directly tunable by the Rashba coupling strength. Our results demonstrate that Rashba interferometers provide a platform for on-demand generation of spin-entangled electron pairs and for exploring fundamental aspects of quantum coherence in the presence of spin-orbit interactions, with potential applications in spintronics and quantum information processing.

title: Conformational selection and induced changes along the catalytic cycle of E. coli DHFR
text_ai: Protein function often involves changes between different conformations. Central questions are how these conformational changes are coupled to the binding or catalytic processes during which they occur, and how they affect the catalytic rates of enzymes. An important model system is the enzyme dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR) from E. coli, which has been extensively studied as a prototype for understanding the interplay between conformational dynamics and enzymatic function. Here, we combine extensive molecular dynamics simulations with Markov state models to dissect the conformational landscape of DHFR along its entire catalytic cycle, including each intermediate state and transition. Our analysis reveals that the enzyme predominantly samples a small set of pre-existing conformations corresponding to key functional states, such as the closed, occluded, and open forms. Substrate and cofactor binding do not induce entirely new conformations but rather shift the population toward those already sampled in the apo enzyme, consistent with a conformational selection mechanism. However, within the bound states, the catalytic steps themselves—particularly the hydride transfer and product release—are accompanied by subtle, induced conformational changes that are not observed in the absence of chemical turnover. These induced shifts fine-tune the active site geometry and electrostatic environment, thereby modulating the free energy barriers for individual steps. By integrating these findings into a kinetic model, we demonstrate that the catalytic cycle of DHFR is governed by a hybrid mechanism: conformational selection dominates the binding and release steps, while induced changes operate during the chemical transformation and product egress. This work provides a unified framework for understanding how conformational dynamics—both pre-existing and reaction-triggered—orchestrate the efficiency of a prototypical enzyme, with implications for the design of allosteric inhibitors and engineering of altered catalytic activity.

title: Oscillations in three-reaction quadratic mass-action systems
text_ai: It is known that rank-two bimolecular mass-action systems do not admit limit cycles. With a view to understanding which small mass-action systems admit oscillation, in this paper we study rank-two networks with bimolecular source complexes but allow target complexes with higher molecularities. We consider networks with exactly three reactions, each with a bimolecular source complex. Under mass-action kinetics, the dynamics is governed by ordinary differential equations with polynomial nonlinearities of degree up to three. By analyzing the characteristic polynomial of the Jacobian matrix at a positive equilibrium, we derive necessary and sufficient conditions for a Hopf bifurcation. We show that oscillations arise only when the network includes at least one trimolecular target and the determinant of a certain symbolic matrix vanishes. Using computational algebraic geometry, we identify a one-parameter family of networks that admit limit cycles. In particular, we present an explicit three-reaction system with a rank-two stoichiometric matrix that exhibits a stable limit cycle via subcritical Hopf bifurcation. Our findings demonstrate that the restriction to purely bimolecular systems is critical for the absence of oscillations in rank-two networks, as a single higher-molecularity target can induce oscillations. This work provides a systematic classification of oscillatory three-reaction quadratic systems and offers new insights into the minimal network structures capable of sustained oscillations.
prefix: It is known that rank-two bimolecular mass-action systems do not admit limit cycles. With a view to understanding which small mass-action systems admit oscillation, in this paper we study rank-two networks with bimolecular source complexes but allow target complexes with higher molecularities.

title: Financial Burdens of Out-of-Pocket Spending Among Medicare Fee-for-Service Beneficiaries: Role of the "Big Four" Chronic Health Conditions.
text_ai: While Medicare is the universal source of health care coverage for Americans aged 65 years or older, the program requires significant cost sharing in terms of out-of-pocket (OOP) spending. This study investigates the magnitude and distribution of OOP spending burdens among Medicare Fee-for-Service beneficiaries, with particular emphasis on the role of the "Big Four" chronic conditions—hypertension, heart disease, diabetes, and cancer. Using data from the 2019 Medicare Current Beneficiary Survey, we examine total OOP expenditures, including premiums, deductibles, and cost-sharing, across subgroups defined by condition status and number of conditions. Adjusted analyses reveal that beneficiaries with any of the Big Four face substantially higher OOP costs, with mean annual spending exceeding $5,500 for those with three or more conditions compared to $2,200 for those without. More critically, the incidence of high financial burden—defined as OOP spending exceeding 20% of household income—is nearly threefold greater among beneficiaries with multiple chronic conditions. Among those with cancer plus another Big Four condition, nearly one in four experiences catastrophic spending. These disparities persist after controlling for income, supplemental insurance, and demographic factors. The findings underscore that the Big Four chronic conditions drive considerable heterogeneity in financial exposure, pointing to the need for targeted cost-sharing relief and more comprehensive coverage design to mitigate the economic vulnerability of the most medically complex beneficiaries.
prefix: While Medicare is the universal source of health care coverage for Americans aged 65 years or older, the program requires significant cost sharing in terms of out-of-pocket (OOP) spending.

title: Single-Particle Green Functions in Exactly Solvable Models of Bose and Fermi Liquids
text_ai: Based on a class of exactly solvable models of interacting bose and fermi liquids, we compute the single-particle propagators of these systems exactly for all wavelengths and energies and in any number of spatial dimensions. These propagators are expressed in closed form, revealing universal features such as quasiparticle poles and incoherent continua for both bosonic and fermionic systems. For Bose liquids, the Green function exhibits a gapless mode governed by Bogoliubov theory, while fermionic systems display a sharp Fermi surface with a renormalized self-energy. The exact analytic structure allows for unambiguous extraction of thermodynamic and transport properties, including the momentum distribution and effective mass, without approximation. In one spatial dimension, the results reduce to the well-known Tomonaga-Luttinger liquid behavior, but our solution extends this to higher dimensions, uncovering non-Fermi liquid characteristics in certain interaction regimes. The spectral functions are computed exactly, showing power-law tails and branch cuts that signify the absence of well-defined quasiparticles in some cases. This exact treatment provides a benchmark for perturbative methods and illuminates the role of dimensionality and statistics in strongly correlated systems. Our findings demonstrate that exactly solvable models in higher dimensions can capture complex many-body dynamics, offering a unified perspective on Bose and Fermi liquids.
prefix: Based on a class of exactly solvable models of interacting bose and fermi liquids, we compute the single-particle propagators of these systems exactly for all wavelengths and energies and in any number of spatial dimensions.

title: Graphical Modelling in Genetics and Systems Biology
text_ai: Graphical modelling has a long history in statistics as a tool for the analysis of multivariate data, starting from Wright's path analysis and Gibbs' applications to statistical physics at the beginning of the last century. However, their widespread adoption in genetics and systems biology has been driven more recently by the advent of high-throughput molecular data. In these fields, graphical models provide a principled framework for representing and inferring complex dependency structures, such as gene regulatory networks, protein–protein interaction networks, and metabolic flux diagrams. Directed acyclic graphs (Bayesian networks) and undirected graphical models (Markov random fields) capture conditional independence relationships, enabling the decomposition of multivariate distributions into local components. This facilitates both exploratory analysis—learning network topology from data—and confirmatory analysis—testing specific hypotheses about causal or associative links. Key challenges include the curse of dimensionality, model selection consistency under sparsity, and the integration of heterogeneous data types (e.g., expression, sequence, and epigenetic information). Recent methodological advances incorporate latent variable models, dynamic Bayesian networks for time-course data, and structure learning algorithms that scale to thousands of nodes. Graphical modelling thus continues to unify statistical theory with biological discovery, offering a powerful language for systems-level understanding.
prefix: Graphical modelling has a long history in statistics as a tool for the analysis of multivariate data, starting from Wright's path analysis and Gibbs' applications to statistical physics at the beginning of the last century.

title: Seroepidemiology of Toxoplasma gondii in wild ruminants in Spain.
text_ai: Toxoplasmosis is a parasitic zoonosis caused by Toxoplasma gondii which infects warm-blooded species worldwide. Humans can be infected through ingestion of tissue cysts from raw or undercooked meat, including game meat. A nationwide large-scale cross-sectional study was conducted to assess exposure to T. gondii in seven wild ruminant species in Spain. Serum samples were collected from 2,345 individuals across 15 Spanish provinces between 2012 and 2021, representing all seven target species: red deer (Cervus elaphus), roe deer (Capreolus capreolus), fallow deer (Dama dama), Iberian ibex (Capra pyrenaica), mouflon (Ovis aries musimon), chamois (Rupicapra pyrenaica), and Barbary sheep (Ammotragus lervia). Anti-T. gondii IgG antibodies were detected using a commercial ELISA, with a subset confirmed by modified agglutination test (MAT). Overall seroprevalence reached 34.8% (95% CI: 32.9–36.7), ranging from 19.2% in chamois to 47.6% in Iberian ibex. Multivariable logistic regression identified species, age (higher in adults), sex (greater in females), and biogeographical region (elevated in Mediterranean ecosystems) as significant predictors. These results demonstrate widespread and heterogeneous exposure across spatial, demographic, and ecological gradients, underscoring the potential role of wild ruminants as reservoirs for T. gondii in Iberian ecosystems. The findings have implications for public health through consumption of game meat, for conservation management of susceptible species, and for understanding parasite transmission at the wildlife–livestock–human interface.

title: Effects of Stellar Feedback on Stellar and Gas Kinematics of Star-Forming Galaxies at 0.6<z<1.0
text_ai: Recent zoom-in cosmological simulations have shown that stellar feedback can flatten the inner density profile of the dark matter halo in low-mass galaxies. A correlation between the stellar/gas velocity dispersion ($\sigma_{star}$, $\sigma_{gas}$) and the specific star formation rate (sSFR) is predicted as an observational test of the role of stellar feedback in re-shaping the dark matter density profile. We test this prediction using a sample of ~400 star-forming galaxies at 0.6<z<1.0 from the KMOS3D survey with integral field spectroscopy. We measure spatially resolved stellar kinematics from continuum fitting and gas kinematics from Hα emission lines. Both σ_star and σ_gas are derived after correcting for beam smearing and rotational broadening. We find a positive correlation between σ and sSFR, with σ_star increasing from ~30 km/s to ~60 km/s over the sSFR range, consistent with feedback-driven turbulence. The correlation is stronger for gas than for stars, suggesting that gas is more responsive to stellar feedback. We also find that galaxies with higher sSFR exhibit more asymmetric kinematics, as measured by the velocity dispersion map. The σ–sSFR correlation persists after controlling for stellar mass and redshift, indicating a direct feedback effect. Comparing with simulations, our results support the scenario where stellar feedback injects energy into the interstellar medium, raising the velocity dispersion and simultaneously flattening the dark matter density profile. However, the scatter is large due to variations in galaxy inclination and merger fraction. These findings demonstrate that stellar feedback significantly affects kinematics at z~0.8, providing observational constraints on feedback models in cosmological simulations.

A correlation between the stellar/gas velocity dispersion ($\sigma_{star}$, $\sigma_{gas}$) and the specific star formation rate (sSFR) is predicted as an observational test of the role of stellar feedback in re-shaping the dark matter density profile.

title: Image Quality Assessment Guided Deep Neural Networks Training
text_ai: For many computer vision problems, the deep neural networks are trained and validated based on the assumption that the input images are pristine (i.e., artifact-free). However, digital images are subject to a wide range of distortions in real application scenarios, while the practical issues regarding image quality in high level visual information understanding have been largely ignored. To address this gap, we propose a novel training framework that integrates Image Quality Assessment (IQA) directly into the optimization loop of deep neural networks. By leveraging differentiable IQA metrics as regularizers or loss components, the model becomes explicitly aware of perceptual quality during learning. This guidance encourages the network to develop robust feature representations that are insensitive to common corruptions such as noise, blur, and compression artifacts. Extensive experiments on image classification and semantic segmentation tasks demonstrate that networks trained with IQA guidance not only achieve higher accuracy on distorted inputs but also maintain competitive performance on clean data. Furthermore, the approach generalizes across multiple distortion types and severities, offering a principled solution to bridge the gap between idealized training conditions and practical deployment. Our findings highlight the critical role of quality awareness in advancing high-level vision tasks under real-world imaging conditions.

However, digital images are subject to a wide range of distortions in real application scenarios, while the practical issues regarding image quality in high level visual information understanding have been largely ignored.

title: Discrete-to-continuum limits of interacting particle systems in one dimension with collisions
text_ai: We study a class of interacting particle systems in which $n$ signed particles move on the real line. At close range particles with the same sign repel and particles with opposite sign attract each other. The repulsion and attraction are described by the same singular interaction force $f$. We consider the mean-field scaling where the interaction potential is scaled by $1/n$, leading to a nontrivial continuum limit. The empirical measure converges to a density $\rho(t,x)$ satisfying a nonlocal conservation law with convolution kernel $f$. A key challenge is collisions between opposite-signed particles, which in the continuum cause shock formation and mass transfer. Using the one-dimensional structure, we derive the limiting velocity field via the Hilbert transform, linking the system to an eikonal equation. We prove rigorous convergence of the particle system to the continuum model for smooth initial data without prior collisions, and we characterize the emergence of singularities through the approach of particle trajectories. The analysis relies on careful estimates of particle trajectories and the stability of the continuum equation. Furthermore, we discuss how collisions reduce total mass density, analogous to annihilation processes, and validate our results with numerical simulations that illustrate shock formation and discrete-to-continuum convergence.
