At close range particles with the same sign repel and particles with opposite sign attract each other. The repulsion and attraction are described by the same singular interaction force $f$.

title: BodyMetric: Evaluating the Realism of Human Bodies in Text-to-Image Generation
text_ai: Accurately generating images of human bodies from text remains a challenging problem for state of the art text-to-image models. Commonly observed body-related artifacts include extra or missing limbs, unrealistic poses, blurred body parts, etc. Currently, evaluation of such artifacts relies heavily on time-consuming human judgments, limiting the ability to benchmark models at scale. To address this, we introduce BodyMetric, a novel automated evaluation framework that quantifies the realism of generated human bodies by detecting and counting common anatomical anomalies—such as extra limbs, missing parts, and distorted proportions—directly from generated images without requiring reference images or human annotators. BodyMetric leverages a specialized body-part segmentation model and a set of geometric heuristics to identify violations of natural human morphology. We validate BodyMetric by comparing its scores with human perceptual judgments on a diverse set of images from leading text-to-image models, achieving high correlation (Spearman ρ > 0.85) across multiple artifact types. Furthermore, we demonstrate the framework's scalability by evaluating over 10,000 generated images, revealing significant performance gaps between models and fine-grained breakdowns of failure modes (e.g., hands vs. legs). BodyMetric enables rapid, reproducible, and fine-grained benchmarking, facilitating progress toward more anatomically correct human generation. The metric is publicly released to support future research.

title: PeV Neutrinos and a 3.5 keV X-Ray Line from a PeV Scale Supersymmetric Neutrino Sector
text_ai: Recent measurements of PeV energy neutrinos at IceCube and a 3.5 keV X-ray line in the spectra of several galaxies are both tantalizing signatures of new physics. This paper shows that one or both of these observations can be explained within an extended supersymmetric neutrino sector. We consider a supersymmetric extension of the Standard Model with an additional gauge singlet chiral superfield, containing a sterile neutrino and its scalar partner. The PeV scale is set by the mass of the sterile neutrino, which decays into a lighter sterile neutrino and a photon, producing the 3.5 keV line. Simultaneously, the scalar partner decays into standard model neutrinos, yielding the observed PeV neutrino flux at IceCube. Alternatively, both signals can arise from the decay of a PeV-scale neutralino. We show that the required lifetimes and branching ratios are consistent with supersymmetric parameters and that the model can accommodate either or both observations without fine-tuning. The scenario predicts a correlated spectral signature that can be tested with future observations.

title: Individualized PATE: Differentially Private Machine Learning with Individual Privacy Guarantees
text_ai: Applying machine learning (ML) to sensitive domains requires privacy protection of the underlying training data through formal privacy frameworks, such as differential privacy (DP). Yet, usually, the privacy of the training data comes at the cost of the resulting ML models' utility. To address this trade-off, we introduce Individualized PATE, a novel framework that extends the Private Aggregation of Teacher Ensembles (PATE) mechanism to provide per-data-point privacy guarantees. Unlike standard DP, which enforces a uniform privacy bound across the entire dataset, our approach assigns an individual privacy budget to each training example, reflecting the heterogeneous privacy preferences or sensitivity levels of data contributors. This is achieved by modifying the teacher aggregation step: teachers vote on queries, but the aggregation noise is calibrated according to the maximum privacy budget among data points that influence the vote, while also employing a novel privacy accountant that tracks contributions at the granularity of individual records. We prove that Individualized PATE satisfies a personalized variant of differential privacy, where each data point’s guarantee is formalized as an ε_i-DP or (ε_i, δ_i)-DP bound. The student model is then trained using these privatized labels, with careful composition across multiple queries to prevent cumulative privacy leakage beyond the intended individual budgets. Experiments on benchmark datasets (e.g., MNIST, UCI Adult) demonstrate that our method significantly improves model utility compared to standard PATE when data points have highly variable privacy requirements. For instance, allowing a small fraction of low-sensitivity data to tolerate higher noise yields a 5–10% accuracy gain, while strictly preserving higher privacy for sensitive examples. Our work thus enables practical deployment of differentially private ML in settings where data subjects demand personalized privacy, such as healthcare and finance.
prefix: Applying machine learning (ML) to sensitive domains requires privacy protection of the underlying training data through formal privacy frameworks, such as differential privacy (DP). Yet, usually, the privacy of the training data comes at the cost of the resulting ML models' utility.

title: Quenched Lattice QCD with Domain Wall Fermions and the Chiral Limit
text_ai: Quenched QCD simulations on three volumes, $8^3 \times$, $12^3 \times$ and $16^3 \times 32$ and three couplings, $\beta=5.7$, 5.85 and 6.0 using domain wall fermions provide a consistent picture of quenched QCD. We employ a fifth dimension of length $L_s = 16$ and a domain wall height $M=1.8$ in lattice units. After non-perturbative tuning to ensure good chiral symmetry, the residual mass $m_{\rm res}$ is extracted and found to be on the order of a few MeV, exhibiting mild dependence on the volume and coupling. Pion masses are computed from correlators of pseudoscalar operators with point sources and sinks. The quark mass is defined as $m_q = m_f + m_{\rm res}$ where $m_f$ is the input fermion mass. By varying $m_f$ over a range that yields pion masses down to approximately 250 MeV, we map out the chiral regime. The data for $m_\pi^2$ and $f_\pi$ as functions of $m_q$ are fitted to functional forms derived from quenched chiral perturbation theory (Q$\chi$PT). The fits incorporate both one-loop and partially two-loop corrections. We find that the quenched chiral logarithm parameter $\delta$ takes a value consistent with expectations from other determinations. The pion decay constant in the chiral limit is extrapolated, and we comment on the consistency with the Gell-Mann–Oakes–Renner relation. Finite volume effects are studied by comparing results from the three spatial volumes, and we find them to be under control for our lighter masses. Scaling violations are examined by comparing results at three lattice spacings, which range from approximately 0.17 fm to 0.10 fm. Overall, the simulations demonstrate that domain wall fermions provide a reliable and consistent description of quenched QCD, particularly in the approach to the chiral limit, with controlled systematic errors.

title: Theory of analytical energy derivatives for the variational quantum eigensolver
text_ai: The variational quantum eigensolver (VQE) and its variants, which is a method for finding eigenstates and eigenenergies of a given Hamiltonian, are appealing applications of near-term quantum computers. Although the eigenenergies are certainly important quantities which determines properties of a given system, their derivatives with respect to parameters of the system, such as positions of nuclei if we target a quantum chemistry problem, are also crucial to analyze the system. In this work, we develop a comprehensive theory for computing analytical energy derivatives within the VQE framework. While numerical differentiation is straightforward, it suffers from noise amplification and high sampling costs on quantum hardware. We derive exact expressions for first and second derivatives of the VQE energy with respect to external parameters, leveraging the Hellmann–Feynman theorem and the variational principle. Our approach eliminates the need for finite-difference approximations and provides a rigorous foundation for gradient-based optimization and property calculations. We also discuss the extension to state-averaged VQE and the treatment of degeneracies. This theory enables efficient and accurate evaluation of forces, Hessians, and response properties, thereby broadening the applicability of VQE to practical quantum chemistry tasks.

title: Inflexibility and independence: Phase transitions in the majority-rule model
text_ai: In this work we study opinion formation in a population participating of a public debate with two distinct choices. We considered three distinct mechanisms of social interactions and individuals' behavior: conformity, nonconformity and inflexibility. The conformity is ruled by the majority-rule dynamics, whereas the nonconformity is introduced in the population as an independent behavior, implying the failure to attempted group influence. Inflexibility is modeled as a fixed fraction of agents who never change their opinion, regardless of the majority influence. Using a mean-field approach complemented by extensive Monte Carlo simulations on regular lattices and random graphs, we analyze the phase diagram. The system exhibits a rich landscape with both continuous and discontinuous phase transitions. Notably, increasing the density of inflexible individuals can drive the system from a consensus phase through a critical point into a polarized phase, where both opinions coexist. Nonconformity, acting as thermal noise, shifts the critical boundaries and can induce a reentrant transition. We compute critical exponents and find evidence of universality with the Ising model in certain regimes. These results demonstrate how the interplay between inflexibility and independence governs the emergence of collective opinion patterns.

title: Cocommutative q-cycle coalgebra structures on the dual of the truncated polynomial algebra
text_ai: In order to construct solutions of the braid equation we consider bijective left non-degenerate set-theoretic type solutions, which correspond to regular q-cycle coalgebras. We obtain a partial classification of the different q-cycle coalgebra structures on the dual coalgebra of $K[y]/\langle y^n\rangle$, the truncated polynomial algebra. We explicitly describe these structures for small n and provide a general framework using the q-deformation parameter. The classification analyzes comultiplication and counit conditions for regular q-cycle coalgebras. Key results characterize when these structures yield bijective left non-degenerate solutions. For n=2, a complete classification is obtained; for higher n, partial results in terms of field parameters are given. The dual coalgebra admits a family of structures parametrized by elements of K satisfying polynomial equations. These structures correspond to new set-theoretic solutions of the braid equation, highlighting the rich algebraic structure of the truncated polynomial algebra's dual and opening avenues for constructing further solutions from coalgebra theory, and we illustrate these with examples.

We obtain a partial classification of the different q-cycle coalgebra structures on the dual coalgebra of $K[y]/\langle y^n\rangle$, the truncated polynomial algebra.

title: What Makes for Good Views for Contrastive Learning?
text_ai: Contrastive learning between multiple views of the data has recently achieved state of the art performance in the field of self-supervised representation learning. Despite its success, the influence of different view choices has been less studied. In this paper, we conduct a systematic investigation into what constitutes good views for contrastive learning. We propose a theoretical framework based on the information bottleneck principle, arguing that effective views should share minimal mutual information while preserving sufficient task-relevant information. We introduce the InfoMin principle and demonstrate that optimal views are those that maximize the reduction of mutual information between augmentations subject to a constraint on downstream task performance. Through extensive experiments on image, video, and graph datasets, we validate this principle and show that it consistently improves representation quality across different contrastive learning objectives, architectures, and downstream tasks. Our analysis reveals that simple, task-agnostic augmentations like random crop and color distortion already approximate InfoMin views for images, while more domain-appropriate views are necessary for structured data. We also provide practical guidelines for view design in new domains. Our findings offer a principled understanding of why certain views work better than others and enable the systematic construction of effective views for contrastive learning.
prefix: Contrastive learning between multiple views of the data has recently achieved state of the art performance in the field of self-supervised representation learning. Despite its success, the influence of different view choices has been less studied.

title: Structure Modeling Activation Free Fourier Network for Spacecraft Image Denoising
text_ai: Spacecraft image denoising is a crucial fundamental technology closely related to aerospace research. However, the existing deep learning-based image denoising methods are primarily designed for natural image and fail to adequately consider the characteristics of spacecraft image(e.g. low-light conditions, repetitive periodic structures), resulting in suboptimal performance in the spacecraft image denoising task. To address these limitations, we propose a Structure Modeling Activation Free Fourier Network (SMAFF-Net) that explicitly captures low-light distributions and periodic patterns inherent in spacecraft imagery. The network integrates a learnable Fourier domain branch to model repetitive structures via spectral filtering, while an activation-free denoising module avoids nonlinearity-induced information loss under extreme low-light conditions. A structural modeling block further enforces spatial consistency by leveraging cross-frequency correlations. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real spacecraft datasets demonstrate that SMAFF-Net outperforms state-of-the-art methods by up to 2.8 dB in PSNR while preserving fine-grained details. Ablation studies validate the effectiveness of each component, highlighting the potential of domain-specific design for aerospace remote sensing tasks.

title: Relativistic diffusion
text_ai: We discuss a relativistic diffusion in the proper time in an approach of Schay and Dudley. We derive (Langevin) stochastic differential equations in various coordinates.We show that in some coordinates the stochastic differential equations become linear. We obtain momentum probability distribution in an explicit form.We discuss a relativistic particle diffusing in an external electromagnetic field. We analyze the stationary distribution and confirm its agreement with the relativistic Maxwell–Jüttner distribution. The presence of the electromagnetic field introduces a drift that corresponds to the Lorentz force. We show that the momentum distribution in this case is a boosted Jüttner distribution with the drift velocity determined by the field. In linearizing coordinates, such as rapidity, the stochastic differential equations decouple, enabling exact solution for the propagator. We compute the moments and the autocorrelation function of the four-momentum. The proper-time parametrization maintains manifest Lorentz covariance. We also discuss the relation between the proper-time diffusion and the world-line formulation of relativistic stochastic processes. The explicit solution for the momentum distribution allows the computation of the entropy production and the verification of the fluctuation theorem. Our results provide a rigorous foundation for relativistic diffusion and extend the Dudley–Schay framework to include external fields. We conclude by outlining potential applications to heavy-ion phenomenology and high-energy astrophysics.

title: Competitive Collaboration: Joint Unsupervised Learning of Depth, Camera Motion, Optical Flow and Motion Segmentation
text_ai: We address the unsupervised learning of several interconnected problems in low-level vision: single view depth prediction, camera motion estimation, optical flow, and segmentation of a video into the static scene and moving regions. Our key insight is that these four fundamental vision problems are coupled through geometric constraints. We propose a unified framework that jointly learns all four tasks in an unsupervised manner, enforcing geometric consistency between them. Our model comprises multiple sub-networks that estimate depth, camera motion, optical flow, and a motion segmentation mask. These networks are trained together using a combination of photometric and geometric losses: the structure-from-motion module reconstructs static regions from depth and camera pose, while optical flow accounts for both static and dynamic regions. Crucially, we introduce a competitive collaboration mechanism: the motion segmentation network learns to separate regions where flow cannot be explained by depth and camera motion alone, and the other networks in turn adapt to focus on their respective domains, leading to more accurate and robust predictions. We evaluate our method on KITTI, Sintel, and Cityscapes, demonstrating state-of-the-art unsupervised depth and flow results while also producing high-quality motion segmentation without any labeled data. Our experiments show that learning these tasks jointly exploits their complementary geometric constraints, resulting in each task benefiting from the others. This work highlights the potential of unsupervised multi-task learning to solve low-level vision problems in complex dynamic scenes.

title: Immediate primary skin closure in type-III A and B open fractures: results after a minimum of five years
text_ai: Between June 1999 and May 2003 we undertook direct primary closure of the skin wounds of 173 patients with Gustilo and Anderson grade-IIIA and grade-IIIB open fractures. These patients were selected from a consecutive group of 557 with type-III injuries presenting during this time. All patients met strict inclusion criteria: a clean, non-crushed wound with minimal contamination, adequate soft-tissue coverage, and no evidence of gross infection at presentation. Exclusion criteria included segmental bone loss, vascular injury requiring repair, or extensive degloving. After aggressive debridement and copious irrigation, the skin was closed over a drain, with deep tissues left open in high-risk cases. No flap or skin graft was used acutely. Patients received intravenous antibiotics for 48 hours, followed by oral therapy for a total of five days. All fractures were stabilized using external fixation or intramedullary nailing according to fracture location and soft-tissue condition. At final follow-up (minimum 5 years; mean 7.2 years), the overall deep infection rate was 8.7% (15/173). For grade-IIIA fractures (n=112), the infection rate was 4.5%; for grade-IIIB (n=61), it was 18.0%. Nonunion occurred in 11.6% (20/173) and was associated with infection in 12 cases. Secondary procedures for bone grafting or soft-tissue coverage were required in 19.1%. Functional outcomes, assessed by the Lower Extremity Functional Scale, were satisfactory in 78% of patients. These results compare favorably with historical series reporting delayed closure or flap coverage, suggesting that immediate primary skin closure is safe and effective in selected grade-IIIA and IIIB open fractures, provided meticulous debridement and appropriate patient selection are employed.
prefix: Between June 1999 and May 2003 we undertook direct primary closure of the skin wounds of 173 patients with Gustilo and Anderson grade-IIIA and grade-IIIB open fractures. These patients were selected from a consecutive group of 557 with type-III injuries presenting during this time.

title: Block-MDS QC-LDPC Codes for Information Reconciliation in Key Distribution
text_ai: Quantum key distribution (QKD) is a popular protocol that provides information theoretically secure keys to multiple parties. Two important post-processing steps of QKD are 1) the information reconciliation (IR) step, where parties reconcile mismatches in generated keys through classical communication, and 2) the privacy amplification (PA) step, where parties distill their common key into a new secure key that the adversary has little to no information about. In practical QKD systems, the IR step must operate efficiently under high quantum bit error rates while minimizing the leaked information. Traditional low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes offer near-capacity performance but often require long block lengths and high-complexity decoding. This paper proposes block maximum distance separable (MDS) quasi-cyclic (QC) LDPC codes tailored for IR. By combining the algebraic structure of MDS codes with the iterative decoding advantage of LDPC codes, the proposed construction achieves high error correction capability with moderate block lengths and low encoding/decoding complexity. We demonstrate through simulations that these codes outperform standard irregular LDPC codes for a range of QKD channel conditions, reducing the frame error rate and the amount of disclosed parity information. The results indicate that block-MDS QC-LDPC codes constitute a promising candidate for efficient and secure IR in both discrete-variable and continuous-variable QKD systems.
prefix: Quantum key distribution (QKD) is a popular protocol that provides information theoretically secure keys to multiple parties. Two important post-processing steps of QKD are 1) the information reconciliation (IR) step, where parties reconcile mismatches in generated keys through classical communication, and 2) the privacy amplification (PA) step, where parties distill their common key into a new secure key that the adversary has little to no information about.

title: Single-domain chemical, thermochemical and thermal remanences in a basaltic rock
text_ai: Tiny basaltic samples containing finely grained titanomagnetite with Curie temperature less than 100 C were heated in air in weak field (25 to 100microT) at temperatures between 400 and 560 C for times as long as 32 hours. The resulting remanence acquisition was tracked via progressive isothermal and alternating-field demagnetization, revealing three distinct magnetic components. A low-coercivity, low-unblocking-temperature fraction, attributed to primary titanomagnetite, was progressively replaced by a higher-coercivity, higher-unblocking-temperature fraction coinciding with oxidation to titanohematite. The first component is a chemical remanent magnetization (CRM) acquired during the early stages of oxidation, where cation vacancies formed without significant lattice reorganization. The second, a thermochemical remanence (TCRM), developed as the oxidation front advanced and the newly formed phases stabilized at elevated temperature, yielding a remanence that partially overlaps with the thermal remanence (TRM) imparted upon cooling. The TRM itself dominated only in samples where the original titanomagnetite survived without substantial alteration. Hysteresis parameters and first-order reversal curve (FORC) diagrams confirmed that all remanence carriers remained in the single-domain size range throughout the experiment. The CRM, TCRM, and TRM showed distinct directional and intensity dependencies on heating duration, field strength, and temperature, with the TCRM exhibiting the highest stability against alternating-field demagnetization. These observations clarify the relative contributions of each remanence type in moderately oxidized basalts, with implications for paleointensity determinations and the interpretation of magnetization in slowly cooled volcanic rocks.

title: Accuracy of model-based tracking of knee kinematics and cartilage contact measured by dynamic volumetric MRI
text_ai: The purpose of this study was to determine the accuracy of knee kinematics and cartilage contact measured by volumetric dynamic MRI. A motor-actuated phantom drove femoral and tibial bone segments through cyclic 3D motion patterns. Volumetric images were continuously acquired using a 3D radially undersampled cine spoiled gradient echo sequence (SPGR-VIPR). The phantom’s motion was controlled by an electrodynamic actuator, with ground-truth kinematics derived from optical tracking of fiducial markers embedded in the bone segments. Dynamic volumetric images were reconstructed at 10 cardiac phases per cycle, and model-based tracking employed a point-to-surface registration algorithm that minimized distances between segmented bone surfaces and a subject-specific model. Contact areas were extracted via proximity analysis between the registered femoral and tibial cartilage surfaces. Accuracy was assessed by comparing tracked kinematics and contact metrics against simultaneously acquired optical data. For kinematics, root-mean-square errors averaged 0.8 mm for translations and 1.2° for rotations across all motion components. Cartilage contact measures—including centroid position, peak pressure location, and total contact area—agreed with ground truth within 1.1 mm and 6% of the area, respectively. Errors were larger at extreme flexion angles and during rapid motion phases, likely due to image blurring and residual undersampling artifacts. These results demonstrate that the proposed approach yields sub-millimeter and sub-degree accuracy in tracking knee kinematics, with sufficient precision to resolve spatially localized cartilage contact patterns from dynamic volumetric MRI. The validated methodology supports future in vivo studies of normative and pathological joint mechanics under physiological loading conditions.

title: 4G 5G Cell-level Multi-indicator Forecasting based on Dense-MLP
text_ai: With the development of 4G/5G, the rapid growth of traffic has caused a large number of cell indicators to exceed the warning threshold, and network quality has deteriorated. It is necessary for operators to solve the congestion in advance and effectively to guarantee the quality of user experience. To address this, we propose a cell-level multi-indicator forecasting framework based on a Dense-MLP architecture. The model jointly predicts multiple key performance indicators—such as resource utilization, traffic volume, and connection count—by leveraging dense connections that capture both cross-indicator correlations and temporal dynamics. Evaluated on real-world 4G/5G datasets, our approach achieves superior accuracy over traditional ARIMA, LSTM, and gradient boosting baselines, with mean absolute percentage errors reduced by 15–25% across indicators. Moreover, the dense connectivity enables efficient training and inference, making it suitable for large-scale deployment. By providing reliable early warnings of threshold violations, the framework empowers operators to proactively trigger load-balancing or capacity expansion, thereby preempting congestion and preserving user experience. This work demonstrates the practical effectiveness of dense neural architectures for operational network analytics.

title: Thinking Assistants: LLM-Based Conversational Assistants that Help Users Think By Asking rather than Answering
text_ai: Many AI systems focus solely on providing solutions or explaining outcomes. However, complex tasks like research and strategic thinking often benefit from a more comprehensive approach to augmenting the thinking process rather than passively getting information. This paper introduces Thinking Assistants: conversational agents built on large language models (LLMs) that primarily elicit user reasoning through targeted questions rather than providing direct answers. Drawing on cognitive scaffolding and Socratic dialogue principles, we design a system that poses iterative, open-ended queries to guide users through problem decomposition, assumption testing, and alternative perspective generation. Unlike conventional Q&A chatbots that prioritize answer accuracy and conciseness, Thinking Assistants intentionally withhold solutions to foster deeper cognitive engagement. We implement a prototype using GPT-4 with a prompt-chaining architecture that dynamically selects questioning strategies (e.g., elaboration, counterfactual, or critical reflection) based on dialogue state and user goal complexity. In a within-subjects study (N=48) comparing our system against a standard LLM assistant for complex analytical tasks (strategic planning, research synthesis), participants using Thinking Assistants reported significantly higher perceived insight (d=0.72) and produced more diverse arguments in their written analyses (d=0.64). Qualitative analysis of interaction logs reveals that users engaged in more extended reasoning chains and self-corrected errors more frequently. However, some users found the questioning style frustrating when under time pressure. We discuss trade-offs between cognitive support and user satisfaction, and propose design implications for domain-adaptive question generation. This work contributes to a growing paradigm of AI systems that augment human thinking by provoking, not providing.

title: Harnessing TH9 cells in cancer immunotherapy.
text_ai: CD4 T cell effector subsets not only profoundly affect cancer progression, but recent evidence also underscores their critical contribution to the anticancer efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors. In 2012, the two seminal studies suggested the superior antimelanoma activity of T H 9 cells over other T cell subsets upon adoptive T cell transfer. However, the translational potential of TH9 cells remains underexplored due to limited understanding of their induction, stability, and functional plasticity within the tumor microenvironment. TH9 cells are characterized by secretion of interleukin-9 (IL-9) and require specific cytokine milieus—notably TGF-β and IL-4—for differentiation. Emerging studies highlight their pleiotropic roles: they can promote antitumor responses by activating mast cells, dendritic cells, and cytotoxic T lymphocytes, yet also exhibit pro-tumorigenic effects in certain contexts. Key challenges include harnessing their effector functions while mitigating exhaustion and conversion to other subsets such as TH2 or TH17 cells. This review synthesizes current knowledge on TH9 biology in cancer, discusses strategies for augmenting their persistence and activity in vivo—including combination with checkpoint blockade or cytokine engineering—and outlines critical gaps for future research to unlock their full immunotherapeutic potential.

title: Lifetime of the superconductive state in short and long Josephson junctions
text_ai: We study the transient statistical properties of short and long Josephson junctions under the influence of thermal and correlated fluctuations. In particular, we investigate the lifetime of the superconductive metastable state finding the presence of noise induced phenomena. We employ a combination of analytic methods (including Langer's theory of metastable decay and the Fokker–Planck equation) and stochastic numerical simulations to compute the mean lifetime as a function of bias current, temperature, and noise correlation time. For short junctions, we observe a nonmonotonic dependence of the lifetime on the noise color, consistent with resonant activation effects. In long junctions, the decay proceeds via nucleation of fluxons; correlated fluctuations modify the nucleation rate and lead to a suppression or enhancement of the lifetime relative to the white‑noise case, depending on the spatial mode that dominates escape. We show that the interplay between junction length, noise correlation time, and damping strength produces a rich phase diagram of metastable lifetimes. Our results provide quantitative predictions for the design of superconducting circuits where noise‑induced switching is a limiting factor.

title: Optimized Treatment Schedules for Chronic Myeloid Leukemia
text_ai: Over the past decade, several targeted therapies (e.g. imatinib, dasatinib, nilotinib) have been developed to treat Chronic Myeloid Leukemia (CML). Despite an initial response to therapy, drug resistance remains a problem for some CML patients. To address this challenge, we propose a mathematical modeling framework that integrates pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic (PK-PD) dynamics of tyrosine kinase inhibitors with a stochastic model of BCR-ABL mutation emergence. By simulating long-term patient responses under various dosing regimens—including continuous daily therapy, intermittent high-dose pulses, and adaptive schedules triggered by molecular monitoring—we identify strategies that minimize the probability of resistance while maintaining deep molecular responses. Our results demonstrate that intermittent schedules, particularly those incorporating drug-free intervals, can suppress the outgrowth of resistant clones by exploiting fitness costs associated with resistance mutations. Furthermore, we show that adaptive dosing, which increases intensity upon detection of rising BCR-ABL transcripts, significantly delays or prevents relapse compared to fixed regimens. Sensitivity analyses reveal that optimal schedules depend critically on mutation fitness and drug half-life, suggesting a need for personalized approaches. These findings provide a mechanistic rationale for clinical trials evaluating alternative dosing strategies in CML and underscore the potential of optimized scheduling to extend durable remission in patients at risk of resistance.

title: Robust Contact State Estimation in Humanoid Walking Gaits
text_ai: In this article, we propose a deep learning framework that provides a unified approach to the problem of leg contact detection in humanoid robot walking gaits. Our formulation accomplishes to accurately and robustly estimate the contact state probability for each leg (i.e., stable or slip/no contact). We employ a temporal convolutional network that fuses proprioceptive and inertial measurements to capture the dynamical patterns of humanoid walking. Using a dataset of both simulated and real trajectories annotated with ground-truth contact states, the model learns to robustly discriminate between stable contact, slip, and no contact. On comprehensive benchmarks, our method achieves a 97% F1 score and reduces false positives by 85% compared to standard threshold-based approaches. The estimator generalizes over varying gait speeds, terrains, and sensor noise levels without requiring manual calibration. It runs at over 1 kHz on the robot's embedded computer, enabling real-time deployment. These results demonstrate that our deep learning framework offers a unified, accurate, and robust solution for contact state estimation in humanoid locomotion.

Our formulation accomplishes to accurately and robustly estimate the contact state probability for each leg (i.e., stable or slip/no contact).

title: Window-based Model Averaging Improves Generalization in Heterogeneous Federated Learning
text_ai: Federated Learning (FL) aims to learn a global model from distributed users while protecting their privacy. However, when data are distributed heterogeneously the learning process becomes noisy, unstable, and biased towards the last seen clients' data, slowing down convergence. To address these issues and improve the robustness and generalization capabilities of the global model, we propose WIMA (Window-based Model Averaging). WIMA maintains a sliding window of recent global model snapshots and computes a weighted average to generate a smoothed update. This dampens the effect of extreme client shifts and reduces bias from the last-seen client, promoting stable convergence. We derive a theoretical convergence bound that demonstrates improved optimization error under heterogeneous conditions. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, and FEMNIST with varying non-i.i.d. distributions show that WIMA consistently outperforms FedAvg, FedProx, and SCAFFOLD, achieving up to 5% higher test accuracy and reducing communication rounds by over 30%, thereby enhancing generalization and robustness in heterogeneous FL.

title: Strategic Play By Resource-Bounded Agents in Security Games
text_ai: Many studies have shown that humans are "predictably irrational": they do not act in a fully rational way, but their deviations from rational behavior are quite systematic. Our goal is to see the extent to which we can explain and justify these deviations as the outcome of rational but resource-bounded agents doing as well as they can, given their limitations. We focus on security games, a canonical domain in which human decision-making has been extensively studied and where systematic deviations from Nash equilibrium play are well documented. We model each human participant as a resource‑bounded agent who, rather than computing an exact Stackelberg strategy, employs a heuristic search over a limited set of possible responses, subject to cognitive constraints such as finite working memory and limited processing time. Within this framework, we derive predictions about the patterns of play that such agents would exhibit, and we compare these theoretical predictions against the behavioral data from several benchmark security‑game experiments. Our analysis shows that many of the observed “irrational” choices—such as over‑responding to low‑probability threats or failing to maximize expected utility when the optimal strategy is complex—are naturally produced by our bounded‑rationality model. Moreover, the model explains heterogeneity across individuals by allowing different levels of cognitive capacity, and it accounts for previously puzzling phenomena like the frequent choice of dominated strategies. We conclude that a substantial portion of human play in security games can be understood as optimal behavior relative to the agents’ computational limitations, rather than as simple errors or biases. These findings suggest that incorporating resource‑bounded rationality into security game models can improve both the accuracy of behavioral predictions and the design of effective defender strategies.

title: Catalyzing Social Interactions in Mixed Reality using ML Recommendation Systems
text_ai: We create an innovative mixed reality-first social recommendation model, utilizing features uniquely collected through mixed reality (MR) systems to promote social interaction, such as gaze recognition, proximity, noise level, congestion level, and conversational intensity. We further extend these models to include right-time features to deliver timely notifications. By integrating these real-time contextual signals into a graph-based recommendation architecture, our model dynamically suggests potential interaction partners in shared MR spaces. We evaluate the system through a user study (N=48) in a simulated social venue, comparing against a baseline recommendation without MR-specific features. Results indicate a 34% increase in initiated conversations and a 28% improvement in perceived social comfort. The inclusion of right-time triggers further reduces notification fatigue by 41%, balancing serendipity with user agency. We discuss implications for designing socially aware MR environments and highlight ethical considerations around gaze and proximity data. This work demonstrates that ML-driven, context-aware recommendations can meaningfully catalyze organic social interactions in mixed reality without overwhelming users.

title: Effect of 5% transdermal lidocaine patches on postoperative analgesia in dogs undergoing hemilaminectomy.
text_ai: To investigate the effect of 5% lidocaine patches on postoperative analgesia in dogs undergoing hemilaminectomy. Client-owned dogs undergoing hemilaminectomy for a single acute intervertebral thoracolumbar disc extrusion were enrolled in this prospective, randomised, blinded clinical trial. Following methadone administration, anaesthesia was induced with propofol, and maintained with isoflurane in oxygen and fentanyl infusion, in both groups. Dogs were randomly allocated to receive either a 5% lidocaine patch (Lido group) or an identical placebo patch (Control group) applied to the shaved dorsolateral thoracolumbar region immediately before extubation. Postoperative pain was assessed using the short-form Glasgow Composite Measure Pain Scale (CMPS-SF) and a numeric rating scale by a single blinded observer at 0, 2, 4, 6, 8, 12, and 24 h after extubation. Rescue analgesia with methadone (0.2 mg/kg IV) was administered when CMPS-SF score ≥ 5 or numeric rating scale ≥ 3. Time to first rescue analgesia, total methadone consumption, and adverse effects were recorded. Differences between groups were analysed with appropriate parametric or non-parametric tests at α = 0.05. Twenty-eight dogs completed the study (14 per group). The Lido group had significantly lower pain scores at 2, 4, and 6 h post-extubation (P < 0.05) and required fewer rescue analgesic interventions compared with the Control group. Median time to first rescue analgesia was longer in the Lido group (8 h; range 6–12 h) than in the Control group (4 h; range 2–6 h) (P = 0.003). Total methadone consumption over 24 h was significantly lower in the Lido group. No local or systemic adverse effects attributable to the lidocaine patch were observed. These results suggest that perioperative application of 5% transdermal lidocaine patches provides effective and safe adjunctive analgesia for the first 6–8 h after hemilaminectomy in dogs, reducing the need for injectable opioids.

title: Carleman-lattice-Boltzmann quantum circuit with matrix access oracles
text_ai: We apply Carleman linearization of the Lattice Boltzmann (CLB) representation of fluid flows to quantum emulate the dynamics of a 2D Kolmogorov-like flow. We assess the accuracy of the result and find a relative error of the order of $10^{-3}$ with just two Carleman iterates, for a range of the Reynolds number up to a few hundreds. The quantum circuit is constructed by representing the Carleman-linearized system through sparse matrix access oracles, which encode the linearized governing equations into a unitary operator amenable to fault-tolerant quantum simulation. We analyze the resource requirements and show that the number of qubits and gate count scale polynomially with lattice size and Carleman order, suggesting a pathway toward quantum advantage for moderate Reynolds numbers and beyond. Numerical experiments confirm that the emulated quantum dynamics match the classical CLB solution within the assessed error bounds, and the method remains stable for Reynolds numbers up to a few hundred without requiring high-order truncation. This work thus demonstrates that combining Carleman linearization with lattice Boltzmann discretization and matrix access oracles yields a viable quantum algorithm for simulating fluid flows, bridging classical fluid mechanics with practical quantum computation.

title: Periodontal status correlates with anti-citrullinated protein antibodies in first-degree relatives of individuals with rheumatoid arthritis.
text_ai: To evaluate periodontal status in first-degree relatives of patients with rheumatoid arthritis (FDR-RA) and detect correlation with the presence of anti-citrullinated protein antibodies (ACPAs). Rheumatologic status and periodontal status were evaluated in a nested case-control study of FDR-RA with no diagnosis of RA at enrolment. Periodontal examination included full-mouth probing depth, clinical attachment loss, bleeding on probing, and plaque index. Serum samples were analyzed for ACPA (anti-CCP2) and rheumatoid factor. ACPA positivity was defined as >20 IU/mL. Periodontitis was classified according to the CDC/AAP definition (moderate or severe). Among 212 FDR-RA (mean age 45.6 years, 72% female), 38% had periodontitis and 12% were ACPA-positive. Those with periodontitis exhibited significantly higher median ACPA levels (18.4 vs. 9.2 IU/mL, P=0.003) and greater frequency of ACPA positivity (22% vs. 6%, P<0.001) compared with periodontally healthy individuals. In multivariable logistic regression adjusting for age, sex, smoking, body mass index, and shared epitope status, moderate-to-severe periodontitis remained independently associated with ACPA positivity (OR 3.14, 95% CI 1.42–6.94). Among ACPA-positive FDR-RA, periodontal severity (mean clinical attachment loss) positively correlated with ACPA titers (Spearman r=0.41, P=0.02). These findings demonstrate a significant association between periodontal disease and ACPA presence in FDR-RA, supporting the hypothesis that periodontal inflammation may promote citrullination and autoantibody generation in the pre-clinical phase of RA. Periodontal evaluation may help identify at-risk individuals for RA prevention strategies.

title: Skew Class-balanced Re-weighting for Unbiased Scene Graph Generation
text_ai: An unbiased scene graph generation (SGG) algorithm referred to as Skew Class-balanced Re-weighting (SCR) is proposed for considering the unbiased predicate prediction caused by the long-tailed distribution. The prior works focus mainly on alleviating the deteriorating performances of the minority predicate predictions, showing drastic dropping recall scores, i.e., losing the majority predicate performances. To address this, SCR introduces a novel re-weighting scheme that explicitly accounts for the skew in class distribution by assigning adaptive weights based on both class frequency and a skewness parameter. Unlike conventional re-balancing methods, SCR preserves majority predicate recall while elevating minority performance through a calibrated loss formulation that prevents over-suppression of frequent classes. Experiments on VG and GQA datasets demonstrate that SCR achieves state-of-the-art trade-offs, improving mean recall by up to 8% without degrading recall@100.

title: NICE^k Metrics: Unified and Multidimensional Framework for Evaluating Deterministic Solar Forecasting Accuracy
text_ai: Accurate solar energy output prediction is key for integrating renewables into grids, maintaining stability, and improving energy management. However, standard error metrics such as Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and Skill Scores (SS) fail to capture the multidimensional nature of solar irradiance forecasting. We propose the NICE^k framework, a unified family of metrics that evaluates deterministic solar forecast accuracy across multiple dimensions: bias, amplitude, timing, variability, and ramp events. Each dimension is quantified by a normalized component, and the parameter k controls emphasis on large errors, allowing adaptation to specific grid needs like balancing reserves or dispatch. We show that traditional metrics such as RMSE and MAE are special cases of NICE^k under particular k choices, yet NICE^k provides richer diagnostic decomposition. Applying the framework to forecasts from three state-of-the-art models over four distinct climate zones reveals that conventional metrics often mask critical trade-offs: a model with low overall RMSE may exhibit poor ramp detection and systematic timing offsets, which the NICE^2 component clearly flags. The multidimensional NICE^k output thus enables targeted model improvement and informed selection for grid integration. This unified approach establishes a new and rigorous standard for evaluating deterministic solar forecasts, promoting transparency and comparability across diverse methods and climates.

title: First Light Curve Analysis of NSVS 8294044, V1023 Her, and V1397 Her Contact Binary Systems
text_ai: The first photometric light curve investigation of the NSVS 8294044, V1023 Her, and V1397 Her binary systems is presented. We used ground-based observations for the NSVS 8294044 system and Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) data for V1023 Her and V1397 Her. Photometric data were reduced using standard procedures, including bias subtraction, flat-field correction, and differential photometry. For NSVS 8294044, the ground-based light curves in the B, V, R, and I filters were obtained at the Xingming Observatory. TESS light curves for V1023 Her and V1397 Her were extracted from the full-frame images and corrected for systematics. All three systems exhibit typical EW-type light curves with nearly equal eclipse depths, indicating a contact configuration. We performed simultaneous light curve modeling using the Wilson–Devinney code, adopting a spot model where necessary to account for asymmetries. For NSVS 8294044, a fillout factor of 0.25 and a mass ratio of 0.48 were derived, classifying it as a W UMa binary of A subtype. V1023 Her shows a moderate fillout of 0.38 and a mass ratio of 0.52, with a slight O’Connell effect suggesting spot activity. V1397 Her is found to be a deep contact system (fillout ~0.55) with a mass ratio of 0.41, consistent with a W-type subclass. Absolute parameters were estimated using published Gaia distances, yielding masses, radii, and luminosities. The systems lie in the contact binary sequence with orbital periods between 0.33 and 0.41 days. Our results confirm all three as genuine contact binaries and provide the first reliable photometric solutions, contributing to the understanding of short-period eclipsing binaries in the low-mass regime.

title: Retrieval-augmented Image Captioning
text_ai: Inspired by retrieval-augmented language generation and pretrained Vision and Language (V&L) encoders, we present a new approach to image captioning that generates sentences given the input image and a set of captions retrieved from a datastore, as opposed to the image alone. Our model integrates a retrieval module that selects captions from a large pre-indexed datastore based on visual similarity to the input image. These retrieved captions are encoded by a pretrained V&L encoder and combined with image features via cross-attention in a transformer decoder. We train the entire pipeline end-to-end on standard captioning datasets. Experiments on COCO and Flickr30k demonstrate that retrieval-augmentation consistently improves both fluency and relevance, achieving new state-of-the-art results on multiple metrics. Ablations confirm that the benefit arises from effectively incorporating external linguistic knowledge, particularly for rare concepts and compositional descriptions. Furthermore, our approach generalizes to zero-shot settings by leveraging retrieval from external corpus, outperforming models that rely solely on image features.

title: Ball-Larus Path Profiling Across Multiple Loop iterations
text_ai: Identifying the hottest paths in the control flow graph of a routine can direct optimizations to portions of the code where most resources are consumed. This powerful methodology, called path profiling, was introduced by Ball and Larus in the mid 90s and has received considerable attention in the last 15 years for its practical relevance. However, the original Ball-Larus method profiles paths only within a single procedure invocation, treating each loop iteration as an independent path instance. This limitation prevents the detection of hot paths that extend across multiple iterations, which are prevalent in scientific and data-intensive applications. To address this, we propose an extension that enables path profiling across multiple loop iterations. Our approach modifies the path numbering and instrumentation to encode iteration count information, allowing the profiler to reconstruct paths that span loop boundaries. We prove that the overhead remains linear in the number of edges, comparable to the original scheme. Experimental evaluation on standard benchmarks demonstrates that our method identifies longer hot paths, leading to more effective compiler optimizations. Additionally, we show that the profiling overhead is acceptable for production use, and that the identified multi-iteration paths provide new optimization opportunities such as loop unrolling and software pipelining.

title: Studying the multi-wavelength signals from short GRBs
text_ai: Since the first host galaxies and afterglows of short GRBs were identified, they have remained very difficult to study: their multiwavelenth afterglows are notoriously faint and host galaxy identification often relies upon minimalising a chance alignment probability. In this work, we present a systematic multi-wavelength analysis of a carefully selected sample of short GRBs with identified host galaxies, leveraging archival data from Swift, Chandra, HST, and ground-based observatories. By employing a consistent forward modeling approach that accounts for jet structure, circumburst density profiles, and extinction, we reconstruct the broad-band afterglow spectra and light curves. Our analysis reveals that a significant fraction of short GRBs exhibit faint optical/NIR counterparts even at early times, while their X-ray and radio emissions often persist, enabling robust determination of the isotropic equivalent energy and the circumburst medium density. Furthermore, we investigate the relation between afterglow properties and host galaxy characteristics, such as stellar mass, star formation rate, and offset from the host center. We find evidence for two distinct populations: one consistent with compact binary merger environments in low-mass, passive galaxies, and another with more active hosts, suggesting a minority of events may arise from alternative progenitor channels. These results underscore the power of coordinated multi-wavelength campaigns in overcoming observational biases and advancing our understanding of short GRB physics and their cosmological context.

title: Optoelectronic Fingerprints of Interference between Different Charge Carriers in Graphene Superlattices and Analogies to Twisted Graphene Bilayers
text_ai: Motivated by recent experimental findings on the low-energy spectrum of Kekul\'e-patterned graphene, the optoelectronic signatures of graphene superlattices with a spatial modulation that triples the size of the unit cell and folds the valleys to the center of the Brillouin zone are studied. Using a tight-binding model and Kubo formalism, we compute the optical conductivity and identify distinct signatures of threefold-symmetric superlattices. These include anomalous Drude weight enhancements and pronounced infrared absorption peaks arising from valley-mixing interference between charge carriers. The results reveal a close analogy to twisted bilayer graphene, where moiré minibands similarly emerge from interlayer coupling. Specifically, the Kekulé-induced band folding replicates the low-energy band structure of small-angle twisted bilayers, leading to comparable optoelectronic responses such as van Hove singularities and selection-rule-driven spectral features. Our findings establish that the interference between different charge carriers—originating from intervalley scattering in superlattices or interlayer tunneling in twisted bilayers—manifests as universal optical fingerprints. This work bridges these two systems, offering experimental guidance for detecting such interference via optical spectroscopy and proposing a unified framework for understanding emergent phenomena in structurally modulated graphene.

title: Visual Analytics for Explainable and Trustworthy Artificial Intelligence
text_ai: Our society increasingly depends on intelligent systems to solve complex problems, ranging from recommender systems suggesting the next movie to watch to AI models assisting in medical diagnoses for hospitalized patients. With the iterative improvement of diagnostic accuracy and efficiency, AI holds significant potential to mitigate medical misdiagnoses by preventing numerous deaths and reducing an economic burden of approximately 450 EUR billion annually. However, the widespread adoption of these black-box models is hindered by their opaqueness, which undermines user trust and impedes domain experts from validating outputs, especially in high-stakes settings like healthcare. To address this challenge, visual analytics has emerged as a critical bridge between model performance and human understanding, enabling interactive exploration of model behavior, data distributions, and decision boundaries. In this paper, we present a visual analytics framework designed to enhance the explainability and trustworthiness of AI systems. Our approach integrates multiple explanation techniques—feature attribution, counterfactual reasoning, and surrogate models—within a coordinated multi-view interface that allows users to inspect predictions at both global and local levels. Through case studies using medical diagnosis datasets, we demonstrate how interactive visualizations help clinicians identify potential biases, verify model alignment with domain knowledge, and calibrate confidence in AI recommendations. Furthermore, we introduce novel visual encodings to represent uncertainty and decision robustness, thereby supporting nuanced trust assessment. The framework’s effectiveness is evaluated via a user study with medical professionals, revealing significant improvements in perceived transparency, trust calibration, and diagnostic agreement compared to baseline interfaces. Our findings underscore the pivotal role of visual analytics in bridging the gap between AI capability and human comprehension, paving the way for safer, more accountable deployment of intelligent systems in critical domains.

title: DiffPoint: Single and Multi-view Point Cloud Reconstruction with ViT Based Diffusion Model
text_ai: As the task of 2D-to-3D reconstruction has gained significant attention in various real-world scenarios, it becomes crucial to be able to generate high-quality point clouds. Despite the recent success of deep learning models in generating point clouds, there are still challenges in producing high-fidelity results due to the disparities between images and point clouds. To address these challenges, we propose DiffPoint, a novel diffusion-based framework that leverages a Vision Transformer (ViT) backbone for point cloud generation from single or multiple views. By embedding image features into a learnable latent space and conditioning the denoising process on view-specific representations, our model effectively bridges the modality gap while preserving fine-grained geometric details. The diffusion process is formulated as a stochastic iterative refinement that transforms random point sets into structured 3D coordinates, with a ViT encoder capturing long-range dependencies across both spatial and channel dimensions. For multi-view inputs, we introduce a cross-attention mechanism that aggregates features from arbitrary numbers of viewpoints, enabling robust reconstruction even under limited or occluded observations. Extensive experiments on ShapeNet and real-world datasets demonstrate that DiffPoint consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in terms of Chamfer distance and F-score, achieving high fidelity and diversity. Notably, our single-view reconstructions rival prior multi-view results, while multi-view settings yield further improvements in completeness and consistency. Ablation studies validate the effectiveness of the ViT backbone and the diffusion conditioning strategy, highlighting the potential of transformer-based generative models for 3D vision tasks.

title: Simulating Head Recovery and Intermittent Discharge in Free Flowing Wells.
text_ai: Modeling of the head recovery (buildup) in and intermittent operation of flowing wells lacks rigorous analytical tools. Presently different methods are applied in discharging and recovery phases. The presented reliable approximate solution considers a continuous free flow process and time variant screen loss parameters. A novel analytical framework is developed that unifies the transient behavior of both phases under a single set of governing equations, eliminating the need for separate models. The solution accounts for nonlinear well losses and time-dependent skin effects, which are often neglected in conventional approaches. Validation against numerical simulations and field data from multiple hydrogeological settings demonstrates high accuracy, with mean absolute errors below 3% for head recovery and 5% for discharge rates. Sensitivity analyses reveal that screen loss parameters critically influence the duration of the recovery period and the magnitude of intermittent flow peaks. The model also provides explicit criteria for identifying when intermittent operation can maintain sustainable yield without excessive drawdown. Practical applications include optimizing pumping schedules and designing wellfield management strategies in fractured and unconfined aquifers. This work bridges a gap in analytical well hydraulics by offering a computationally efficient alternative to full numerical modeling, suitable for real-time operational decision-making. The approach is extendable to multi-well interference scenarios and variable-rate sequences.

title: Image Fusion Transformer
text_ai: In image fusion, images obtained from different sensors are fused to generate a single image with enhanced information. In recent years, state-of-the-art methods have adopted Convolution Neural Networks (CNNs) to encode meaningful features for image fusion. Specifically, CNN-based methods perform image fusion by fusing local features. However, CNNs are inherently limited by their local receptive fields, which restricts their ability to capture long-range dependencies and global contextual information that are critical for tasks such as multi-modal image fusion, where complementary structures appear across spatially distant regions. To address this limitation, we propose the Image Fusion Transformer (IFT), a novel end-to-end architecture that leverages a transformer encoder to model both local and global feature interactions. Unlike conventional CNN-based fusion strategies, IFT employs a hierarchical patch embedding scheme to partition input images into non-overlapping patches, which are then linearly projected into token sequences. These tokens are processed by a stack of transformer layers with multi-head self-attention, enabling the network to learn spatially aware relationships and adaptively weight features from each sensor based on their contextual relevance. Furthermore, we introduce a cross-modal fusion module that fuses the tokenized representations using a learned attention mask, ensuring that salient information from each modality is preserved while suppressing redundant or conflicting signals. Extensive experiments on publicly available datasets for infrared–visible, multi-focus, and medical image fusion demonstrate that IFT outperforms state-of-the-art CNN-based methods across multiple metrics, including mutual information, gradient-based fusion quality, and visual perception. The results confirm that transformer-based global reasoning significantly enhances fusion performance, particularly in scenarios with large misalignments or low contrast.

title: Effective Hamiltonian of topologically stabilized polymer states
text_ai: Topologically stabilized polymer conformations observed in melts of nonconcatenated polymer rings and crumpled globules, are considered to be a good candidate for the description of the spatial structure of mitotic chromosomes. Despite significant efforts, the microscopic Hamiltonian capable of describing such systems, remains yet inaccessible. Here, we derive such a Hamiltonian using a field-theoretic coarse-graining that incorporates topological constraints via a Gaussian linking number potential. The resulting effective free energy contains a term proportional to the square of the local linking density, which penalizes entanglements. We validate the model through Monte Carlo simulations of melts of rings and crumpled globules, finding excellent agreement with known scaling laws: R_g ~ N^{1/3} for rings and the characteristic spatial correlations of fractal globules. Furthermore, the Hamiltonian predicts a first-order topological transition upon varying compaction, relevant to chromosome condensation during mitosis. We also demonstrate that the effective Hamiltonian can be mapped onto a model of interacting loops, providing a direct link to Hi-C data. Our approach provides a first-principles microscopic foundation for topologically stabilized polymer states and opens the door to quantitative predictions for chromosome organization.

title: Symplectic structure of post-Newtonian Hamiltonian for spinning compact binaries
text_ai: The phase space of a Hamiltonian system is symplectic. However, the post-Newtonian Hamiltonian formulation of spinning compact binaries in existing publications does not have this property, when position, momentum and spin variables $[X, P, S_1, S_2]$ compose its phase space. This non-symplecticity arises because the spin variables do not satisfy standard Poisson brackets, violating the Jacobi identity and causing non-conservation of phase space volume. We restore symplecticity via an explicit canonical transformation that linearizes the spin brackets, preserving the physical content. With these canonical variables, we derive a Hamiltonian accurate to third post-Newtonian order, including spin-orbit and spin-spin interactions. The resulting equations of motion exactly preserve the symplectic form, ensuring geometric consistency. Numerical tests confirm no secular drift in energy or angular momentum over billions of orbital cycles, demonstrating the robustness of the formulation. This symplectic Hamiltonian enables the use of symplectic integrators for long-term simulations, which is essential for gravitational wave data analysis where accurate waveforms over many cycles are required. Additionally, the approach eliminates the need for non-canonical spin supplementary conditions, as the canonical variables automatically satisfy the correct algebra. Our work provides a rigorous foundation for studying the conservative dynamics of spinning compact binaries within a symplectic framework, bridging the gap between post-Newtonian theory and Hamiltonian geometry.

title: CUNet: A Compact Unsupervised Network for Image Classification
text_ai: In this paper, we propose a compact network called CUNet (compact unsupervised network) to counter the image classification challenge. Different from the traditional convolutional neural networks learning filters by the time-consuming stochastic gradient descent, CUNet learns the filter bank from diverse image patches with the simple K-means, which significantly avoids the requirement of scarce labeled training images, reduces the training consumption, and maintains the high discriminative ability. Subsequently, the learned filters are convolved with the input images to generate rich feature maps, which are then pooled and encoded into compact representations via a codebook. These representations are fed into a linear classifier, achieving state-of-the-art performance on several benchmark datasets while requiring only a fraction of the parameters and training time of existing deep models. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CUNet not only rivals but often surpasses fully supervised networks, particularly in low-data regimes, validating its effectiveness for practical image classification tasks.

title: Randomized Oversampling for Generalized Multiscale Finite Element Methods
text_ai: In this paper, we study the development of efficient multiscale methods for flows in heterogeneous media. Our approach uses the Generalized Multiscale Finite Element (GMsFEM) framework. The main idea of GMsFEM is to approximate the solution space locally using a few multiscale basis functions. Although effective, the construction of accurate multiscale basis functions traditionally requires solving local eigenvalue problems on each coarse neighborhood. This step becomes computationally demanding when numerous realizations or parameters are involved. To address this, we propose a randomized oversampling strategy that reduces the computational cost without sacrificing accuracy. The key idea is to employ randomized sampling of oversampled domains to generate a set of candidate multiscale basis functions, from which a smaller set is selected via a spectral decomposition. This randomized approach significantly reduces the offline cost compared to deterministic oversampling techniques. We analyze the theoretical properties of the resulting method, showing that the approximation error decays rapidly with the number of basis functions. Numerical experiments for flows in highly heterogeneous media confirm that the proposed method achieves comparable accuracy to standard GMsFEM while requiring substantially less computational effort. Moreover, the method is well-suited for uncertainty quantification and multi-query scenarios where many simulations are needed.

The main idea of GMsFEM is to approximate the solution space locally using a few multiscale basis functions.

title: Probing the near-IR flux excess in young star clusters
text_ai: We report the results of a recent study of young star clusters (YSCs) in luminous blue compact galaxies (BCGs). The age distributions of the YSCs suggest that the starburst episode in Haro 11, ESO 185-IG13, and Mrk 930 started not more than 30-40 Myr ago. We combine near-IR photometry from the Hubble Space Telescope (HST) and ground-based spectroscopy to characterize the spectral energy distributions (SEDs) of these YSCs. A significant fraction exhibit a near-IR flux excess relative to simple stellar population (SSP) predictions for their optical ages, with amplitudes up to 0.5 mag at 1.6 μm. This excess is most pronounced in clusters with ages between 5 and 15 Myr, consistent with the emergence of red supergiants (RSGs) and luminous asymptotic giant branch (AGB) stars. Comparing with evolutionary synthesis models that include extended AGB phases and variable RSG lifetimes, we find that the observed excess requires either enhanced carbon star formation or a modified initial mass function (IMF) slope toward the high-mass end. Alternative scenarios, such as nebular continuum emission from photoionized gas or the presence of embedded massive young stellar objects, are ruled out by the lack of corresponding mid-IR excess and the absence of strong emission lines. Our results imply that standard SSP models systematically underestimate the near-IR flux of YSC populations during the crucial phase when feedback from massive stars shapes the interstellar medium. This bias directly affects derived star formation rates and mass estimates when using near-IR tracers, particularly in compact starburst environments like BCGs.

title: COUNTDOWN: a Run-time Library for Performance-Neutral Energy Saving in MPI Applications
text_ai: Power and energy consumption is becoming key challenges to deploy the first exascale supercomputer successfully. Large-scale HPC applications waste a significant amount of power in communication and synchronization-related idle times. However, due to the time scale at which communication happens, transitioning in low power states during communication's idle times may introduce unacceptable overhead in applications' execution time. This paper introduces COUNTDOWN, a run-time library that transparently reduces energy consumption of MPI applications without degrading performance. COUNTDOWN leverages a lightweight online predictor to estimate the duration of idle periods within MPI calls—such as those occurring during blocking receives, barriers, or collective operations—and dynamically selects the most appropriate low-power state (e.g., C-states or P-states) for the CPU only when the predicted idle time exceeds the state-transition overhead. To minimize interference, the library employs a deferred-activation strategy that triggers power state changes asynchronously, and it monitors actual idle times to adapt its prediction model on-the-fly. We evaluate COUNTDOWN on a production cluster using a suite of real-world HPC benchmarks and applications. Results show that COUNTDOWN achieves average energy savings of 12–18% on communication-heavy kernels, and up to 28% on full-scale scientific codes, while keeping execution time overhead below 1% in all tested configurations. Importantly, the library requires no source-code modifications and is fully compatible with standard MPI implementations. These findings demonstrate that performance-neutral energy savings are feasible even at the very short idle timescales characteristic of modern HPC communication, providing a practical path toward more efficient exascale systems.

title: Analysis of a Memcapacitor-Based for Neural Network Accelerator Framework
text_ai: Data-intensive computing tasks, such as training neural networks, are crucial for artificial intelligence applications but often come with high energy demands. One promising solution is to develop specialized hardware that directly maps neural networks, utilizing arrays of memristive devices to perform parallel multiply-accumulate operations. This work analyzes a memcapacitor-based neural network accelerator framework, leveraging the unique charge-controlled dynamics of memcapacitors to surpass limitations inherent in memristor-based designs. Unlike memristors, which suffer from write noise and leakage currents, memcapacitors store information via capacitance modulation, enabling near-zero static power consumption and improved state retention. The proposed framework models crossbar arrays of memcapacitive synapses, evaluating their accuracy in executing multiply-accumulate operations through SPICE simulations and system-level benchmarks. Key metrics considered include energy-delay product, area overhead, and robustness to device variations. Results demonstrate a 3.2× reduction in energy per operation compared to equivalent memristive accelerators, with comparable inference accuracy across standard datasets (MNIST, CIFAR-10). Furthermore, a hybrid training scheme is introduced that combines ex situ pretraining with in situ fine-tuning via charge injection, mitigating device mismatch. The analysis reveals that memcapacitor arrays offer a scalable, low-power alternative for analog neural network accelerators, particularly suited for edge deployments where energy constraints are critical. These findings establish a foundational assessment for future large-scale memcapacitive computing fabrics.

title: Modular Many-Body Quantum Sensors
text_ai: Quantum many-body systems undergoing phase transitions have been proposed as probes enabling beyond-classical enhancement of sensing precision. However, this enhancement is usually limited to a very narrow region around the critical point. Here, we systematically develop a modular approach for introducing multiple phase transitions in a many-body system. Each module is an independently tunable many-body system that can be operated near its own critical point. By engineering controllable couplings between modules, we create a composite sensor with multiple, distributed phase transitions. This modular design allows us to shape the sensor’s overall response, achieving high sensitivity over a broad parameter range rather than a single narrow region. We compute the quantum Fisher information and show that the modular architecture preserves enhancement even when individual modules are detuned from their critical points, effectively circumventing the fundamental limitation of single-critical-point sensors. Additionally, the scheme offers resilience against parameter inhomogeneities and decoherence. Our framework provides a scalable, robust route to practical many-body quantum sensors with tailored metrological capabilities.

title: Treatment of chronic nonunions of the humerus with free vascularized fibula transfer: a report of thirteen cases
text_ai: Chronic nonunions of the humerus remain a challenging problem. We reviewed 13 cases of chronic nonunion of the humerus resulting from trauma or osteomyelitis treated with vascularized fibula transfer after failure of conventional treatment. Patient averages were 35 years of age, follow-up of 19 months, and 4.2 prior operations. Union was achieved in 11 of 13 patients at an average of 4.5 months, with the two failures subsequently healing after additional bone grafting. One patient experienced a superficial wound infection that resolved with oral antibiotics; there were no deep infections, graft fractures, or vascular complications. At final follow-up, all patients demonstrated stable shoulders and elbows with functional range of motion, and pain scores decreased significantly from preoperative levels. Donor site morbidity was limited to transient ankle stiffness in one patient. These results indicate that free vascularized fibula transfer offers a reliable salvage option for recalcitrant humeral nonunions, achieving high union rates and satisfactory functional recovery despite multiple prior procedures.

title: The Milky Way atlas for linear filaments II. clump rotation versus filament orientation
text_ai: Dense clumps distributed along filaments are the immediate medium for star formation. Kinematic properties of the clumps, such as velocity gradient and angular momentum, combined with filament orientation, provide important clues to the formation mechanism of filament-clump configurations and the role of filaments in star formation. Here we present a systematic analysis of the relationship between clump rotation and filament orientation using the Milky Way atlas for linear filaments. From the catalog of 568 well-resolved filaments, we identify 1,231 dense clumps with reliable ^13CO (1–0) and C^18O (1–0) line data from the LAMA survey. For each clump, we derive velocity gradients via linear least-squares fitting of the centroid velocity field and compute the projected angular momentum orientation. Filament orientations are determined from their major axis position angles. We find that clump velocity gradients tend to be preferentially aligned perpendicular to the host filament’s long axis, with a mean offset of 78° ± 5°, and the alignment is strongest for the most massive clumps (M > 100 M⊙). This perpendicular alignment is consistent with a scenario where clumps form via gravitational fragmentation along filaments and subsequently acquire rotation through shear from the filament’s longitudinal flow. In contrast, clumps with more chaotic velocity fields show no preferred orientation. Our results imply that the filament-scale kinematic environment plays a decisive role in setting the angular momentum of dense cores, thereby influencing the initial conditions for star formation. The observed orientation rule provides a new observational constraint for numerical simulations of filament evolution and core formation.
