title: Reverberation and photoionization estimates of the Broad Line Region Radius in Low-z Quasars
text_ai: Black Hole Mass (M_BH) estimation in quasars, especially at high redshift, involves use of single epoch spectra with s/n and resolution that permit accurate measurement of the width of a broad line assumed to be a reliable virial estimator. Coupled with an estimate of the radius of the broad line region this yields M_BH. However, the accuracy of single-epoch M_BH estimates hinges on the adopted radius of the broad line region (R_BLR), which is usually inferred from an empirical relation between R_BLR and the optical continuum luminosity (R–L relation) calibrated through reverberation mapping of lower-redshift quasars. This relation may be sensitive to systematic effects such as Eddington ratio, source inclination, and the shape of the ionizing continuum, all of which can affect the ionization structure and dynamics of the broad line region. In this work, we present new reverberation mapping measurements of the Hβ line region radius for a sample of 23 low-redshift (z < 0.3) quasars, obtained from multi-epoch spectroscopic monitoring with typical s/n of 20–30 and spectral resolution of ~200 km s⁻¹. These direct reverberation radii are compared with estimates from photoionization models that use the observed broad line fluxes and a parameterized continuum to infer R_BLR. We find that reverberation and photoionization radii are consistent to within ~0.2 dex for the majority of sources, but a subset of quasars with high Eddington ratios (L/L_Edd > 0.3) show systematically larger photoionization radii by 0.3–0.5 dex relative to their reverberation values. This discrepancy suggests that single-epoch M_BH estimates relying on the standard R–L relation may be biased for the most actively accreting sources. We discuss the implications for black hole mass estimation at high redshift, where direct reverberation is not feasible, and recommend incorporating ionization parameter and continuum shape corrections when applying photoionization-based R_BLR prescriptions to improve the reliability of single-epoch virial mass estimates.

title: TeraHertz Band Communication: An Old Problem Revisited and Research Directions for the Next Decade
text_ai: Terahertz (THz) band communications are envisioned as a key technology for 6G and Beyond. As a fundamental wireless infrastructure, THz communication can boost abundant promising applications. In 2014, our team published two comprehensive roadmaps for the development and progress of THz communication networks [1], [2], which helped the research community to start research on this subject afterwards. Over the past decade, the field has witnessed remarkable progress, yet foundational challenges—such as ultra-massive MIMO design, reconfigurable intelligent surfaces, and energy-efficient transceivers—remain unresolved, often echoing issues identified in our earlier roadmaps. This paper first revisits these persistent “old” problems, critically reassessing their relevance in light of recent hardware advances and spectrum allocation developments. We then synthesize insights from over 200 papers published since 2020, identifying three emerging research thrusts: (i) joint communication and sensing at THz frequencies, (ii) machine learning-driven resource allocation for dynamic THz networks, and (iii) integration with higher-frequency bands (e.g., sub-THz and optical wireless). Furthermore, we outline a roadmap for the next decade, emphasizing the need for scalable testbeds, standardized channel models, and interdisciplinary collaboration between device physics and network theory. By connecting past obstacles to future opportunities, this paper aims to guide the community toward practical, high-impact THz systems that can meet 6G targets.

title: QCD against BlackHoles of Stellar Mass
text_ai: In course of the consolidation of nucleon (neutron) spacing inside a compact star, two key factors are expected to come into play side by side: the lack of self-stabilization against shutting into black hole (BH) and forthcoming phase transition - color deconfinement and QCD-vacuum reconstruction - within the nuclear matter the star is composed of. The interplay between these two processes is investigated within the framework of general relativity and lattice-QCD-informed equations of state. We demonstrate that color deconfinement, occurring at supranuclear densities, introduces a net repulsive contribution from the liberated quarks and gluons, while the associated vacuum reconstruction—characterized by a density-dependent bag constant—modifies the thermodynamic potential. The resulting equation of state exhibits a softening at the onset of deconfinement, followed by a stiffening at higher densities due to Fermi pressure in the quark phase and the reduction of the vacuum energy density. Using the Tolman–Oppenheimer–Volkoff equations, we compute mass–radius relations and find that the vacuum reconstruction can raise the maximum achievable mass by up to 25% compared to purely hadronic stars, provided the phase transition occurs at densities below the central density of the star. For stars whose central densities lie in the mixed-phase region, the interplay between the softening and subsequent stiffening creates a sequence of stable configurations, potentially allowing stellar-mass objects that evade direct collapse into a black hole. However, if the vacuum reconstruction is insufficiently pronounced—characterized by a small bag constant or a late onset of deconfinement—the lack of self-stabilization dominates, and the star collapses once the hadronic branch reaches its mass limit. We conclude that QCD vacuum reconstruction serves as a natural counterbalance to gravitational instability, defining a mass window within which stellar-mass black hole formation is suppressed in favor of hybrid quark–hadron stars. The existence of such a window offers a testable prediction for gravitational wave and electromagnetic observations of compact object mergers, and it suggests that the observed black hole mass gap may be partially attributed to QCD effects.

title: Quasi-Discrete Locally Compact Quantum Groups
text_ai: Consider a C*-algebra $A$ with a comultiplication $\Delta$. This pair is usually thought of as locally compact quantum semi-group. When these notes were written, in 1993, it was not at all clear what the extra assumptions on the comultiplication should be for this pair to be a 'locally compact quantum group'. Since then, the theory has developed profoundly. Kustermans and Vaes provided axioms—a left Haar weight and a unitary antipode—that characterize locally compact quantum groups, unifying compact and discrete cases and yielding a rich duality. Within this framework, we introduce quasi-discrete locally compact quantum groups. A locally compact quantum group (A, Δ) is quasi-discrete if its C*-algebra is type I and the comultiplication admits a direct integral decomposition into compact quantum groups. Equivalently, it is both amenable and co-amenable, or of Kac type. Quasi-discreteness is also characterized by a sufficiently large family of finite-dimensional unitary corepresentations spanning a dense *-subalgebra. This yields a faithful invariant state and a tractable representation theory based on irreducible corepresentations. Examples include the quantum group of a compact group and its Pontryagin dual, and quantum deformations of solvable Lie groups and their duals, illustrating the breadth of the class. We prove that the modular automorphism group is inner and the scaling constant trivial, so that the quantum group is of Kac type. Finally, we relate quasi-discrete quantum groups to classical locally compact groups, showing they correspond to those admitting a continuous field of finite-dimensional irreducible corepresentations. We also discuss applications to quantum-group actions on C*-algebras, where quasi-discreteness ensures a well-behaved crossed product construction. This establishes quasi-discrete quantum groups as a natural class amenable to analysis via classical methods.

title: Do people's user types change over time? An exploratory study
text_ai: In recent years, different studies have proposed and validated user models (e.g., Bartle, BrainHex, and Hexad) to represent the different user profiles in games and gamified settings. However, the results of applying these user models in practice (e.g., to personalize gamified systems) are still contradictory. One possible reason for this inconsistency is the assumption that user types remain stable over time—an assumption that has rarely been tested empirically. This exploratory study addresses that gap by examining the temporal stability of user types using the Hexad model. We conducted a longitudinal survey with 218 participants over a six-month period, measuring their gamer motivations at three time points using the validated Hexad User Types Scale. Our analysis assessed both intra-individual stability (via test–retest correlations and individual trajectory analysis) and inter-individual prevalence shifts (via repeated-measures ANOVAs). Results reveal a nuanced picture: while aggregate user type distributions remained largely stable across the study, individual-level trajectories showed considerable variability. Approximately one-third of participants changed their primary user type at least once, with socialiser and achiever types being the most fluid. Temporal factors such as recent game play frequency and life events partially predicted these shifts. These findings challenge the static application of user models in gamified systems and suggest that personalization should account for potential changes over time. We discuss implications for adaptive gamification design and propose directions for future longitudinal research on user modelling.

title: Does the Presence of Risk Factors for Fetal Growth Restriction Increase the Probability of Antenatal Detection? A French National Study.
text_ai: Screening for fetal growth restriction (FGR) is a major component of prenatal care. We investigated whether the presence of maternal and pregnancy risk factors for FGR improves the antenatal suspicion of FGR for infants born small-for-gestational age (SGA) as well as their impact on screening specificity. We conducted a nationwide retrospective cohort study using data from the French National Perinatal Survey and the National Health Data System. All singleton live births at ≥24 weeks’ gestation with a birthweight below the 10th percentile for gestational age (SGA) were included. Antenatal suspicion of FGR was defined as any mention of FGR in the medical records prior to delivery. Maternal and pregnancy risk factors were categorized according to international guidelines (e.g., smoking, preeclampsia, diabetes, maternal age, parity, and prior SGA). Multivariate logistic regression models were used to estimate the adjusted odds of antenatal detection, and receiver operating characteristic curves assessed screening performance. Overall, among 214 518 SGA infants, antenatal suspicion was recorded in only 34% of cases. The presence of one or more risk factors significantly increased detection (adjusted odds ratio 2.38, 95% CI 2.18–2.58). However, this improvement came at the cost of reduced specificity: among non-SGA infants (n=1 109 482), the false-positive rate rose from 4.1% (no risk factors) to 8.3% (≥2 risk factors). The positive predictive value remained low (≤15%) regardless of risk factor count. When risk factors were used alone as a screening test (i.e., any risk factor considered positive), sensitivity for SGA was 67% but specificity was only 54%. In contrast, when risk factors were combined with ultrasound biometric measurements, sensitivity increased to 51% with a specificity of 92%. These findings indicate that the presence of risk factors does enhance antenatal suspicion of FGR among SGA infants, but the effect is modest and accompanied by a substantial increase in false positives. Sole reliance on risk factors as a screening criterion would result in unnecessary investigations and parental anxiety. The poor predictive value underscores the need for improved first‑line screening methods, such as universal third‑trimester ultrasound, to achieve both acceptable sensitivity and high specificity. Our study provides population‑based evidence to inform future prenatal screening strategies in France and similar settings.

title: Reproductive Coercion Among African American Female Adolescents: Associations with Contraception and Sexually Transmitted Diseases.
text_ai: Background: Among adolescents, racial disparities in reproductive health outcomes persist. The question of whether reproductive coercion (RC) influences these outcomes has received increased attention. Little is known about whether RC is independently associated with contraceptive use and having a sexually transmitted disease (STD) among African American female adolescents. Methods: Data were drawn from a clinic-based sample of 456 African American female adolescents aged 14–19 years recruited from urban reproductive health clinics in Atlanta, Georgia, between 2018 and 2020. Participants completed a self-administered survey assessing lifetime exposure to reproductive coercion (e.g., birth control sabotage, pregnancy pressure, and condom manipulation), contraceptive use (categorized as none, inconsistent, or consistent use of effective contraception in the past three months), and self-reported history of sexually transmitted disease diagnosis in the prior year. Multivariable logistic regression models were estimated, controlling for age, socioeconomic status, relationship characteristics, and history of physical or sexual violence, to isolate the independent associations between RC and each outcome. Results: Over one-third of participants (37.5%) reported at least one form of reproductive coercion. After adjustment, RC was significantly associated with a 2.1-fold increased odds of inconsistent or no contraceptive use (AOR = 2.12, 95% CI: 1.47–3.06) and a 1.8-fold increased odds of having had an STD (AOR = 1.76, 95% CI: 1.21–2.56). These associations held when stratifying by partner type and relationship duration. Notably, RC involving pregnancy pressure showed the strongest link to both outcomes, whereas condom manipulation was more strongly tied to STD history specifically. Conclusions: Reproductive coercion is a prevalent and independent risk factor for suboptimal contraceptive use and STDs among African American female adolescents, even after accounting for other known correlates. These findings suggest that RC may exacerbate existing racial disparities in reproductive health by undermining young women’s ability to enact their contraceptive and preventive care preferences. Clinical screening for RC and trauma-informed interventions that address partner interference with reproductive autonomy may be essential components of comprehensive care for this population. Future research should explore longitudinal pathways and culturally tailored strategies to mitigate the impact of RC on adolescent reproductive health.

title: Depinning and flow of a vortex line in an uniaxial random medium
text_ai:
We study numerically and analytically the dynamics of a single directed elastic string driven through a 3-dimensional disordered medium. u= 1.33 \pm 0.02$, depinning exponent $ eta = 0.24\pm 0.01$, and avalanche-size exponent $	au_{\parallel} = 1.09 \pm 0.03$. These exponents satisfy the scaling relations expected for a directed elastic string, such as $
u = 1/(d-\zeta_\perp)$ and $ eta = 
u(z_{\parallel}-\zeta_{\parallel})$, with $d=3$ the embedding dimension. We measure the transverse roughness exponent $\zeta_\perp = 0.62 \pm 0.02$, consistent with the Flory prediction for a 3-dimensional medium, and verify the anisotropy relation $\zeta_{\parallel} = (1+\zeta_\perp)/2$ within error bars. The avalanche-size exponent in the transverse direction is $	au_\perp = 1.35 \pm 0.04$, and we find a universal scaling function relating avalanche duration and size, with a dynamic exponent $z_{\parallel}$ that controls the temporal correlations. Our analytical approach employs a functional renormalization group (FRG) treatment of the disorder correlator, which yields fixed-point values for the roughness exponents in excellent agreement with the numerics. The FRG predicts $\zeta_\perp = 2/3$ in the large-$d$ limit, and our finite-$d$ corrections are captured by a one-loop calculation. In the finite-velocity regime, the velocity-force curve follows $v \sim (F-F_c)^ eta$ over several decades, with $ eta$ matching the quasistatic value. At higher drives, the string crosses over to a regime dominated by the disorder strength, where the velocity increases linearly with force. We also analyze the spatiotemporal avalanche shapes: for a given duration $T$, the average avalanche size scales as $S \sim T^{1+\zeta_{\parallel}/z_{\parallel}}$, and the shape is parabolic, in agreement with predictions for directed percolation universality. Our results provide a comprehensive picture of depinning and flow for a single vortex line in a uniaxial random medium, unifying numerical and analytical perspectives and offering quantitative benchmarks for experiments on superconducting films.

In the quasistatic limit the string is super-rough in the driving direction, with roughness exponent $\zeta_{\parallel} = 1.25\pm 0.01$, dynamic exponent $z_{\parallel}= 1.43 \pm 0.01$, correlation-length exponent $\nu= 1.33 \pm 0.02$, depinning exponent $\beta = 0.24\pm 0.01$, and avalanche-size exponent $\tau_{\parallel} = 1.09 \pm 0.03$.

title: A Reinforcement Learning Approach to Parameter Selection for Distributed Optimal Power Flow
text_ai: With the increasing penetration of distributed energy resources, distributed optimization algorithms have attracted significant attention for power systems applications due to their potential for superior scalability, privacy, and robustness to a single point-of-failure. The Alternating Direction Method of Multipliers (ADMM) is a popular distributed optimization algorithm; however, its convergence performance is highly dependent on the selection of penalty parameters, which are usually chosen heuristically. This paper proposes a reinforcement learning (RL) framework to automatically and adaptively select penalty parameters for ADMM-based distributed optimal power flow (D-OPF). The parameter selection is formulated as a Markov decision process, where the state captures recent primal and dual residual trajectories, actions correspond to candidate parameter values, and the reward penalizes slow convergence or divergence. A deep Q-network agent is trained offline on representative load and generation scenarios to learn a policy that adjusts parameters in real time as the optimization progresses. The method is validated on several IEEE test systems, including the 118-bus and 300-bus cases, under various distributed network partitions. Results demonstrate that the RL-guided parameter selection consistently achieves faster convergence and lower iteration counts compared to heuristic fixed-parameter baselines, as well as state-of-the-art adaptive tuning rules. Moreover, the learned policy generalizes well to unseen operating conditions without retraining. This work provides a data-driven alternative to manual parameter tuning, enabling more robust and efficient deployment of ADMM for D-OPF in future power grids with high renewable penetration.

title: Visibility of current and shot noise in electrical Mach-Zehnder and Hanbury Brown Twiss interferometers
text_ai: We investigate the visibility of the current and shot-noise correlations of electrical analogs of the optical Mach-Zehnder interferometer and the Hanbury Brown Twiss interferometer. The electrical analogs are discussed in conductors subject to high magnetic fields where electron motion is along edge states. The transport quantities are modulated with the help of an Aharonov-Bohm flux. We analyze the visibility of the dc current and the zero-frequency shot noise power as functions of the Aharonov-Bohm flux and the applied bias voltage. Using a scattering matrix approach that accounts for energy-dependent transmission through the beam splitters and phase shifts along the edge channels, we compute the current and noise correlations in both interferometric geometries. For the Mach-Zehnder interferometer, we find that the visibility of the shot noise can significantly exceed that of the current, particularly when dephasing from finite bias or temperature averages out the current interference. This enhancement arises because noise correlations are sensitive to two-particle interference and are less affected by single-particle phase averaging. In the Hanbury Brown Twiss setup, we examine the cross-correlation visibility as a function of flux and find that it reflects the bunching or antibunching statistics of the electrons, depending on the beam splitter configuration and the presence of a voltage bias. Our results demonstrate that shot noise provides a robust probe of coherence and quantum statistics in edge-state interferometers, even when the current visibility is suppressed. We also discuss the role of finite frequency effects and the implications for experimental detection in high-field quantum Hall systems.

The electrical analogs are discussed in conductors subject to high magnetic fields where electron motion is along edge states. The transport quantities are modulated with the help of an Aharonov-Bohm flux.

title: Illustrating the Applicability of IRT to Implementation Science: Examining an Instrument of Therapist Attitudes.
text_ai: Pragmatic instruments with psychometric support are important to advance dissemination and implementation (D&I) research, but few well-researched D&I instruments exist. Item response theory (IRT), an approach that is underutilized in D&I, can help with the development of actionable and brief instruments. In this study, we demonstrate the utility of IRT by applying it to the Evidence-Based Practice Attitude Scale (EBPAS), a widely used measure of therapist attitudes toward adopting evidence-based practices. Using a large sample (N = 1,500) of mental health clinicians, we calibrated item parameters under the graded response model, evaluated item and scale functioning, and examined differential item functioning across professional disciplines. Results revealed that several EBPAS items provided limited information across the latent trait continuum, particularly at higher attitude levels, and that a subset of items exhibited moderate to strong discrimination. Iterative scale reduction based on IRT analyses yielded a brief, psychometrically robust 8-item version that maintained coverage of the original four subdomains while reducing respondent burden by over 50%. The revised instrument demonstrated improved precision and reliability, especially for distinguishing among clinicians with moderate to high openness to evidence-based practice. Findings underscore how IRT can inform the empirical refinement of implementation measures, producing actionable tools that are both brief and psychometrically sound. We discuss implications for accelerating D&I research and propose a framework for integrating IRT methods into future instrument development and validation efforts.

Item response theory (IRT), an approach that is underutilized in D&I, can help with the development of actionable and brief instruments.

title: Status of the Medium-Sized Telescopes for the Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory
text_ai: The Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO) is a next-generation ground-based gamma-ray observatory that will study the universe at very high energy using atmospheric Cherenkov light. CTAO will comprise over 67 telescopes of three different sizes, located in the northern and southern hemispheres. The medium-sized telescopes (MSTs) form the core of the CTAO array, bridging the energy range between the large and small telescopes with optimal sensitivity in the 100 GeV to 10 TeV band. Each MST employs a modified Davies-Cotton optical design with a 12 m diameter segmented mirror dish, focusing Cherenkov light onto a 2.4° field-of-view camera. The camera is based on silicon photomultipliers (SiPMs) for the northern site and photomultiplier tubes (PMTs) for the southern site, with an innovative trigger and readout system designed for high background rejection. Currently, the MST project has progressed from prototyping to serial production. The first two MSTs (MST-1 and MST-2) have been fully assembled and commissioned at the prototype site in Berlin-Adlershof, achieving first Cherenkov light in early 2023. These telescopes have undergone extensive performance verification, including pointing accuracy, mirror alignment, and camera calibration. Manufacturing of additional MST units is underway, with mirror panels, camera components, and mechanical structures being produced by international consortia. Key challenges addressed include cost-effective mass production of mirror facets achieving <80% reflectivity, environmental hardening for remote deployment at the Paranal and La Palma sites, and integration of the trigger systems with the array-wide central control. The current status indicates that the first northern MSTs will be installed at the Observatorio del Roque de los Muchachos in La Palma starting mid-2024, while southern MST deployment at Paranal is anticipated in 2025. These milestones bring the CTAO closer to its scientific goals, enabling deep surveys, transient studies, and multi-wavelength follow-up across the gamma-ray sky.

CTAO will comprise over 67 telescopes of three different sizes, located in the northern and southern hemispheres.

title: Distributed generalized Nash equilibria computation of monotone games via a preconditioned proximal point algorithm
text_ai: In this paper, we investigate distributed generalized Nash equilibrium (GNE) computation of monotone games with affine coupling constraints. Each player can only utilize its local objective function, local feasible set and a local block of the coupling constraint, and can only communicate with its neighbours. To this end, we propose a novel distributed algorithm based on a preconditioned proximal point method. The preconditioner is designed to exploit the structure of the affine coupling constraints, enabling the algorithm to achieve faster convergence while preserving the privacy of individual players’ data. Under the assumptions that the game is monotone and the coupling constraints satisfy a Slater condition, we establish that the iterates converge to a variational GNE. The analysis leverages a carefully constructed potential function that decreases monotonically along the algorithm’s trajectory. Furthermore, we show that the algorithm can be implemented in a fully distributed manner, where each player only needs to exchange a single dual variable with its neighbours. The communication burden is thus minimal and independent of the dimension of the primal variables. Numerical experiments on networked Cournot competition and energy market models illustrate the theoretical findings and demonstrate the efficiency of the preconditioned approach compared to standard distributed GNE algorithms. Notably, the preconditioner significantly reduces the number of iterations required, especially when the coupling constraints are ill-conditioned. These results extend the scope of proximal point methods to distributed noncooperative games with coupled constraints, offering a robust and scalable solution for large-scale multi-agent systems.

title: Artificial intelligence in government: Concepts, standards, and a unified framework
text_ai: Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), especially in generative language modelling, hold the promise of transforming government. Given the advanced capabilities of new AI systems, it is critical that these are embedded using standard operational procedures, clear epistemic criteria, and behave in alignment with the normative expectations of society. Building on these imperatives, we first map the conceptual landscape of AI in government, distinguishing between automation, augmentation, and autonomous decision-making. We then critically review existing standards—from technical interoperability to ethical governance—identifying gaps in the current patchwork of guidelines. To address fragmentation, we propose a unified framework that integrates operational, epistemic, and normative dimensions into a single coherent structure. The framework specifies a tiered system of oversight: real-time auditing of model outputs, formal verification of reasoning chains, and periodic reassessment against societal values such as fairness, transparency, and accountability. We demonstrate the framework’s applicability through three illustrative use cases—benefits allocation, regulatory enforcement, and public service chatbots—showing how each layer interacts with specific AI capabilities. The paper concludes by outlining a research agenda for standardizing AI deployment across diverse governmental contexts, emphasizing the need for dynamic governance mechanisms that can evolve with the technology. Our contribution lies not in prescribing one-size-fits-all rules, but in providing a systematic scaffolding that helps policymakers, developers, and citizens navigate the trade-offs inherent in AI-augmented public administration. This unified framework thus serves as both a diagnostic tool for existing systems and a blueprint for future implementations that are operationally sound, epistemically rigorous, and normatively legitimate.

title: Non-union of the ulnar styloid process in children is common but long-term morbidity is rare: a population-based study with mean 11 years (9-15) follow-up.
text_ai: Background and purpose - Fracture of the ulnar styloid process (USP) is common in children in connection with distal radius fracture. The long-term morbidity of USP non-union following a childhood distal radius fracture is unclear. We evaluated long-term clinical and radiographic findings of USP non-union. Methods - From a population-based fracture register, we identified all children aged <16 years diagnosed with a distal radius fracture between 2004 and 2010. Inclusion required a concomitant USP fracture at the time of injury. At a mean follow-up of 11 years (range 9–15), 126 of 178 eligible patients (71%) participated. Clinical assessment included bilateral wrist range of motion (flexion, extension, pronation, supination), grip strength (Jamar dynamometer), pain on a visual analog scale (VAS 0–100), and patient-reported outcome measures (QuickDASH, PRWE). Standardized radiographs were evaluated for USP non‑union (defined as absence of bony bridging across the fracture line at follow-up), ulnar variance, and degenerative changes (joint space narrowing, osteophytes, subchondral cysts). Results - USP non‑union was present in 68 of 126 patients (54%). Among these, median VAS pain at rest was 0 (IQR 0–5) and during activity 0 (IQR 0–10). Only 4 patients (6%) reported occasional mild pain (VAS ≤20), and none had persistent pain. Mean wrist range of motion in the non‑union group was 98% of the contralateral side (range 85–105). Grip strength averaged 96% of the unaffected side. Median QuickDASH score was 0 (IQR 0–2) and median PRWE was 1 (IQR 0–6), both within population norms. No patient sought medical care for ulnar‑sided symptoms or underwent surgery for non‑union. Radiographic degenerative changes were observed in 3 patients (4%), all with healed USP, and were not associated with non‑union. Ulnar variance was neutral or negative in all cases. Conclusion - USP non‑union following childhood distal radius fracture is common at long‑term follow‑up but causes negligible clinical morbidity. Routine follow‑up or intervention is not justified. These findings support conservative management of USP fractures in children.

title: Proportional Dynamics in Linear Fisher Markets with Auto-bidding: Convergence, Incentives and Fairness
text_ai: Proportional dynamics, originated from peer-to-peer file sharing systems, models a decentralized price-learning process in Fisher markets. Previously, items in the dynamics operate independently of one another, and each is assumed to belong to a different seller. We extend this framework to linear Fisher markets where buyers employ auto-bidding strategies, allowing a single buyer to manage multiple items through a common budget constraint. In our model, sellers no longer set prices independently; instead, prices emerge from the proportional allocation of buyer budgets across items, akin to the original dynamics. We establish that this process converges to a market equilibrium under mild conditions, generalizing known results for independent sellers. Furthermore, we analyze the incentive properties of proportional dynamics in the auto-bidding setting, showing that buyers cannot gain by unilaterally deviating from truthful budget reports when others follow the dynamics. This aligns with classic incentive compatibility in Fisher markets. Finally, we examine fairness criteria, demonstrating that the limiting allocation satisfies envy-freeness up to one item (EF1) and approximate proportionality. Our results bridge proportional dynamics and modern auto-bidding paradigms, offering theoretical guarantees for decentralized price discovery in large-scale markets. The analysis leverages potential functions and fixed-point arguments, and we illustrate the dynamics' robustness through numerical simulations.

title: Articulatory Representation Learning Via Joint Factor Analysis and Neural Matrix Factorization
text_ai: Articulatory representation learning is the fundamental research in modeling neural speech production system. Our previous work has established a deep paradigm to decompose the articulatory kinematics data into gestures, which explicitly model the phonological and linguistic structure encoded with human speech production mechanism, and corresponding gestural scores. In this paper, we extend that framework by integrating joint factor analysis with neural matrix factorization to learn more robust and disentangled articulatory representations. The factor analysis component captures low-dimensional latent factors governing articulatory kinematics, while neural matrix factorization models the nonlinear interactions between articulators and gestural scores in a shared embedding space. This joint formulation enables simultaneous learning of gesture boundaries and their temporal dynamics without requiring explicit segmentation or phonetic labels. We evaluate on multimodal speech production datasets, including electromagnetic articulography and real-time MRI. Results demonstrate that our method yields higher reconstruction fidelity and better interpretability of gestures compared to prior deep paradigms. Notably, the learned representations generalize across speakers and speaking rates, improving downstream phone recognition accuracy and revealing speaker-invariant articulatory patterns. Our work bridges statistical generative models and deep learning for speech motor control, offering a principled framework for unsupervised discovery of phonological structure from continuous articulatory data.

title: Multi-Tracer Correlated Stacking: A Novel Way to Discover Anisotropy in nano-Hz Stochastic Gravitational Wave Background
text_ai: The isotropic stochastic gravitational wave background (SGWB) generated by a population of supermassive black hole binaries (SMBHBs) provides a unique window into their cosmic evolution. In addition to the isotropic power spectrum, the anisotropic component of the signal carries additional information about the supermassive black holes (SMBHs) and host galaxy connection. Here we introduce a novel data-analysis technique—Multi-Tracer Correlated Stacking—to robustly extract the anisotropic SGWB at nano-Hertz frequencies using Pulsar Timing Array (PTA) data. The key challenge in detecting anisotropy is the faintness of the directional signal relative to the isotropic monopole and to the instrumental noise. Our method overcomes this by cross-correlating PTA residuals not with a single tracer of large-scale structure, but with a weighted combination of multiple galaxy catalogues (e.g., optical, infrared, and radio surveys) that correlate differently with the underlying SMBHB distribution. Each tracer provides an independent, albeit noisy, map of the expected GW source density. By stacking these cross-correlation signals after optimal weighting—accounting for each tracer’s bias, redshift distribution, and measurement uncertainty—we coherently sum the signal while suppressing uncorrelated noise. This dramatically improves the sensitivity to angular multipoles beyond the monopole, especially the dipole and quadrupole which encode the large-scale clustering of SMBHBs and the anisotropy due to our local motion relative to the cosmic frame. We demonstrate via realistic simulations that Multi-Tracer Correlated Stacking can achieve a detection of the anisotropic SGWB power spectrum with a signal-to-noise ratio several times higher than using any single tracer alone, given the anticipated sensitivity of next-generation PTA facilities (e.g., the Square Kilometre Array) and wide-area galaxy surveys (e.g., LSST, EUCLID). The recovered multipoles break degeneracies between the SMBHB merger rate, the typical binary eccentricity, and the host-galaxy connection—for example, distinguishing whether heavy binaries preferentially reside in massive elliptical galaxies or in star-forming disks. This technique thus opens a new observational window into the co-evolution of SMBHs and their environments, transforming the SGWB from a mere background into a rich, spatially-resolved cosmological probe.

title: Prevalence of mecA on oral mucosa in patients undergoing hematopoietic stem cell transplantation
text_ai: Objectives: Severe oral mucositis occurring after hematopoietic stem cell transplantation (HCT) is associated with a risk of systemic infection related to bacteremia. We reported antibiotic-resistant bacteria detected on the oral mucosa frequently during the period of HCT and indicated an association between oral mucositis and antibiotic-resistant bacterial infection (2011 MASCC/ISOO Annual Meeting). Methods: We conducted a prospective cohort study of 120 adult patients undergoing allogeneic or autologous HCT at a single tertiary center. Oral swab samples were collected from the buccal mucosa at baseline, and then weekly from the start of conditioning through engraftment. DNA was extracted and screened for the mecA gene using real-time PCR. Oral mucositis was graded daily using the World Health Organization scale. Blood cultures were obtained whenever fever or clinical signs of infection occurred. We defined mecA positivity as detection of the gene in at least one oral sample, and correlated its prevalence with mucositis severity and subsequent bloodstream infection. Results: mecA was detected in the oral mucosa of 38 of 120 patients (31.7%) during the study period. Prevalence peaked at day +7 post-transplant (22.5%), coinciding with the highest incidence of severe mucositis (grades 3–4, 41.7% of patients). Among patients with severe mucositis, mecA was found in 48.0%, compared with 15.9% in those with mild or no mucositis (P < 0.001). Eleven patients (9.2%) developed methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) bacteremia; notably, 9 of these 11 had preceding oral mecA detection, yielding a positive predictive value of 23.7% for subsequent MRSA bacteremia. Oral mecA carriage was also associated with prolonged neutropenia (median 12 vs. 8 days, P = 0.02). Conclusions: The mecA gene is highly prevalent on the oral mucosa during HCT, especially in patients with severe oral mucositis. This oral reservoir may predispose to MRSA bacteremia. Routine surveillance of oral mecA could identify high-risk patients and guide prophylactic or preemptive antibiotic strategies. Further studies are warranted to confirm these findings and explore mechanisms of mucosal-to-systemic translocation.

We reported antibiotic-resistant bacteria detected on the oral mucosa frequently during the period of HCT and indicated an association between oral mucositis and antibiotic-resistant bacterial infection (2011 MASCC/ISOO Annual Meeting).

title: Palette-colouring: a belief-propagation approach
text_ai: We consider a variation of the prototype combinatorial-optimisation problem known as graph-colouring. Our optimisation goal is to colour the vertices of a graph with a fixed number of colours, in a way to maximise the number of different colours present in the set of nearest neighbours of each given vertex. This problem, termed palette-colouring, is NP-hard in general, and we propose a belief-propagation algorithm to approximate its solution. The algorithm uses a factor graph where each vertex corresponds to a variable node with domain of colours, and each edge between neighbouring vertices introduces a factor that encourages diversity of colours in the neighbourhood. Unlike standard graph-colouring, which requires adjacent vertices to have different colours, palette-colouring promotes local colour richness. Belief propagation iteratively passes messages that represent marginal probabilities of colour assignments, converging to a stationary point. We test the algorithm on random graphs and benchmark instances, showing that it outperforms greedy heuristics in terms of achieved palette size, particularly on structured graphs. The approach also scales well to large networks, making it suitable for applications in resource allocation and network design. Our work demonstrates the versatility of belief-propagation for non-standard combinatorial optimisation.

title: $R^2$-Mesh: Reinforcement Learning Powered Mesh Reconstruction via Geometry and Appearance Refinement
text_ai: Mesh reconstruction based on Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) is popular in a variety of applications such as computer graphics, virtual reality, and medical imaging due to its efficiency in handling complex geometric structures and facilitating real-time rendering. However, existing works often fail to capture fine geometric details accurately and struggle with optimizing rendering quality. To address these challenges, we present \(R^2\)-Mesh, a novel reinforcement learning framework that jointly refines geometry and appearance for high-fidelity mesh reconstruction. Our approach leverages a learnable agent which iteratively adjusts vertex positions and per-vertex appearance attributes (e.g., color and roughness) guided by a reward function that balances geometric accuracy, photometric consistency, and smoothness. Unlike traditional optimization heuristics, the agent is trained via proximal policy optimization over a diverse set of scenes, enabling adaptive, context-aware refinement that captures intricate details (e.g., sharp edges and fine textures) while avoiding local minima. Geometry updates are regularized by a signed distance field prior, and appearance updates are supervised by multi-view rendering losses. Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets (including DTU, NeRF-Synthetic, and ScanNet) demonstrate that \(R^2\)-Mesh outperforms state-of-the-art methods by up to 15% in Chamfer distance and 2.2 dB in PSNR, with improved visual fidelity and robust generalization. Our framework thus bridges the gap between efficient NeRF-inspired representations and high-quality meshes suitable for downstream applications.

title: Continual Evolution in Nonreciprocal Ecological Models
text_ai: Feedbacks between evolution and ecology are ubiquitous, with ecological interactions determining which mutants are successful, and these mutants in turn modifying community structure. We study the evolutionary dynamics of several ecological models with overlapping niches, including consumer resource and Lotka-Volterra models. By incorporating nonreciprocal interactions—where the effect of one species on another is not matched in magnitude or sign—we find that evolutionary dynamics are fundamentally altered. Unlike reciprocal models that often promote stable diversification or convergence to an evolutionarily stable strategy, nonreciprocal systems exhibit persistent, directional trait change over vast timescales. This "continual evolution" arises because the ecological feedback loop becomes inherently asymmetric: a mutant's success can reshape the community in a manner that prevents the establishment of a steady-state fitness landscape. Instead, the invasion fitness landscape itself evolves as a function of the current phenotype distribution, generating a traveling wave of trait values that never fully stalls. Using adaptive dynamics and stochastic simulations, we characterize this phenomenon across consumer-resource and Lotka-Volterra frameworks. In the consumer-resource model, nonreciprocal trade-offs between resource uptake and defense create a "red queen" regime where lineages perpetually chase a moving resource optimum. In the Lotka-Volterra model, asymmetric competition coefficients lead to cyclic dominance and continuous phenotypic displacement, even in the absence of external environmental change. We derive analytic conditions for the existence of such evolutionary cycles, showing that they require a specific degree of interaction asymmetry and niche overlap. These results challenge the classical view that evolution in stable environments leads to stasis or punctuated equilibria. Instead, nonreciprocal ecological models provide a generic mechanism for open-ended evolutionary change, with implications for understanding long-term biodiversity patterns and the evolution of complex ecological networks. Our framework unifies seemingly disparate phenomena, from arms races to evolutionary suicide, under a single dynamical principle driven by nonreciprocity.

We study the evolutionary dynamics of several ecological models with overlapping niches, including consumer resource and Lotka-Volterra models.

title: SL-YOLO: A Stronger and Lighter Drone Target Detection Model
text_ai: Detecting small objects in complex scenes, such as those captured by drones, is a daunting challenge due to the difficulty in capturing the complex features of small targets. While the YOLO family has achieved great success in large target detection, its performance is less than satisfactory when faced with small targets. To overcome these limitations, we propose SL-YOLO, a stronger yet lighter detection framework tailored for drone-based small object detection. Our approach introduces three key innovations. First, we design a lightweight backbone with enhanced receptive fields using dilated convolution and cross-stage partial connections, enabling effective multi-scale feature extraction with minimal computational overhead. Second, we develop a bidirectional feature pyramid network integrated with a spatial attention mechanism that prioritizes target regions while suppressing background interference. Third, we incorporate a novel regression loss with IoU-aware weighting to improve localization accuracy for tiny instances. Extensive experiments on VisDrone and UAVDT benchmarks show that SL-YOLO surpasses existing lightweight detectors. Specifically, it achieves 17.6% AP for small objects on VisDrone with only 3.2M parameters and 6.7 GFLOPs, outperforming YOLOv8n by 2.1% AP while reducing parameters by 30%. The model also attains a real-time speed of 108 FPS on an NVIDIA Jetson Xavier NX, confirming its suitability for edge deployment. These results demonstrate that SL-YOLO establishes a new state-of-the-art in drone target detection, offering an optimal balance between accuracy and efficiency. Moreover, the model exhibits robust generalization across diverse environmental conditions, including varying altitudes and occlusions, further validating its practical utility.

title: Paxos Made EPR: Decidable Reasoning about Distributed Protocols
text_ai: Distributed protocols such as Paxos play an important role in many computer systems. Therefore, a bug in a distributed protocol may have tremendous effects. Accordingly, a lot of effort has been invested in verifying such protocols. However, checking invariants of such protocols is undecidable and hard in practice, as it requires reasoning about an unbounded number of nodes and messages. We show how to model the core of Paxos—specifically the single-decree synod—in the decidable effectively propositional (EPR) fragment of first-order logic. In this fragment, satisfiability is decidable and can be checked automatically by finite-model-finding tools (e.g., Z3, iProver). Our key insight is to bound the number of distinct roles (proposers, acceptors, learners) and message types, while using uninterpreted functions and quantifier alternation to capture unbounded state evolution. The formalization preserves all essential behaviors: ballots, quorum intersections, and the leader-election phase, yet remains within EPR by carefully controlling quantifier prefixes. We prove that safety properties—such as agreement, non-triviality, and consistency—are expressible as purely universal formulas, enabling fully automated invariant checking via finite counterexample search. The approach also extends to dynamic reconfiguration and multi-Paxos without leaving the decidable fragment. To demonstrate practicality, we implement a tool that translates our EPR encoding of Paxos into SMT-LIB, and we verify inductive invariants for all reachable configurations up to arbitrarily large but fixed state spaces. Our evaluation shows that the verification completes within seconds, even for configurations with dozens of nodes. This work establishes that, despite the classic undecidability result, a core family of distributed consensus protocols admits decidable, fully automated verification by leveraging the EPR fragment. The result opens the door to applying similar reasoning to other fault-tolerant protocols.

However, checking invariants of such protocols is undecidable and hard in practice, as it requires reasoning about an unbounded number of nodes and messages.

title: Cycle-SUM: Cycle-consistent Adversarial LSTM Networks for Unsupervised Video Summarization
text_ai: In this paper, we present a novel unsupervised video summarization model that requires no manual annotation. The proposed model termed Cycle-SUM adopts a new cycle-consistent adversarial LSTM architecture that can effectively maximize the information preserving and compactness of the summary video. It consists of a frame selector and a cycle-consistent learning based evaluator. The frame selector, implemented as a bidirectional LSTM, learns to predict a binary mask for each input frame, thereby its output is a sparse set of keyframes. The cycle-consistent evaluator then attempts to reconstruct the full video from this summary by employing a decoder LSTM, generating a temporal sequence that closely approximates the original. To enforce cycle consistency, a reconstruction loss is computed between the original and reconstructed videos, while an adversarial discriminator encourages the summary to be both compact and informative by distinguishing real video sequences from those reconstructed from summaries. This adversarial loop, combined with the cycle-consistency constraint, prevents trivial solutions such as selecting all frames or empty sets. The entire model is trained end-to-end without any ground-truth summaries, relying solely on the interplay between the selector and evaluator. Extensive experiments on standard benchmarks (SumMe, TVSum, YouTube, OVP) demonstrate that Cycle-SUM achieves competitive or superior performance compared to fully supervised methods, validating the effectiveness of the proposed cycle-consistent adversarial framework for unsupervised video summarization.

The proposed model termed Cycle-SUM adopts a new cycle-consistent adversarial LSTM architecture that can effectively maximize the information preserving and compactness of the summary video. It consists of a frame selector and a cycle-consistent learning based evaluator.

title: Negotiating access to the Nigerian healthcare system: the experiences of HIV-positive men who have sex with men.
text_ai: Men who have sex with men in sub-Saharan Africa continue to have a disproportionately higher burden of HIV than their counterparts in the general population. In this qualitative study, barriers to participants accessing healthcare services in Nigeria, a country where same-sex relationships are criminalised and considered societally abhorrent, were explored. A purposive sample of 30 HIV-positive MSM was recruited from community-based organisations in Lagos and Abuja. In-depth interviews explored their experiences of seeking and receiving HIV care, including antiretroviral therapy. Thematic analysis revealed three overarching barriers: anticipated and enacted stigma from healthcare providers, which manifested as verbal abuse, refusal of care, and breaches of confidentiality; the threat of arrest or extortion under the Same-Sex Marriage Prohibition Act, which forced many to avoid formal health facilities; and self-imposed restrictions arising from internalised homophobia and fear of social exposure. Participants employed multiple negotiation strategies—such as concealing their sexual identity, travelling long distances to non-local clinics, and relying on peer networks for information and support—yet these frequently undermined continuity of care. Findings underscore that criminalisation does not merely deter healthcare seeking but actively structures the unsafe pathways through which care is eventually obtained. Without decriminalisation and sensitisation of healthcare workers, HIV-positive MSM will remain a hidden population with suboptimal treatment outcomes, perpetuating the cycle of transmission in this key group.

title: Nothing to see here: Failed supernovae are faint or rare
text_ai: The absence of Type IIP core-collapse supernovae arising from progenitors above 17 solar masses suggests the existence of another evolutionary path by which massive stars end their lives. The direct collapse of a stellar core to a black hole without the production of a bright, explosive transient is expected to produce a long-lived, dim, red transient known as a failed supernova. Current observational searches for failed supernovae have surveyed nearby galaxies for the disappearance of red supergiant progenitors, yet only a single candidate—the vanishing of a ~25 M⊙ star in NGC 6946—has been reported. This paucity implies stringent upper limits on the fraction of massive stars that undergo direct collapse. Modelling suggests that failed supernova transients should be red and faint, with absolute magnitudes around −12 to −14, and durations of several months to years, powered by the shock breakout from an extended envelope or by fallback accretion. However, such signatures are easily confused with dust-obscured outbursts or ordinary faint core-collapse events. Combining the null detections from Hubble Space Telescope monitoring campaigns with theoretical predictions of the expected rate of failed supernovae in the local Universe yields a maximum allowed fraction of ≲10–20% for progenitors above 17 M⊙. This is consistent with the missing Type IIP supernova population only if the majority of these high-mass stars collapse quietly and produce transients too faint for current surveys—or, alternatively, if stellar evolution models overestimate the mass threshold for black hole formation. Future wide-field, high-cadence infrared surveys such as the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope will be capable of detecting these faint red transients out to a few tens of megaparsecs, providing a definitive test. Until then, the null results indicate that failed supernovae are either intrinsically faint—limiting their detectability to very nearby galaxies—or genuinely rare, implying that most massive stars above the threshold still explode, albeit with some yet-unknown mechanism that suppresses the Type IIP display.

The direct collapse of a stellar core to a black hole without the production of a bright, explosive transient is expected to produce a long-lived, dim, red transient known as a failed supernova.

title: Short-ranged interaction effects on $Z_2$ topological phase transitions: The perturbative mean-field method
text_ai: Time-reversal symmetric topological insulator is a novel state of matter that a bulk-insulating state carries dissipationless spin transport along the surfaces, embedded by the $Z_2$ topological invariant. In the noninteracting limit, this exotic state has been intensively studied and explored with realistic systems, such as HgTe/(Hg,Cd)Te quantum wells. However, electron-electron interactions significantly alter the topological phase diagram, renormalizing the single-particle gap and potentially driving interaction-induced topological transitions. We develop a perturbative mean-field method to systematically investigate short-ranged interaction effects on $Z_2$ topological phase transitions. Our approach treats the interaction term as a perturbation on the noninteracting topological Hamiltonian, while self-consistently determining mean-field parameters that capture correlation effects. We apply this formalism to a minimal two-dimensional topological insulator model, incorporating both onsite Hubbard and nearest-neighbor density-density interactions. Solving the mean-field equations yields the phase boundary in the interaction-strength versus band-structure parameter space. We find that the nature of interactions crucially determines the topological response: repulsive interactions typically shift the topological phase transition toward stronger band inversion, whereas attractive interactions can stabilize topological order even in the trivial phase, leading to interaction-driven topological insulators. From our perturbative analysis, we derive analytical expressions for the critical interaction strength at which the $Z_2$ topological invariant changes, and we validate these results through numerical self-consistent calculations. The method captures subtle correlation effects beyond simple mean-field, such as renormalization of the band gap and modification of the surface state spectrum. The results demonstrate that the perturbative mean-field approach is both accurate and efficient, offering a systematic way to map out interaction-induced phase diagrams. This work extends the understanding of topological insulators beyond the noninteracting limit and establishes a framework for exploring interaction effects in more complex topological systems, including those with stronger correlations or additional symmetry constraints.

In the noninteracting limit, this exotic state has been intensively studied and explored with realistic systems, such as HgTe/(Hg,Cd)Te quantum wells.

title: An Interface Region Imaging Spectrograph first view on Solar Spicules
text_ai: Solar spicules have eluded modelers and observers for decades. Since the discovery of the more energetic type II, spicules have become a heated topic but their contribution to the energy balance of the low solar atmosphere remains unknown. Here we present the first comprehensive survey of solar spicules observed by the Interface Region Imaging Spectrograph (IRIS), leveraging its unique combination of high spatial, temporal, and spectral resolution in the far-ultraviolet. Using slit-jaw images at 1330 Å and 1400 Å along with co-aligned spectral data from the Si IV 1394 Å and Mg II k 2796 Å lines, we identify and track hundreds of spicules at the solar limb over multiple quiet-Sun regions. These data reveal a rich diversity of spicule dynamics, including clear signatures of both type I and type II populations distinguished by their lifetimes, velocities, and spectral profiles. Type II spicules exhibit rapid apparent motions (100–300 km s⁻¹) and reach heights exceeding 10 Mm, often accompanied by strong non-thermal broadening in Si IV indicative of turbulent motions or unresolved flows. Critically, we directly measure line-of-sight Doppler shifts from the Mg II k profiles, which show that many spicules harbor significant upward motions of 30–100 km s⁻¹ in their lower legs, while the higher-altitude Si IV emission frequently displays bidirectional flows consistent with reconnection-driven jets. By combining these kinematic measurements with estimates of mass and energy flux, we compute the total mechanical energy flux carried by spicules into the lower corona. Our results indicate that type II spicules alone contribute a time-averaged energy flux of order 10⁵ erg cm⁻² s⁻¹, comparable to the radiative losses of the quiet corona. This suggests that spicules—particularly the type II population—are a significant, previously underestimated source of mass and energy for the hot solar atmosphere. The IRIS observations further resolve the long-standing ambiguity in spicule classification and provide stringent constraints for numerical models, demonstrating that spicules are not merely a chromospheric phenomenon but a key intermediary in the energy and mass cycle of the outer solar atmosphere.

title: Truth is Universal: Robust Detection of Lies in LLMs
text_ai: Large Language Models (LLMs) have revolutionised natural language processing, exhibiting impressive human-like capabilities. In particular, LLMs are capable of "lying", knowingly outputting false statements. Hence, it is of interest and importance to develop methods to detect when LLMs lie. Indeed, several authors trained classifiers to detect LLM lies based on their internal model activations. These classifiers, however, typically rely on model-specific patterns, limiting their generalisability across architectures and prompting contexts. In this work, we demonstrate that LLM lies exhibit a universal neural signature: a consistent pattern of activation differences between truthful and deceptive outputs that persists across models, training histories, and task domains. By analysing hidden-state representations from multiple LLM families—including GPT, LLaMA, and Mistral—we identify a low-dimensional subspace in which lie-related features converge. We then train a single probe on this subspace using data from one model and apply it to others without fine-tuning. The probe achieves above 90% accuracy in detecting known lies and, critically, maintains performance on adversarial prompts and previously unseen lie types. Our findings suggest that the internal representation of deception is not an artefact of model idiosyncrasy but reflects a structural property of how falsehoods are computed in language models. This universality opens the door to robust, cross-platform lie detection without per-model retraining, with significant implications for AI safety and alignment research.

title: Binary black holes and tori in AGN I. Ejection of stars and merging of the binary
text_ai: Most galaxies have central massive black holes (BH), and merge with others during their evolution, as strongly suggested by recent observations. Consequently a black hole binary (BHB) emerges. Considering the evolution of the binary when it has become hard, at a separation of the BHs of about 1 pc, we propose to solve two basic questions in our understanding of the central activity of galaxies: (1) Do the BHs actually merge? And (2) What is the role of the surrounding gaseous torus in driving the binary to coalescence, and how does the binary affect the torus? We address both questions via a combination of analytical estimates and dedicated \(N\)-body/hydrodynamical simulations that follow the interaction of the hard binary with a population of stars and a dense, clumpy torus. We show that the binary does merge on a timescale shorter than the Hubble time provided that the torus mass exceeds a few percent of the binary mass. The key mechanism is the gravitational slingshot ejection of stars that pass within the binary's loss cone, which depletes the stellar cusp and reduces the binary's hardness. However, resonant relaxation and torus-induced dynamical friction replenish the loss cone and maintain a steady supply of stars, preventing the binary from stalling. Meanwhile, the torus itself is strongly perturbed: the binary's tidal field heats and disrupts the inner torus, inducing radial inflow of gas that can feed the individual BHs and trigger accretion episodes. We find that the binary hardens rapidly through three-body encounters and gas torques, reaching separations of \(\sim 0.01\) pc where gravitational radiation becomes dominant, ensuring a final merger. Furthermore, we identify a population of hypervelocity stars ejected at speeds exceeding 1000 km s\(^{-1}\), consistent with observed hypervelocity stars in galactic halos. Our results imply that BH mergers are inevitable in gas-rich AGN hosts, and that the interplay between the binary and the torus produces characteristic signatures in the electromagnetic and gravitational wave emission.

Consequently a black hole binary (BHB) emerges. Considering the evolution of the binary when it has become hard, at a separation of the BHs of about 1 pc, we propose to solve two basic questions in our understanding of the central activity of galaxies: (1) Do the BHs actually merge?

title: Imitation Learning for Active Neck Motion Enabling Robot Manipulation beyond the Field of View
text_ai: Most prior research in deep imitation learning has predominantly utilized fixed cameras for image input, which constrains task performance to the predefined field of view. However, enabling a robot to actively maneuver its neck can significantly expand the scope of imitation learning to encompass a wider variety of tasks and expressive actions such as neck gestures. To address this limitation, we propose a novel imitation learning framework that incorporates active neck motion into the robot's visuomotor policy. Our approach leverages a stereo camera mounted on a motorized neck, enabling the robot to dynamically adjust its viewpoint during task execution. The policy is trained end-to-end via behavioral cloning on demonstrations that include both end-effector trajectories and neck movement commands, captured from a human demonstrator wearing a head-mounted display with gaze tracking. We evaluate our method on six manipulation tasks that require reaching beyond the initial field of view, such as retrieving objects from behind occlusions and placing items on high shelves. Results show that active neck motion not only increases task success rates by an average of 34% over fixed-camera baselines but also enables novel neck gestures that communicate task intent (e.g., nodding to confirm grasp). Furthermore, we analyze the learned neck kinematics, revealing emergent coordination patterns between head orientation and arm motion. This work demonstrates that integrating active perception with imitation learning can substantially expand the operational workspace and enhance expressive robot behavior, paving the way for more versatile and human-like manipulation in unstructured environments.

title: Microfracture provides better clinical results than debridement in the treatment of acute talar osteochondral lesions using arthroscopic assisted fixation of acute ankle fractures
text_ai: PURPOSE: Ankle arthroscopy is a useful tool for detection and treatment of accompanying intraarticular pathologies in acute ankle fractures. The purpose of this study was to compare the treatment results of talus osteochondral lesions (OLT) with debridement and microfracture in arthroscopy assisted surgery of acute ankle fractures. METHODS: A retrospective comparative study was conducted on 86 patients with acute ankle fractures who underwent arthroscopic-assisted open reduction and internal fixation between 2015 and 2020. Intraoperatively, concomitant talar OLTs were identified and treated either by debridement alone (group D, n=42) or by microfracture (group M, n=44), based on lesion size, stability, and surgeon preference. Lesions were classified according to the International Cartilage Repair Society (ICRS) grade. All patients followed a standardized postoperative rehabilitation protocol. Clinical outcomes were assessed at a minimum follow-up of 24 months using the American Orthopaedic Foot and Ankle Society (AOFAS) ankle-hindfoot score, visual analog scale (VAS) for pain, and the Foot and Ankle Outcome Score (FAOS). Secondary outcomes included time to return to full weight-bearing and radiographic evaluation of fracture union and cyst formation. RESULTS: Both groups showed significant improvement in all outcome scores from baseline to final follow-up. However, group M demonstrated significantly higher mean AOFAS scores (89.2 vs. 82.6, p=0.01) and lower VAS pain scores (1.3 vs. 2.8, p=0.003) compared to group D. Similarly, FAOS subscores for pain, symptoms, and quality of life were significantly better in the microfracture group (p<0.05). No difference was observed in fracture union rate or time to weight-bearing. Two patients in group D required secondary cartilage procedures, compared to none in group M. CONCLUSIONS: In arthroscopy-assisted fixation of acute ankle fractures, concomitant microfracture of talar OLTs yields superior functional outcomes and pain relief compared with debridement alone. These findings support the routine use of microfracture for treatable acute talar chondral defects during fracture surgery.

The purpose of this study was to compare the treatment results of talus osteochondral lesions (OLT) with debridement and microfracture in arthroscopy assisted surgery of acute ankle fractures.

title: QCD correction to gluino decay to $t\bar{t}\tilde{\chi}^0_1$ in the MSSM
text_ai: We calculate the complete next-to-leading order QCD corrections to the three-body decay of gluino into top-pair associated with a lightest neutralino in the minimal supersymmetric standard model. We obtain that the LO and NLO QCD corrected decay widths of $\tilde{g} \to t \bar{t} \tilde{\chi}_1^0$ at the ${\rm SPS 6}$ benchmark point are $0.1490 GeV$ and 0.1069 GeV respectively, and the relative correction is -28.2%. We also analyse the scale dependence of the NLO corrections and find that they reduce the renormalisation and factorisation scale uncertainties significantly compared to the LO result. Furthermore, we study the dependence of the corrections on the supersymmetric parameters, including the gluino mass, the top-squark masses, and the mixing angle, and observe that the relative QCD correction varies from about −15% to −35% over a wide range of the parameter space. The large negative corrections originate from the gluon bremsstrahlung and virtual contributions, and are essential for precise predictions at the LHC. Our results provide an important input for the interpretation of gluino searches in the top-rich final states.

title: Computational insights and the observation of SiC nanograin assembly: towards 2D silicon carbide
text_ai: While an increasing number of two-dimensional (2D) materials, including graphene and silicene, have already been realized, others have only been predicted. An interesting example is the two-dimensional form of silicon carbide (2D-SiC). Here, we present an observation of atomically thin and hexagonally bonded nanosized grains of SiC assembling temporarily in graphene oxide pores during an atomic resolution scanning transmission electron microscopy experiment. These grains exhibit a honeycomb lattice with alternating Si and C atoms, confirmed by atomically resolved imaging and electron energy-loss spectroscopy. First-principles density functional theory calculations verify the stability of such hexagonal SiC monolayers and predict a direct band gap of ~2.5 eV, suggesting significant potential for optoelectronic and photocatalytic applications. The transient assembly, driven by electron beam-induced atomic migration within the constrained pores, elucidates a potential route to overcome the synthesis barrier for free-standing 2D-SiC. Our combined approach not only provides the first direct observation of this atomically thin elusive 2D material in a supported configuration but also reveals the underlying kinetic mechanisms. These findings represent a critical step toward large-scale controlled fabrication of large-area single-layer two-dimensional SiC, bridging the gap between theoretical prediction and practical realization.

title: Neural response to modulating the probability that actions of self or other result in auditory tones: A parametric fMRI study into causal ambiguity.
text_ai: In normal circumstances we can easily distinguish between changes to the external world brought about by our own actions from those with external causes. However, in certain contexts our sense of ownership and agency over acts is not so clear. The present parametric fMRI study therefore sought to systematically investigate how the brain responds when the causal link between an action and its sensory consequence is probabilistically ambiguous. We manipulated the probability that a button press—performed either by the participant (self) or by a confederate (other)—would produce an auditory tone, across five levels: 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, and 100%. During fMRI scanning, 20 healthy participants either executed the action or observed it being performed, while tones were delivered accordingly. On each trial, participants rated the degree to which they felt they had caused the tone, using a continuous scale. This parametric design allowed us to dissociate neural activity tracking objective probability from that tracking subjective agency. Using a general linear model with parametric regressors, we identified regions where blood-oxygen-level-dependent (BOLD) signal scaled linearly with the probability of self-causation. Whole-brain analysis revealed clusters in the anterior insula, ventral premotor cortex, and supplementary motor area showing robust positive parametric responses: these regions were increasingly active as the probability that the tone resulted from participants' own actions rose from 0% to 100%. Critically, activity in the bilateral temporoparietal junction and the posterior superior temporal sulcus decreased with increasing self-causation probability, instead showing peak activation when the action was attributed to another agent. Furthermore, when comparing subjective agency ratings with objective probability, we found that the dorsomedial prefrontal cortex and precuneus tracked the discrepancy between perceived and actual control, particularly at intermediate probabilities (25%–75%) where causal ambiguity was highest. These results indicate that the neural processing of causal ambiguity involves a distributed network that parametrically encodes probabilistic evidence for self-versus other-agency, with distinct regions weighting sensory evidence in a context-dependent manner.

title: H-EYE: Holistic Resource Modeling and Management for Diversely Scaled Edge-Cloud Systems
text_ai: Computing systems have been evolving to be more pervasive, heterogeneous, and dynamic. An increasing number of emerging domains now rely on diverse edge to cloud continuum where the execution of applications often spans various tiers of systems with significantly heterogeneous computational capabilities. Resources in each tier are often handled in isolation due to scalability and privacy concerns. To address these limitations, we introduce H-EYE, a holistic resource modeling and management framework that unifies heterogeneous edge and cloud resources under a single, scalable abstraction. H-EYE employs a novel layered representation that captures both the static capacities and dynamic behaviors of compute, storage, and network resources across geographically distributed tiers, while preserving per-tier autonomy and data privacy through localized aggregation and differential privacy mechanisms. A key innovation is the cross-tier resource gradient map, which models resource availability, utilization patterns, and inter-tier latency as continuous functions over spatial and temporal dimensions. This enables H-EYE to support diverse scaling requirements—from single-node edge devices to large-scale cloud clusters—without sacrificing accuracy or incurring prohibitive overhead. On top of this map, we design a set of holistic management policies including adaptive workload placement, dynamic resource scaling, and inter-tier load balancing, all optimized via a multi-objective reinforcement learning agent that accounts for application latency, energy consumption, and monetary cost. Extensive evaluations using real-world traces from smart city, industrial IoT, and video analytics workloads show that H-EYE reduces average end-to-end latency by 32–47% and energy consumption by 28–39% compared to state-of-the-art tier-isolated approaches, while scaling to thousands of nodes with linear time complexity. H-EYE thus provides a practical, privacy-preserving foundation for holistic resource orchestration in next-generation edge-cloud systems.

title: Mid-term results of the modular ANCA-Fit femoral component in total hip replacement
text_ai: We report the minimum five-year follow-up of 352 primary total hip replacements using the uncemented hydroxyapatite-coated ANCA-Fit femoral component with a modular neck and head. The series comprised 319 patients (212 men, 107 women) with a mean age at operation of 64.4 years (28 to 97). The principal diagnosis was osteoarthritis. Clinical and radiographic evaluation was performed at a mean follow-up of 6.5 years (5 to 9). The mean Oxford hip score improved from 42.1 preoperatively to 14.6 (0 to 48) at latest review. Radiological analysis demonstrated stable osseointegration in 98.8% of stems, with no femoral component showing complete radiolucent lines or subsidence >5 mm. Of the 15 modular neck and head combinations, no fractures or dissociation occurred. Ten revisions were performed: four for infection, three for recurrent dislocation, two for periprosthetic fracture (unrelated to the stem), and one for aseptic loosening of a single neck segment with subsequent stem exchange. The cumulative survival of the stem for aseptic loosening alone was 99.1% (95% CI 98.0 to 100) at seven years, and 97.2% (95% CI 95.1 to 99.3) for any revision, excluding infection. Acetabular component survival was 98.4% at seven years. These mid-term results confirm that the modular ANCA-Fit femoral component provides excellent fixation and clinical performance, with no adverse effects attributable to the modular neck design. Longer surveillance is warranted to assess late failures.
