title: The Implications of Local Fluctuations in the Galactic Midplane for Dynamical Analysis in the Gaia Era
text_ai: Orbital properties of stars, computed from their six-dimensional phase space measurements and an assumed Galactic potential, are used to understand the structure and evolution of the Galaxy. Stellar actions, computed from orbits, have the attractive quality of being invariant under certain assumptions and are therefore used as quantitative labels of a star's orbit. However, the underlying assumption of a smooth, static potential may be violated by local fluctuations—such as those induced by spiral arms, molecular clouds, or the Galactic bar—which introduce time-dependent perturbations. These fluctuations, though small in amplitude, can systematically alter the inferred actions of stars, particularly for those on orbits that are resonant with the perturbations or that spend significant time near the midplane. In the Gaia era, where vast numbers of stars have precise six-dimensional phase-space coordinates, understanding the impact of these local fluctuations is critical for robust dynamical inference. Here we explore the degree to which neglecting such fluctuations biases derived actions and orbital parameters. Using a suite of test-particle simulations in a time-dependent potential that models local midplane variations, we quantify the scatter and systematic offsets in actions for stars in the solar neighborhood. We find that stars with vertical oscillation frequencies near integer ratios with the perturbation pattern speed experience enhanced diffusion in action space. Even for non-resonant stars, the integrated effect over a few orbital periods leads to spurious correlations between actions and spatial position. These results imply that dynamical analyses using assumed invariants—such as chemo-dynamical tagging or Galactic archeology—may require either corrections for local perturbations or a careful selection of stellar samples to avoid regions most affected by midplane fluctuations. Our work provides a framework for incorporating such effects into future potential models and highlights the need for caution when interpreting action-based labels from Gaia data.

title: Position-Constrained Stochastic Inference for Cooperative Indoor Localization
text_ai: We address the problem of distributed cooperative localization in wireless networks, i.e. nodes without prior position knowledge (agents) wish to determine their own positions. In non-cooperative approaches, positioning is only based on information from reference nodes with known positions (anchors). However, in cooperative positioning, information from other agents is considered as well. In this paper, we propose a novel position-constrained stochastic inference framework that leverages both anchor measurements and inter-agent information under realistic constraints. Our approach models the joint posterior distribution of agent positions using a factor graph representation, where each node incorporates local range measurements and position bounds derived from network topology or environmental constraints. To enable scalable and distributed inference, we introduce a belief propagation algorithm that operates on this constrained graph, integrating stochastic sampling steps to handle nonlinear measurement models and non-Gaussian uncertainties. The key innovation lies in the explicit incorporation of position constraints—such as maximum movement radius or floor-plan boundaries—which significantly reduce the solution space and improve convergence. We validate our method through extensive simulations and real-world experiments in indoor environments with varying anchor densities and network sizes. Results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm achieves higher localization accuracy and faster convergence compared to standard cooperative schemes, especially in challenging scenarios with sparse anchors or high measurement noise. The constrained inference framework thus offers a practical and robust solution for cooperative indoor localization in resource-constrained wireless networks.

title: Return to Play After Multiligament Knee Injuries in National Football League Athletes.
text_ai: Return to play (RTP) of National Football League (NFL) athletes after isolated anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) tears has been reported. However, no studies have reported on RTP of NFL athletes after multiligament knee injuries. NFL athletes with multiligament knee injuries have lower RTP rates and longer recoveries than athletes with isolated ACL tears. The purpose of this study was to characterize RTP rates, time to RTP, and post-injury performance in NFL athletes sustaining multiligament knee injuries and to compare these outcomes with previously reported benchmarks for isolated ACL tears. A retrospective cohort design was employed using publicly available injury reports, team injury lists, and player performance data from the 2010–2020 NFL seasons. Inclusion criteria comprised players who sustained a multiligament knee injury (involving at least two of the following: ACL, posterior cruciate ligament, medial collateral ligament, lateral collateral ligament, or posterolateral corner) and underwent surgical reconstruction. Players with prior knee ligament injuries or concomitant fractures were excluded. The primary outcome was RTP, defined as playing in at least one regular-season game post-injury. Secondary outcomes included time from injury to first game appearance and change in performance metrics (games played per season, yards, touchdowns, and Pro Football Focus grade) relative to the two seasons before injury. Descriptive statistics and Kaplan-Meier survival analysis were used to estimate RTP rates and median recovery times. Multivariable logistic regression identified predictors of RTP, including age, position, number of ligaments injured, and specific ligament involvement. A total of 38 NFL athletes met inclusion criteria. The most common injury pattern was combined ACL and medial collateral ligament tears (n=16, 42%), followed by ACL and posterior cruciate ligament injuries (n=10, 26%). Overall RTP rate was 47% (n=18), significantly lower than the 82% rate reported for isolated ACL tears in NFL athletes (p<0.01). Median time to RTP was 15.8 months (interquartile range, 12.2–19.4 months), compared with 10.1 months for isolated ACL injuries. Among athletes who returned, 55% played for two or fewer seasons post-injury, and performance declined by an average of 34% in games played per season and 41% in yards relative to pre-injury levels. Older age (>28 years) and involvement of three or more ligaments were negative predictors of RTP (p<0.05). Athletes with ACL and medial collateral ligament injuries had higher RTP rates (56%) than those with involvement of the posterior cruciate ligament (30%). These findings confirm that multiligament knee injuries in NFL athletes result in substantially lower RTP rates and longer recovery times compared with isolated ACL tears, and that performance upon return is markedly diminished. The results provide prognostic information for players, team physicians, and athletic personnel, and underscore the need for optimized rehabilitation protocols and realistic expectations in this high-demand population.

title: Voltage Estimation in Low-Voltage Distribution Grids with Distributed Energy Resources
text_ai: The present distribution grids generally have limited sensing capabilities and are therefore characterized by low observability. Improved observability is a prerequisite for increasing the hosting capacity of distributed energy resources such as solar photovoltaics (PV) in distribution grids. In this context, this paper presents learning-aided low-voltage estimation using untapped but readily available and widely distributed sensors from cable television (CATV) networks. These sensors, originally deployed for broadband communication, are repurposed to measure voltage magnitudes with high temporal resolution at numerous points across the grid. A physics-informed neural network framework is proposed to fuse these sparse measurements with a reduced grid model, enabling accurate real-time voltage estimation even under significant PV intermittency. The approach is validated on a realistic 240-node low-voltage network with measured PV generation and load profiles. Results demonstrate that integrating only 10–15% of CATV sensors reduces the root-mean-square voltage estimation error by over 60% compared to standard state-of-the-art methods relying solely on smart meter data. Furthermore, the method proves robust to sensor noise and communication delays, maintaining performance within 2% of nominal voltage. The proposed framework thus offers a practical, cost-effective pathway to enhanced observability, facilitating higher DER penetration without extensive infrastructure upgrades.

title: Pulmonary Artery Systolic Pressure Response to Exercise in Patients with Rheumatic Mitral Stenosis: Determinants and Prognostic Value.
text_ai: Pulmonary hypertension in response to exercise is a marker of the hemodynamic severity of mitral stenosis (MS). However, the factors related to elevated pulmonary pressure with exercise are not well defined. The aim of this study was to assess the parameters associated with the pulmonary pressure response to exercise in patients with pure rheumatic MS. Patients underwent supine bicycle exercise echocardiography with continuous monitoring of pulmonary artery systolic pressure (PASP) estimated from tricuspid regurgitant velocity and right atrial pressure. Resting and peak exercise hemodynamic and Doppler parameters were recorded, including mitral valve area (MVA), mean mitral gradient, left atrial volume index, right ventricular function (tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion, systolic excursion velocity), and left ventricular global longitudinal strain. Exercise capacity was quantified as metabolic equivalents (METs). A total of 142 patients (mean age 48±12 years, 72% female) with pure rheumatic MS (MVA 1.2±0.3 cm²) were enrolled. During exercise, PASP increased from 32±8 mmHg at rest to 55±14 mmHg at peak (p<0.001). An abnormal PASP response, defined as peak PASP >50 mmHg, was observed in 64% of patients. In multivariate linear regression, independent determinants of higher peak PASP included smaller MVA (β=−0.38, p<0.001), higher resting mean mitral gradient (β=0.25, p=0.003), greater left atrial volume index (β=0.21, p=0.01), and lower peak METs (β=−0.18, p=0.03). Notably, tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion at rest did not predict exercise PASP. Over a median follow-up of 3.2 years, 28 patients (20%) experienced the composite endpoint of pulmonary edema, hospitalization for heart failure, or mitral valve intervention (balloon valvuloplasty or surgery). After adjustment for age, sex, rhythm, and MVA, an abnormal PASP response to exercise remained independently associated with adverse outcomes (hazard ratio 2.64, 95% CI 1.37–5.09, p=0.004). Receiver-operating characteristic analysis identified a peak PASP threshold of 54 mmHg as optimal for predicting events (area under the curve 0.76). Addition of exercise PASP to a model containing resting hemodynamics and clinical variables significantly improved risk reclassification (net reclassification improvement 0.31, p=0.01). These findings demonstrate that in patients with pure rheumatic MS, exercise PASP is determined not only by mitral valve obstruction severity but also by left atrial compliance and functional capacity. Importantly, the pulmonary pressure response to exercise provides incremental prognostic value beyond resting parameters, supporting its incorporation into routine risk assessment. Exercise echocardiography thus enhances the hemodynamic evaluation of MS, identifying patients at higher risk who may benefit from earlier intervention.

title: SCOUT: Teaching Pre-trained Language Models to Enhance Reasoning via Flow Chain-of-Thought
text_ai: Chain of Thought (CoT) prompting improves the reasoning performance of large language models (LLMs) by encouraging step by step thinking. However, CoT-based methods depend on intermediate reasoning steps, which limits scalability and generalization. Recent work explores recursive reasoning, where LLMs reuse internal layers across iterations to refine latent representations without explicit CoT supervision. However, these recursive approaches often lack the interpretability and reliability of explicit CoT, hindering their deployment in complex reasoning tasks. To bridge this gap, we introduce SCOUT (Stepwise Contextual Optimization via Unified Thinking), a method that teaches pre-trained language models to internalize a flow-based reasoning process. SCOUT leverages a novel Flow Chain-of-Thought (FCoT) mechanism, where the model learns to dynamically route information through its layers, generating latent reasoning trajectories that mimic step-by-step chains without requiring external token-level supervision. This is achieved via a lightweight fine-tuning phase that combines self-supervised consistency training with a small set of annotated reasoning flows, enabling the model to discover efficient multi-step inference paths within its own architecture. We evaluate SCOUT across diverse benchmarks, including GSM8K, CSQA, and StrategyQA. Results demonstrate that SCOUT outperforms standard CoT prompting by up to 6% absolute accuracy while reducing inference cost by 40%, and surpasses existing recursive methods by 4% on average. Moreover, SCOUT exhibits superior generalization to out-of-distribution reasoning tasks and maintains robust performance under input perturbations. Ablation studies confirm the importance of the flow-based design: FCoT produces more coherent latent steps than untrained recursion and yields intermediate representations that are interpretable via probing. Our findings suggest that SCOUT offers a scalable and interpretable alternative to explicit CoT, effectively marrying the transparency of stepwise reasoning with the efficiency of iterative refinement. This work opens new avenues for embedding structured reasoning directly into pre-trained models without sacrificing adaptability.

title: How Black Holes Stop Their Host Galaxy from Growing Without AGN Feedback
text_ai: Super-massive black holes (SMBHs) with $M_{\bullet} \sim 10^9 $ M$_{\odot}$ at $z>6$ likely originate from massive seed black holes (BHs). We investigate the consequences of seeding SMBHs with direct collapse BHs (DCBHs) ($M_{\bullet}=10^{4-6}\, \mathrm{M}_\odot$) on proto-galactic disc growth. We employ a suite of high-resolution, zoom-in cosmological simulations that track the assembly of a $10^{12}\, \mathrm{M}_\odot$ halo at $z=7$, seeded with a DCBH of $10^5\,\mathrm{M}_\odot$ at its center. These simulations explicitly exclude any AGN feedback processes—such as radiation pressure, jets, or winds—to focus solely on gravitational and hydrodynamical effects. Our results show that the BH's tidal field disrupts the gaseous disc beyond a critical radius of $\sim 100$ pc, preventing gas inflow and thus quenching star formation. The deep potential well of the BH drives gas into an eccentric, warped configuration, reducing rotational support and inducing gravitational instabilities. Consequently, the disc cannot maintain a stable, extended structure; gas is either ejected into the circumgalactic medium or accreted onto the BH at a self-limiting rate of $\sim 10^{-3}\,\mathrm{M}_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$. Over timescales of $10^8$–$10^9$ years, the star formation rate drops from several hundred to less than $1\,\mathrm{M}_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, effectively halting galaxy growth. These findings demonstrate that early SMBHs can regulate their host galaxies through pure gravitational means, without any need for AGN feedback. This mechanism naturally explains the presence of quenched massive galaxies at high redshift and offers a pathway for establishing the $M_{\bullet}$–$\sigma$ relation. Our work implies that gravitational seeding alone can initiate BH-galaxy co-evolution, with profound implications for early structure formation and the origin of supermassive black holes.

title: New interventions to treat chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension.
text_ai: Chronic thromboembolic pulmonary hypertension (CTEPH) can be defined as a type of precapillary pulmonary hypertension (PH) resulting from incomplete resolution of pulmonary embolism. Symptoms are exertional breathlessness and most patients come to a cardiologist's attention with a dilated right heart on echocardiography. While pulmonary endarterectomy (PEA) remains the gold-standard intervention for operable disease, up to 40% of patients are deemed ineligible due to distal thrombus location or comorbidities. Consequently, balloon pulmonary angioplasty (BPA) has emerged as a transformative percutaneous technique for inoperable or residual CTEPH. Recent refinements—including staged procedures, pressure-wire-guided dilation, and intravascular imaging—have dramatically reduced complications such as reperfusion edema while improving hemodynamic and functional outcomes. Concurrently, targeted medical therapy has advanced: riociguat, a soluble guanylate cyclase stimulator, is the only approved pharmacologic agent, yet novel pathways are being explored. Preclinical and early clinical data on endothelin receptor antagonists, prostacyclin analogues, and tyrosine kinase inhibitors demonstrate potential synergistic benefits when combined with BPA or PEA. Moreover, multimodality treatment algorithms—integrating surgery, angioplasty, and pharmacotherapy—are redefining the therapeutic landscape, enabling personalized strategies based on thrombus burden, right ventricular function, and comorbidities. Emerging data support the safety and efficacy of BPA as first-line therapy in select distal disease, while hybrid approaches for segmental lesions show improved survival compared to monotherapy. Diagnostic innovations, including dual-energy computed tomography and magnetic resonance perfusion, now allow precise lesion mapping and prediction of post-interventional hemodynamic response. Despite these advances, challenges persist: optimal timing of interventions, management of concomitant conditions such as pulmonary arterial hypertension, and long-term anticoagulation strategies require further study. This review synthesizes recent evidence on these new interventions—from technical refinements in BPA to novel drug classes and integrated care pathways—highlighting their potential to transform CTEPH prognosis. We conclude that a multidisciplinary, stepwise approach incorporating these modalities can achieve near-normal hemodynamics and functional recovery in the majority of patients, shifting the paradigm from a historically poor prognosis to one of meaningful long-term survival and quality of life.

title: Prognosis of French COVID-19 patients with chronic liver disease: A national retrospective cohort study for 2020.
text_ai: The impact of chronic liver disease on outcomes in patients with COVID-19 is uncertain. Hence, we aimed to explore this association. We explored the outcomes of all adult inpatients with COVID-19 in France, in 2020. We computed adjusted odds ratios to measure the associations between chronic liver disease, alcohol use disorders, mechanical ventilation and day-30 in-hospital mortality. We used the French national hospital discharge database (PMSI), which covers all public and private hospitalizations in France. All adult patients (≥18 years) hospitalized with a confirmed COVID-19 diagnosis (ICD-10 code U07.1) between 1 January and 31 December 2020 were included. Chronic liver disease (CLD) was defined by ICD-10 codes K70–K77, excluding acute hepatic failure, and further categorized as alcoholic (K70) or non-alcoholic (K71–K77) liver disease. Alcohol use disorders were identified via codes F10, K70 (overlap with alcoholic liver disease), and Z72.1. Comorbidities (hypertension, diabetes, obesity, chronic kidney disease, cardiovascular disease, and chronic respiratory disease) were retrieved using standard algorithms. Mechanical ventilation (MV) comprised invasive and non-invasive ventilation; day-30 in-hospital mortality was defined as death within 30 days of admission. We performed multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, sex, all listed comorbidities, and hospital characteristics (teaching status, region, COVID-19 admission volume), with clustering by hospital. Adjusted odds ratios (aOR) and 95% confidence intervals (CI) are reported. Among 128,941 adults hospitalized with COVID-19 in 2020, 5,342 (4.1%) had CLD, of which 2,109 (39.5%) were alcoholic. Alcohol use disorders were present in 7,641 patients (5.9%). Patients with CLD were younger (mean age 65 vs. 71 years) but had higher comorbidity burdens. After full adjustment, CLD was associated with increased odds of MV (aOR 1.38, 95% CI 1.29–1.48) and day-30 mortality (aOR 1.25, 95% CI 1.17–1.34). Alcoholic liver disease showed stronger associations (MV: aOR 1.54, 95% CI 1.39–1.71; mortality: aOR 1.42, 95% CI 1.28–1.57) than non-alcoholic CLD (MV: aOR 1.24, 95% CI 1.12–1.37; mortality: aOR 1.11, 95% CI 1.01–1.22). Alcohol use disorders independently predicted both outcomes, even after excluding alcoholic liver disease (MV: aOR 1.21, 95% CI 1.10–1.33; mortality: aOR 1.18, 95% CI 1.08–1.29). Sensitivity analyses restricting to patients with cirrhosis yielded similar findings. In this large, nationwide cohort, chronic liver disease, particularly of alcoholic origin, was independently associated with higher risks of mechanical ventilation and day-30 in-hospital mortality in COVID-19 inpatients. Alcohol use disorders conferred additional risk beyond that attributable to liver disease alone. These findings highlight the need for targeted prevention and management strategies for this vulnerable population during the pandemic.

title: Efficacy of the combination of modern medicine and traditional Chinese medicine in pulmonary fibrosis arising as a sequelae in convalescent COVID-19 patients: a randomized multicenter trial.
text_ai: The coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus-2 (SARS-CoV-2) has led to a significant number of mortalities worldwide. COVID-19 poses a serious threat to human life. The clinical manifestations of COVID-19 are diverse and severe and 20% of infected patients are reported to be in a critical condition. Pulmonary fibrosis has emerged as a debilitating sequela in a substantial proportion of convalescent COVID-19 patients, contributing to persistent respiratory dysfunction and reduced quality of life. Despite the urgent need for effective interventions, standard modern medical therapies for post-COVID-19 pulmonary fibrosis remain limited in their ability to reverse established fibrotic changes or improve long-term outcomes. Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM), with its holistic approach and multi-target mechanisms, has been historically applied to treat chronic pulmonary conditions, yet rigorous evidence for its synergistic effect with modern medicine in this specific context is lacking. This randomized, multicenter, parallel-group trial aimed to evaluate the efficacy and safety of combining modern medical treatment (standard-of-care antifibrotic agents, corticosteroids, and pulmonary rehabilitation) with a standardized TCM regimen (based on syndrome differentiation) versus modern medicine alone in convalescent COVID-19 patients with confirmed pulmonary fibrosis. A total of 240 patients from eight tertiary hospitals in China were enrolled between January 2021 and June 2022, with follow-up at 12 and 24 weeks. Inclusion criteria required radiologically confirmed pulmonary fibrosis, persistent respiratory symptoms (e.g., dyspnea, cough), and reduced forced vital capacity (FVC) below 80% of predicted at enrollment. Patients were randomly assigned 1:1 to the combination group (modern medicine plus TCM) or the control group (modern medicine alone). The primary outcome was the change in FVC percent predicted from baseline to week 24. Secondary outcomes included changes in high-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) fibrosis scores, six-minute walk distance (6MWD), St. George's Respiratory Questionnaire (SGRQ) scores, and serum biomarkers (KL-6, TGF-β1). Safety was assessed by adverse event monitoring. At week 24, the combination group demonstrated a significantly greater improvement in FVC percent predicted compared with the control group (mean difference 6.8%, 95% CI 4.1–9.5; p<0.001). HRCT fibrosis scores decreased by 3.2 points (SD 1.4) in the combination group versus 1.6 points (SD 1.2) in controls (p<0.01). The 6MWD increased by 52 m (SD 22) versus 28 m (SD 19; p<0.001), and SGRQ total score improved by 14.2 points (SD 6.8) versus 8.1 points (SD 5.8; p<0.001). Serum KL-6 and TGF-β1 levels declined more markedly in the combination group (both p<0.01). Adverse events were comparable between groups, with no serious TCM-related toxicity. These findings indicate that the addition of a standardized TCM regimen to modern medical therapy significantly enhances pulmonary function, radiologic regression, functional capacity, and quality of life in convalescent COVID-19 patients with pulmonary fibrosis, with a favorable safety profile. The combination approach may offer a promising therapeutic strategy for this challenging sequela, warranting further mechanistic studies and long-term follow-up.

title: Anticancer and cancer preventive compounds from edible marine organisms.
text_ai: A direct impact of food on health, which demonstrates that dietary habit is one of the most important determinants of chronic diseases such as cancers, has led to an increased interest of the consumers toward natural bioactive compounds as functional ingredients or nutraceuticals. Among edible marine organisms, seaweeds, microalgae, fish, and shellfish represent underexploited reservoirs of secondary metabolites with demonstrated anticancer and chemopreventive properties. Sulfated polysaccharides (e.g., fucoidan, carrageenan), phlorotannins, carotenoids (astaxanthin, fucoxanthin), and omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (EPA, DHA) have been shown to modulate key hallmarks of cancer. Their mechanisms include induction of apoptosis via caspase activation, cell cycle arrest at G0/G1 or G2/M phases, inhibition of angiogenesis through VEGF suppression, and downregulation of NF-κB-mediated inflammatory pathways. Epidemiological studies correlate high consumption of marine-derived foods with reduced incidence of colorectal, breast, and prostate cancers. In vitro and in vivo models further validate that these compounds can inhibit tumor initiation, promotion, and progression while exhibiting low toxicity toward normal cells. However, challenges remain regarding bioavailability, standardized extraction, and synergistic interactions with other dietary components. This review critically assesses the current evidence, identifies promising molecular targets, and discusses the potential integration of marine bioactive compounds into functional foods and nutraceutical formulations for cancer prevention and adjunctive therapy.

title: Optimal liquidation for a risk averse investor in a one-sided limit order book driven by a Levy process
text_ai: In a one-sided limit order book, satisfying some realistic assumptions, where the unaffected price process follows a Levy process, we consider a market agent that wants to liquidate a large position of shares. We assume that the agent has constant absolute risk aversion and aims at maximising the expected utility of the cash position at the end of time. We formulate the liquidation problem as a stochastic optimal control where the agent chooses the rate of trading over time. The execution price is determined by the limit order book shape, assumed to be a deterministic function of cumulative order flow, with temporary price impact. The unaffected price process is a Lévy process with jumps. The objective is to maximise expected exponential utility of terminal cash. This leads to a Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equation, which we simplify using the property of constant absolute risk aversion. By assuming a power-law shape for the limit order book, we derive a closed-form optimal liquidation strategy that is deterministic and independent of the price path, given by a linear function of time. We demonstrate that jump risk accelerates the optimal liquidation speed for large positions. Numerical simulations confirm the theoretical results.

title: Nuclear dimension and Z-stability of pure C*-algebras
text_ai: In this article I study a number of topological and algebraic dimension type properties of simple C*-algebras and their interplay. In particular, a simple C*-algebra is defined to be (tracially) (m,\bar{m})-pure, if it has (strong tracial) m-comparison and is (tracially) \bar{m}-almost divisible. These notions are related to each other, and to nuclear dimension. Specifically, I demonstrate that for a simple, unital C*-algebra, finiteness of nuclear dimension implies (tracial) (m,\bar{m})-purity with parameters determined by the dimension, and conversely, (tracial) (m,\bar{m})-purity together with the existence of a tracial state forces the nuclear dimension to be at most 2m + \bar{m}. Moreover, I show that a simple C*-algebra is pure—that is, (m,\bar{m})-pure for some m and \bar{m}—if and only if it is Z-stable and has finite nuclear dimension, confirming the Toms–Winter conjecture in this context. The non-unital case is handled through a careful analysis of unitizations and hereditary subalgebras, extending the main equivalences. I also introduce strong tracial versions of m-comparison and \bar{m}-almost divisibility, which are shown to be equivalent to their global counterparts under mild assumptions, such as the presence of a faithful tracial state. Examples are constructed to illustrate the independence of the parameters m and \bar{m}, demonstrating the flexibility of the purity notion and its sharpness. These results unify and refine previous work on nuclear dimension and Z-stability, providing new tools for the classification of simple nuclear C*-algebras and shedding light on the structure of pure C*-algebras within the Elliott programme.

title: Characterising the VHE diffuse emission in the central 200 parsecs of our Galaxy with H.E.S.S
text_ai: The diffuse very high-energy (VHE, > 100 GeV) gamma-ray emission observed in the central 200 pc of the Milky Way by H.E.S.S. was found to follow the dense matter distribution in the Central Molecular Zone (CMZ) up to a longitudinal distance of about 130 pc to the Galactic Centre (GC), where the flux rapidly decreases. The observed morphology, extending along the Galactic plane, suggests a cosmic-ray (CR) origin, with hadronic interactions of ∼PeV protons with ambient gas providing a natural explanation for the spectral and spatial characteristics. A detailed analysis of the energy-dependent morphology reveals no significant variation across the H.E.S.S. energy range (0.2–40 TeV), implying that the diffusion coefficient is spatially uniform within the CMZ and that the CR proton spectrum is remarkably hard (index ∼2.3). The flux decrease beyond |ℓ| ≈ 0.5° is interpreted as an environmental transition: either the CR density drops due to a confinement region boundary, or the gas density falls below the sensitivity threshold. Modelling with CR-driven emission from the Sgr A* supermassive black hole (SMBH) outburst history, combined with a radially dependent diffusion scenario, reproduces the observed intensity profile, favouring a recent (∼10 kyr) major injection episode. The data also enable a precise measurement of the total CR energy density within the CMZ, exceeding the local Galactic value by a factor of ∼100. Foreground and background contributions from the Galactic Ridge are subtracted using a dedicated template analysis, confirming that the diffuse emission is intrinsic to the CMZ. The spectral energy distribution of the diffuse component is consistent with a power law with exponential cutoff at ∼50 TeV, tentatively linking the emission to a population of PeVatrons—likely the SMBH or compact stellar clusters—whose CRs interact before escaping. These results deepen our understanding of particle acceleration and transport in the extreme environment of the Galactic Centre, provide stringent constraints on CR propagation models, and demonstrate the unique power of H.E.S.S. to probe the densest region of our Galaxy at VHE. Future observations with CTA will extend these studies to lower fluxes and higher energies, enabling a definitive test of the hadronic origin and the nature of the central engine.

title: Amorphous SiO2 nanoparticles promote cardiac dysfunction via the opening of the mitochondrial permeability transition pore in rat heart and human cardiomyocytes.
text_ai: Silica nanoparticles (nanoSiO 2 ) are promising systems that can deliver biologically active compounds to tissues such as the heart in a controllable manner. However, cardiac toxicity induced by nanoSiO 2 has been recently related to abnormal calcium handling and energetic failure in cardiomyocytes. Moreover, the precise mechanisms underlying this energetic debacle remain unclear. Here, we hypothesized that nanoSiO2 exposure leads to cardiac dysfunction through the opening of the mitochondrial permeability transition pore (mPTP). To test this, we exposed Langendorff-perfused rat hearts and human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CMs) to amorphous nanoSiO2 (20 nm) at concentrations ranging from 10 to 100 μg/mL. In rat hearts, nanoSiO2 caused dose-dependent declines in left ventricular developed pressure (LVDP) and maximal rates of contraction and relaxation (±dP/dt), along with elevated left ventricular end-diastolic pressure, indicative of both systolic and diastolic failure. These functional impairments coincided with a 50% reduction in ATP levels and a three-fold increase in reactive oxygen species (ROS) production. Mitochondrial membrane potential (ΔΨm), assessed via JC-1 fluorescence, dissipated, and isolated mitochondria exhibited swelling, a hallmark of mPTP opening. Administration of the mPTP inhibitor cyclosporin A (CsA, 1 μM) fully abrogated nanoSiO2-induced declines in LVDP and ATP depletion, confirming the causal role of mPTP. In hiPSC-CMs, nanoSiO2 exposure for 24 hours increased cytosolic calcium (Fluo-4 AM) and mitochondrial calcium (Rhod-2 AM) by 2.5-fold, leading to loss of cell viability. Further analysis indicated that nanoSiO2 promoted calcium influx through L-type calcium channels, as pretreatment with verapamil reduced calcium overload and mPTP opening. Additionally, nanoSiO2 increased mitochondrial ROS production via NADPH oxidase activation, and antioxidants such as N-acetyl cysteine prevented mPTP opening and cell death. Time-course analysis revealed that mPTP opening occurred within 2 hours, preceding ATP depletion and cell death. Transmission electron microscopy showed disrupted mitochondrial cristae and amorphous densities, while nanoSiO2 upregulated the mPTP component cyclophilin D at both mRNA and protein levels in a dose-dependent manner. siRNA-mediated knockdown of cyclophilin D prevented mitochondrial swelling and ΔΨm dissipation, and attenuated nanoSiO2-induced apoptosis (caspase-3 activation) by 70%. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that nanoSiO2 promotes cardiac dysfunction by opening mPTP through mitochondrial calcium overload and oxidative stress, resulting in bioenergetic collapse and contractile failure. This mechanism elucidates the previously unclear pathway of nanoSiO2 cardiotoxicity and identifies mPTP as a promising therapeutic target to mitigate adverse cardiac effects associated with silica nanoparticle-based drug delivery systems. Accordingly, co-administration of mPTP inhibitors with nanoSiO2-based drug carriers may offer a strategy to prevent cardiac side effects while preserving therapeutic benefits.

title: Towards An Efficient LLM Training Paradigm for CTR Prediction
text_ai: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated tremendous potential as the next-generation ranking-based recommendation system. Many recent works have shown that LLMs can significantly outperform conventional click-through-rate (CTR) prediction approaches. Despite such promising results, the computational inefficiency inherent in the current training paradigm makes it particularly challenging to train LLMs for ranking-based recommendation tasks on large datasets. This paper proposes a novel training paradigm, termed **Efficient LLM for CTR (ELCTR)**, which leverages three key innovations to mitigate computational bottlenecks. First, we introduce a **hierarchical distillation framework** that transfers ranking knowledge from a frozen pre-trained LLM to a compact student network via pairwise preference learning, reducing the need for full model updates. Second, we design a **dynamic negative sampling strategy** that focuses training on hard negatives—samples where the model’s ranking is ambiguous—by adapting the sampling ratio based on training loss, thus accelerating convergence. Third, we employ **parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT)** via low-rank adaptation (LoRA) modules inserted into the LLM’s attention layers, drastically cutting memory and compute requirements while preserving representational capacity. We evaluate ELCTR on three large-scale public CTR benchmarks (Avazu, Criteo, and Amazon Books) and a proprietary industrial dataset comprising over 2 billion user-item interactions. Results demonstrate that ELCTR achieves a **5.4× speedup in training time** and a **72% reduction in GPU memory usage** compared to the standard full-parameter fine-tuning baseline, while maintaining—or in some cases improving—key ranking metrics including AUC, NDCG@10, and HitRate@10. Ablation studies confirm that each component contributes non-trivially: the distillation alone yields a 2.1× speedup, hard-negative sampling adds 1.8×, and PEFT reduces memory by 50%. Furthermore, the student model retains over 98% of the teacher LLM’s ranking accuracy, demonstrating that efficiency does not come at the cost of effectiveness. These findings suggest that ELCTR offers a practical and scalable solution for deploying LLM-based CTR prediction in real-time recommendation systems, addressing a critical barrier to adoption. By decoupling the heavy LLM from the training loop and focusing compute on informative samples, our paradigm opens avenues for further scalability and paves the way for LLMs to become a viable backbone for industrial recommendation at scale.

title: Evaluation of nerve capture using classical landmarks for genicular nerve radiofrequency ablation: 3D cadaveric study.
text_ai: Radiofrequency (RF) denervation of the superolateral genicular nerve (SLGN), superomedial genicular nerve (SMGN) and inferomedial genicular nerve (IMGN) is commonly used to manage chronic knee joint pain. However, knowledge of articular branches captured, using classical landmarking techniques, remains unclear. Therefore, this cadaveric study aimed to evaluate the articular branches captured during RF ablation of the SLGN, SMGN, and IMGN using established anatomical landmarks. Twenty fresh-frozen cadaveric knees (10 specimens) were dissected to identify the target nerves and their articular branches. Three-dimensional coordinates were recorded using a digitizer, and standard ablation probe placements were simulated based on published landmark descriptions: 2 cm proximal to the adductor tubercle for SMGN, 2 cm proximal to the lateral epicondyle for SLGN, and at the medial joint line for IMGN. Capture was defined as the probe tip being within 5 mm of the target nerve’s articular branch. Results demonstrated that classical landmarks captured the SMGN articular branch in 85% of cases, but the SLGN was captured in only 60%, with the probe often positioned too posteriorly. The IMGN capture rate was 75%, though considerable variability existed due to the nerve’s branching pattern and the overlying sartorius muscle. Furthermore, in 20% of specimens, the RF lesion would have missed the primary articular branch entirely. These findings suggest that while classical landmarks provide moderate capture of the SMGN and IMGN, they are suboptimal for the SLGN. Anatomic variation and landmark inaccuracy frequently result in incomplete denervation, potentially explaining variable clinical outcomes. A refined, three-dimensional approach to probe placement may improve target coverage and procedural efficacy.

title: Chronotaraxis as a harbinger of medial thalamic infarction.
text_ai: Chronotaraxis is an impairment of the perception of the sequencing of time. This alteration of temporality has been described as being characteristically associated with thalamic involvement, specifically in the dorsomedial nucleus. We report the clinical cases of two patients with acute ischaemic strokes located in said territory, with a clinical presentation based on this symptom and the recognition of which was essential in the therapeutic approach. Both patients presented with an isolated, yet profound, disruption of temporal sequencing in the absence of classical focal neurological deficits such as hemiparesis, sensory loss, or visual field cuts. In the first patient, a 58-year-old male with vascular risk factors, the sole complaint was a “confusion about the order of events” during the preceding 24 hours. He was unable to recount the chronology of his morning activities, though individual episodic memories remained intact. Neurological examination revealed no motor or sensory abnormalities, but bedside cognitive testing demonstrated a striking inability to arrange a simple three-step sequence of hand gestures. Diffusion-weighted MRI confirmed a small, restricted focus of infarction in the left dorsomedial thalamic nucleus. The second patient, a 72-year-old female with atrial fibrillation, described a similar loss of time flow: she could recall isolated incidents from the previous day but could not sequence them. Magnetic resonance angiography revealed an acute ischaemic lesion in the right medial thalamus, corresponding to the paramedian artery territory. Notably, in both cases, the chronotaraxis preceded the development of more typical thalamic symptoms—such as behavioural apathy, confabulation, or anterograde amnesia—by several hours. Recognition of this symptom prompted immediate vascular imaging and timely initiation of antithrombotic therapy, preventing further propagation of the infarct. These findings underscore that chronotaraxis should be considered a specific, localizing sign of acute involvement of the dorsomedial thalamic nucleus, particularly in the setting of small-vessel or embolic occlusion of the thalamoperforating arteries. Clinicians must be attuned to this subtle temporal gnostic disturbance, as its early identification can expedite diagnostic workup and therapeutic intervention. We propose that chronotaraxis, when isolated, serves as a harbinger—a sentinel symptom—that heralds an evolving medial thalamic infarction, allowing for a window of opportunity to avert more extensive injury and long-term cognitive sequelae.

title: Repeated end range spinal movement while seated abolishes the proprioceptive deficit induced by prolonged flexed sitting posture. A study assessing the statistical and clinical significance of spinal position sense.
text_ai: Sustained spinal flexion has been proposed to affect the properties of spinal tissues, increase postural muscle's activation latency and act detrimentally on proprioception. This study evaluated the effect of flexed posture (FP) on spinal proprioception and assessed the immediate effect of spinal movement on the presumable flexion-induced proprioceptive deficit. Participants (n = 30, asymptomatic) sat in a standardized flexed posture for 15 minutes. Proprioceptive acuity was assessed using a lumbar repositioning task, measuring absolute, constant, and variable errors in degrees before and after FP. Following FP, a significant proprioceptive deficit was observed, with absolute error increasing from 2.1° ± 0.8° to 3.9° ± 1.2° (p < 0.001). Subsequently, participants performed 12 cycles of repeated end‑range spinal movement (flexion‑extension cycles to full range) while seated. Immediately after this movement intervention, repositioning error returned to baseline levels (2.0° ± 0.9°; p = 0.72 vs. pre‑FP). Constant error analysis revealed that FP induced a directional bias toward spinal flexion (mean shift of +1.1°; p < 0.01), which was also abolished by movement. To assess clinical significance, effect sizes were calculated (Cohen’s dz = 1.84 for the FP‑induced deficit; dz = 0.12 for the post‑movement comparison), and minimal detectable change (MDC95 = 0.9°) was exceeded by the deficit (mean change 1.8°) but not by the post‑movement change. These results indicate that the proprioceptive impairment from sustained flexed sitting is statistically and clinically significant, and that repeated end‑range spinal movement is a fully effective immediate countermeasure. This finding suggests a simple behavioral strategy to restore sensory‑motor control after prolonged sitting, with implications for spinal health and injury prevention. The study underscores that even short durations of static flexion alter position sense, but movement quickly reverses the deficit. Future work should explore the duration of this restorative effect and its impact on spinal loading patterns.

title: The role of ambient temperature and body mass on body temperature, standard metabolic rate and evaporative water loss in southern African anurans of different habitat specialisation.
text_ai: Temperature and water availability are two of the most important variables affecting all aspects of an anuran's key physiological processes such as body temperature ( T b ), evaporative water loss (EWL) and standard metabolic rate (SMR). continuation: In this study, we examined how ambient temperature (Ta) and body mass interact to influence Tb, SMR, and EWL in four southern African anuran species, each representing a distinct habitat specialisation: the fully aquatic Xenopus laevis, the semi-aquatic Amietia delalandii, the terrestrial Breviceps adspersus, and the arboreal Hyperolius marmoratus. Individuals spanning a wide body mass range (1.5–55 g) were acclimated to laboratory conditions and then exposed to five Ta treatments (10, 15, 20, 25, and 30°C) in a controlled environmental chamber. Body temperature was recorded using cloacal thermocouples, SMR was measured as oxygen consumption via closed-system respirometry, and EWL was determined gravimetrically over a 2-hour period under constant humidity. We hypothesized that species-specific habitat adaptations would modulate the thermal and hydric sensitivity of these metrics, with more terrestrial and arboreal species exhibiting lower EWL and higher thermal independence in Tb, while body mass would exert a negative allometric effect on mass-specific rates. Our results revealed that Tb was consistently within 0.5°C of Ta across all species and temperatures, indicating minimal thermoregulatory capacity regardless of habitat. SMR increased exponentially with Ta in all species, but the temperature coefficient (Q10, 15–25°C) differed significantly: 2.8 for X. laevis, 2.5 for A. delalandii, 3.2 for B. adspersus, and 3.0 for H. marmoratus, suggesting that terrestrial and arboreal species have higher thermal sensitivity, potentially reflecting adaptations to more variable thermal environments. Body mass scaling of SMR (mass exponent b) ranged from 0.68 to 0.81, with the lowest exponent in the aquatic species and highest in the terrestrial species, indicating that larger individuals of terrestrial and arboreal species have disproportionately higher metabolic costs at higher Ta. For EWL, habitat specialisation was the dominant factor: B. adspersus had the lowest EWL across all Ta (mean ± SE: 0.12 ± 0.03 mg g⁻¹ h⁻¹ at 30°C), while X. laevis had the highest (1.45 ± 0.21 mg g⁻¹ h⁻¹). Body mass scaling of EWL was strongly negative for all species (b = −0.15 to −0.28), but the effect was most pronounced in H. marmoratus, suggesting size-dependent water conservation strategies in arboreal frogs. Statistically significant interactions between Ta and habitat specialisation were found for both SMR (F₆,₁₂₈ = 4.32, p < 0.001) and EWL (F₆,₁₂₈ = 6.87, p < 0.001), driven by the divergent responses of the aquatic and terrestrial species at high temperatures. These findings demonstrate that habitat specialisation profoundly shapes the physiological responses of southern African anurans to thermal and hydric challenges, with consequences for energy balance and water balance under changing environmental conditions. The reduced EWL and higher metabolic thermal sensitivity of terrestrial and arboreal species likely reflect adaptations to desiccating conditions but may impose constraints at low temperature or under prolonged drought. Conversely, aquatic species, while less constrained by evaporative demands, may be more vulnerable to warming aquatic habitats. Overall, this study underscores the importance of integrating habitat specialisation and body mass into predictive models of amphibian responses to climate change, particularly in biodiverse regions such as southern Africa where anuran communities span a gradient of aridity and thermal regimes.

title: The Mystery of Two Straight Lines in Bacterial Genome Statistics. Release 2007
text_ai: In special coordinates (codon position--specific nucleotide frequencies) bacterial genomes form two straight lines in 9-dimensional space: one line for eubacterial genomes, another for archaeal genomes. All the 348 distinct bacterial genomes available in Genbank in April 2007, belong to these lines with high accuracy. The main challenge now is to explain the observed high accuracy. We propose that these lines represent a universal genomic constraint, likely arising from the interplay between mutational biases and selective pressures operating at the codon level. The observed collinearity suggests that genome composition is not free to wander randomly in the 9D space but is confined to a one-dimensional manifold. This could be explained by a few undirected parameters, such as GC content and codon usage preferences, that are linearly correlated across species. Alternatively, the lines might reflect a fundamental property of the genetic code and the underlying biochemistry of transcription and translation. We test these hypotheses by analyzing deviations from the lines in outlier genomes, examining the effects of varying mutation rates, and performing phylogenetic comparative analyses. The high precision of the fit—with residuals typically below 0.5%—indicates a robust evolutionary attractor, possibly related to optimal growth conditions or energy efficiency. Our findings call for a deeper theoretical framework linking genome statistics to cellular physiology and evolution, with implications for understanding the universal features of life.

title: Loewner Theory in annulus I: evolution families and differential equations
text_ai: Loewner Theory, based on dynamical viewpoint, is a powerful tool in Complex Analysis, which plays a crucial role in such important achievements as the proof of famous Bieberbach's conjecture and well-celebrated Schramm's Stochastic Loewner Evolution (SLE). Recently Bracci et al [Bracci et al, to appear in J. Reine Angew. Math. have developed a general framework for Loewner theory on multiply connected domains. In the present paper, we specialize to the case of the annulus, which is the simplest multiply connected domain. We introduce the concept of an evolution family on the annulus, which is a family of holomorphic self-maps satisfying a composition law. We show that such evolution families are governed by a generalized Loewner differential equation that involves a Herglotz vector field on the annulus. This vector field is holomorphic on the annulus and has a specific boundary behavior. We prove that there is a one-to-one correspondence between evolution families and certain vector fields. Moreover, we discuss the normalization of the evolution families and provide a complete characterization. As a byproduct, we obtain a new proof of the existence of radial and chordal Loewner equations on the annulus. This work is the first part of a series; in forthcoming parts we will study stochastic versions and applications to conformal invariants.

title: On the ubiquity of duopolies in constant sum congestion games
text_ai: We analyse a coalition formation game between strategic service providers of a congestible service. The key novelty of our formulation is that it is a constant sum game, i.e., the total payoff across all service providers (or coalitions of providers) is fixed, and dictated by the size of the market. We show that, under mild assumptions on the congestion cost functions and the market size, every strong Nash equilibrium of the coalition formation game results in a duopoly: exactly two coalitions form, each providing the service jointly. This holds regardless of the number of initial players, and even when providers are asymmetric in their costs or capacities. The intuition stems from the constant sum structure: any deviation that reduces the number of coalitions below two can be profitably blocked by a splinter group, while any deviation that increases the number above two invites a merger that increases joint payoff. Consequently, the core of the game contains only duopolistic coalition structures, and these are also the unique outcomes that are stable against simultaneous coalitional deviations. We further characterise the market shares and congestion levels in such duopolies, showing that they mimic the outcome of a classic two-player congestion game. Finally, we discuss implications for regulatory policy, noting that even with many competing service providers, the inevitable long-run market structure is a duopoly — a stark result that challenges the conventional wisdom that more providers necessarily foster competition.

title: Principles of Open Fracture Management
text_ai: Open fractures are contaminated wounds that contain gram-positive and gram-negative organisms; therefore, wide-spectrum antibiotic therapy should be incorporated into the treatment plan. Antibiotics should be initiated as soon after injury as possible, preferably within 3 hours of injury, after which time the rate of infection has been reported to increase. The cornerstone of effective management lies in a systematic, multidisciplinary approach. The Gustilo-Anderson classification system remains the most widely utilized framework for grading open fractures based on wound size, degree of soft tissue injury, fracture comminution, and contamination severity. This classification stratifies injuries into types I, II, and III (with IIIA, IIIB, and IIIC subtypes), each dictating escalating urgency and complexity of intervention. Meticulous, serial surgical debridement is the second fundamental principle, aimed at removing all devitalized soft tissue, bone fragments, and foreign material to convert a contaminated surgical wound into a clean one. This must be performed under tourniquet control—without exsanguination to preserve ischemic tissue viability—and often requires extension of the wound to allow complete visualization of the fracture and surrounding compartments. High-pressure pulsatile lavage with copious volumes of sterile saline is employed to reduce bacterial load, though recent evidence suggests that low-pressure irrigation may be equally effective while minimizing further soft tissue trauma. Temporary fracture stabilization, achieved through external fixation, splinting, or definitive internal fixation, is essential for pain control, prevention of further soft tissue damage, and facilitation of wound care. The timing of definitive fixation depends on overall patient physiology, contamination level, and soft tissue envelope condition, with damage control orthopaedics reserved for the critically injured. Wound management mandates a deliberate, staged approach: repeat debridements every 24 to 48 hours until the wound is clinically clean before considering definitive closure. Primary closure is rarely indicated; delayed primary closure, split-thickness skin grafting, or vascularized flap coverage (muscle or fasciocutaneous) within 5 to 7 days minimizes infection risk and optimizes functional outcomes. Adherence to these sequential principles—prompt antibiotic administration, classification-guided debridement, provisional stabilization, and timely soft tissue reconstruction—remains the bedrock of successful open fracture care, reducing rates of deep infection, nonunion, chronic osteomyelitis, and limb amputation while maximizing patient recovery and return to function.

title: Interpretable Data-Driven Demand Modelling for On-Demand Transit Services
text_ai: In recent years, with the advancements in information and communication technology, different emerging on-demand shared mobility services have been introduced as innovative solutions in the low-density areas, including on-demand transit (ODT), mobility on-demand (MOD) transit, and crowdsourced mobility services. However, due to their infancy, there is a strong need to understand and model the demand for these services. This paper proposes an interpretable data-driven framework for demand modelling of on-demand transit services, addressing the critical gap between predictive accuracy and model transparency. Leveraging high-resolution trip records from a real-world ODT pilot in a suburban region, we extract a comprehensive set of spatiotemporal, built environment, and socio-demographic features that capture underlying demand drivers. A gradient boosting machine is employed as the core prediction engine, achieving strong out-of-sample performance with a mean absolute error of 1.2 trips per hour per zone. To ensure interpretability, we apply Shapley additive explanations (SHAP) to decompose the model’s outputs, revealing that service accessibility, time of day, and proximity to activity centers are the most influential factors. Notably, the SHAP analysis uncovers non-linear and interaction effects that would be obscured by traditional parametric models—for example, the diminishing marginal return of fleet size in low-density zones. Beyond predictive capability, the framework generates actionable insights for service planning: it identifies underserved areas with latent demand and highlights windows of unmet need during off-peak hours. Comparative experiments with linear and tree-based alternatives confirm that interpretability does not come at the expense of accuracy; rather, the proposed model provides a transparent view into demand generation mechanisms. These findings have direct implications for the design of efficient, equitable ODT systems and for the calibration of dynamic pricing and fleet allocation strategies. By bridging machine learning performance with interpretability, this work offers a practical tool for transit agencies and mobility operators seeking to deploy demand-responsive services in low-density contexts.

title: Entanglement distillation based on polarization and frequency hyperentanglement
text_ai: Entanglement distillation has many applications in quantum information processing and is an important tool for improving the quality and efficiency of quantum communication, cryptography, computing, and simulation. We propose an entanglement distillation scheme using only one pair of polarization-frequency hyperentangled photons, which can be equivalently viewed as containing two pairs of entangled logical qubits: a pair of polarization-entangled qubits and a pair of frequency-entangled qubits. By exploiting the inherent correlations between these two degrees of freedom, our protocol achieves deterministic entanglement purification without the need for additional auxiliary photons or multiple iterations. The scheme operates through linear optical elements and frequency-selective components, enabling the extraction of a maximally entangled state from a partially mixed input with unit success probability in the ideal case. We analyze the performance under realistic noise conditions, including polarization decoherence and frequency-mode mismatch, and demonstrate that a significant improvement in fidelity can be attained with modest experimental requirements. Furthermore, the use of hyperentanglement allows for the simultaneous distillation of both polarization and frequency entanglement, effectively doubling the distilled entanglement yield per photon pair. Our approach offers a resource-efficient alternative to conventional distillation protocols, making it particularly attractive for long-distance quantum communication where photon loss and noise are prevalent.

title: MAP Estimation, Message Passing, and Perfect Graphs
text_ai: Efficiently finding the maximum a posteriori (MAP) configuration of a graphical model is an important problem which is often implemented using message passing algorithms. The optimality of such algorithms is only well established for singly-connected graphs and other limited settings. In this work, we demonstrate that the problem of exact MAP estimation via message passing is intimately related to the concept of perfect graphs. Perfect graphs are defined by the property that the chromatic number equals the clique number for every induced subgraph. We show that when the graph underlying the graphical model is perfect and the potentials are log-supermodular, the max-product algorithm converges to the true MAP assignment. This generalizes optimality results for tree-structured and bipartite graphs. Our approach builds on recent advances in perfect graph theory. Moreover, we prove that for any graphical model with a perfect graph, the linear programming relaxation of the MAP problem is tight, and message passing solves this LP exactly. This yields a unified framework explaining message passing success in applications such as error-correcting codes and computer vision. Finally, we discuss efficient detection of perfect graphs and extensions to approximate inference.

title: Gaps in treatment among users of osteoporosis medications: the dynamics of noncompliance
text_ai: PURPOSE: Cyclical patterns of compliance have been observed with many health-related activities such as dieting and exercise. It is not known whether such patterns of compliance exist among users of chronic medications. We sought to estimate the percentage of patients who restart osteoporosis therapy after a prolonged lapse in medication use and to identify the factors associated with a return to compliance. METHODS: Using a large administrative claims database from 2004–2008, we identified women aged ≥45 years who initiated osteoporosis therapy (bisphosphonates, raloxifene, or calcitonin) and had a treatment gap of at least 90 days following an initial period of continuous use (≥2 fills within 6 months). Patients were followed for up to 18 months after the gap. Restart was defined as a subsequent pharmacy claim for any osteoporosis medication within the observation window. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify patient, provider, and regimen characteristics associated with restart. RESULTS: Among 87,432 eligible initiators, 31,194 (35.7%) experienced a prolonged gap of ≥90 days. Of these, 9,477 (30.4%) restarted therapy within the follow-up period, with the median time to restart being 142 days. Restart rates varied markedly by prior therapy: patients who had been on a once-weekly bisphosphonate were significantly more likely to restart than those on a daily regimen (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] 1.43; 95% CI 1.32–1.55). Other factors positively associated with restart included older age (≥75 years, AOR 1.19; 95% CI 1.10–1.29), prior fracture history (AOR 1.36; 95% CI 1.25–1.48), and a visit to a rheumatologist or endocrinologist in the six months before the gap (AOR 1.22; 95% CI 1.13–1.31). Conversely, use of a selective estrogen receptor modulator (AOR 0.72; 95% CI 0.64–0.81) and higher out-of-pocket costs (AOR 0.88 per $10 increment; 95% CI 0.85–0.91) were associated with lower odds of restart. CONCLUSIONS: More than one third of osteoporosis medication users experienced a prolonged treatment gap, but only one third of these resumed therapy within 18 months. Noncompliance is thus not necessarily permanent; many patients re-engage after an extended lapse. The dynamics of restart are similar to cyclical patterns seen in health behaviors, suggesting that noncompliance with chronic medications may be modeled as a recurrent, rather than absorbing, state. Strategies to facilitate earlier restart—such as patient education, regimen simplification, and follow-up after gaps—could improve overall adherence in this population. Clinicians should be aware that a period of nonuse does not preclude future compliance, and interventions targeting the modifiable factors identified here may help reduce prolonged treatment gaps.

title: Advice Complexity of Adaptive Priority Algorithms
text_ai: The priority model was introduced to capture "greedy-like" algorithms. Motivated by the success of advice complexity in the area of online algorithms, the fixed priority model was extended to include advice, and a reduction-based framework was developed for proving lower bounds on the amount of advice required to achieve certain approximation ratios in this rather powerful model. In this work, we extend this framework to the adaptive priority model, where the algorithm dynamically selects the order in which items are processed based on decisions made so far. We develop a reduction-based technique for proving lower bounds on the amount of advice necessary for adaptive priority algorithms to achieve certain approximation guarantees. Our main results include tight lower bounds for well-studied problems such as Minimum Vertex Cover, Maximum Matching, and Minimum Dominating Set. In particular, we show that for Minimum Vertex Cover, any adaptive priority algorithm achieving an approximation ratio better than 2 requires at least Ω(n) bits of advice, matching an upper bound achievable with O(n) advice. Conversely, we prove that for Maximum Matching, O(log n) bits of advice suffice to obtain an optimal solution, while Ω(log n) bits are necessary, thus establishing a logarithmic threshold. For Minimum Dominating Set, we prove that Ω(n) advice is required for any constant approximation factor, and O(n) advice suffices to achieve a logarithmic approximation, highlighting a broad spectrum of advice requirements. We also demonstrate the power of adaptivity by constructing a problem instance where adaptive priority algorithms with constant advice outperform any fixed priority algorithm using a polynomial amount of advice, thereby revealing a fundamental gap between the two models. Our reduction framework is carefully adapted to account for the dynamic ordering choices of adaptive algorithms, employing combinatorial gadgets that encode advice-dependent decisions. Additionally, we present lower bounds for weighted variants, showing that the advice complexity increases with the precision of weights. These results provide a comprehensive characterization of the advice complexity landscape for adaptive priority algorithms, contributing to the broader understanding of limited information in greedy-like computations.

title: Effect of Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation on Pain Management: A Systematic Narrative Review
text_ai: Recently, clinicians have been using repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) for treating various pain conditions. This systematic narrative review aimed to examine the use and efficacy of rTMS for controlling various pain conditions. A PubMed search was conducted for articles that were published until June 7, 2019 and used rTMS for pain alleviation. Of the 1,247 articles initially identified, 97 met the inclusion criteria after full-text screening. Studies encompassed a range of pain types, including neuropathic pain, fibromyalgia, complex regional pain syndrome, migraine, and chronic low back pain. Most investigations employed high-frequency (≥5 Hz) rTMS applied to the primary motor cortex (M1), though dorsolateral prefrontal cortex and other targets were also explored. Outcome measures varied, with the most common being the Visual Analog Scale, Numeric Rating Scale, and Brief Pain Inventory. Across studies, rTMS demonstrated statistically significant but clinically modest reductions in pain intensity, typically ranging from 20% to 40% improvement relative to sham or baseline. Effect sizes were generally larger for neuropathic pain than for other conditions. Treatment protocols varied widely in terms of stimulation frequency, intensity, number of pulses, and session duration, and the optimal parameters remain undefined. Durability of analgesia was limited, with effects often diminishing within days to weeks after the last session. Adverse events were generally mild and transient, most commonly headache and scalp discomfort. Notably, the quality of evidence was compromised by small sample sizes, heterogeneous methodologies, and limited blinding. The narrative synthesis suggests that rTMS may offer a safe, noninvasive adjunctive option for pain management, particularly for neuropathic pain syndromes that are refractory to pharmacological interventions. However, the clinical significance of the observed effects is constrained by modest magnitude and short duration of relief. Future research should prioritize large, sham-controlled trials with standardized protocols, longer follow-up periods, and exploration of maintenance schedules to establish rTMS as a viable therapeutic tool for chronic pain.

title: Quantum secret sharing for a multipartite system under energy dissipation
text_ai: We propose a protocol for multipartite secret sharing of quantum information through an \textit{amplitude damping} quantum channel. This network is, for example, of two organizations communicating with their own employees connected via classical channels locally. We consider a GHZ state distributed among four members in an asymmetric fashion where the members of a sub-party collaborate to decode the received information at their end. We analyze the protocol's performance under varying damping strengths, quantifying the fidelity of the reconstructed secret and the mutual information among parties. The asymmetric distribution allows a threshold structure where only a designated subset can recover the full quantum state, while others obtain only partial information. Error mitigation strategies based on local operations and classical communication are examined to counteract the information loss due to amplitude damping. Our results demonstrate that the protocol remains secure against both individual and collective eavesdropping attacks within a finite damping regime, with a trade-off between decoherence resilience and the number of collaborating employees. We further discuss extensions to larger networks and the resource overhead required for faithful state reconstruction. The work provides a practical framework for implementing distributed quantum tasks in noisy environments typical of current quantum hardware.

title: Self-Refine Instruction-Tuning for Aligning Reasoning in Language Models
text_ai: The alignments of reasoning abilities between smaller and larger Language Models are largely conducted via Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) using demonstrations generated from robust Large Language Models (LLMs). Although these approaches deliver more performant models, they do not show sufficiently strong generalization ability as the training only relies on the provided demonstrations. To bridge this gap, we propose Self-Refine Instruction-Tuning (SR-IT), a novel framework that iteratively refines the training data by leveraging the target model’s own outputs and self-corrective feedback. Unlike static demonstration-based SFT, SR-IT employs a two-stage process: (1) initial fine-tuning on a seed set of LLM-generated reasoning chains, followed by (2) iterative cycles where the model generates candidate responses on unlabeled prompts, self-evaluates correctness and clarity, and selectively incorporates refined trajectories into the training set. This self-refinement mechanism enables the model to gradually internalize more robust reasoning patterns beyond the original demonstrations, improving generalization without requiring additional LLM supervision. Empirical evaluations across mathematical reasoning, commonsense QA, and multi-step inference tasks demonstrate that SR-IT consistently outperforms standard SFT baselines, achieving up to a 12% relative gain in accuracy on out-of-distribution benchmarks. Moreover, the approach yields models that exhibit stronger self-correction capabilities and flatter loss landscapes, indicating better-calibrated reasoning. These results suggest that self-refine instruction-tuning offers a scalable and effective paradigm for aligning reasoning abilities across model sizes, reducing reliance on static, externally-generated data.

title: Development and clinical study of submicronic-atropine sulphate respiratory fluid as a novel organophosphorous poisoning antidote.
text_ai: Increased use of organophosphate insecticides (OPI) and possibility of terror groups using stocks of nerve agents underscore the need to develop effective and safe antidotes. While intramuscular administration of antidotes like atropine sulphate (AS) has certain lacunae, intravenous route may not be always feasible in emergency field conditions. Here, we describe the development and clinical evaluation of a submicronic atropine sulphate (AS) respiratory fluid intended for inhalation, designed to overcome the limitations of parenteral routes. The formulation was engineered to produce respirable droplets with a mass median aerodynamic diameter below 1 µm, enabling deep lung deposition and rapid systemic absorption via the alveolar-capillary interface. Preformulation studies optimized excipient composition (including isotonicity agents and preservatives) to ensure stability, sterility, and tolerability of the aerosolized product. A randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial was conducted in 36 healthy volunteers to assess pharmacokinetics, safety, and tolerability. Subjects received either a single inhaled dose of submicronic AS (equivalent to 0.5 mg intravenous atropine) or intramuscular AS (0.5 mg) via a standardized nebulizer. Serial plasma samples were analyzed by LC-MS/MS for atropine concentration. Primary endpoints included time to peak concentration (Tmax), maximum concentration (Cmax), and area under the curve (AUC0–∞). Secondary endpoints comprised heart rate variability, pupillary dilation, and adverse event monitoring. The inhaled formulation achieved a Tmax of 4.2 ± 0.8 min versus 28.5 ± 5.1 min for intramuscular administration (p<0.001), with comparable Cmax and AUC values. No serious adverse events occurred; transient cough and mild throat irritation were reported in 3 subjects. These data demonstrate that submicronic AS respiratory fluid provides rapid, reliable systemic delivery, offering a practical and needle-free alternative for organophosphate poisoning in mass casualty or austere field settings. Further studies in poisoned models are warranted to confirm antidotal efficacy.

title: Simulating near-field enhancement in transmission of airborne viruses with a quadrature-based model.
text_ai: Some infectious diseases, such as influenza, tuberculosis, and SARS-CoV-2, may be transmitted when virus-laden particles expelled from an infectious person are inhaled by someone else, which is known as the airborne transmission route. These virus-laden particles are more concentrated in the expiratory jet of an infectious person than elsewhere in a well-mixed room, but this near-field enhancement in virion exposure has not been well quantified. To address this, we developed a quadrature-based model that resolves the spatial distribution of viral particles in the expiratory jet and its surroundings. The model employs a multi-moment representation of the particle size distribution coupled with a Lagrangian jet description. By discretizing the droplet phase into quadrature nodes, we track concentration, size, and viability with distance from the source. Simulations cover various expiratory activities (coughing, speaking, breathing) and environmental conditions (ventilation rates 0.5–10 ACH, relative humidity 20–80%). Using four quadrature nodes, we capture moments (number, surface area, volume) critical for viral load estimation. We validated the model against experimental dispersion data. Our results quantify the near-field enhancement factor—the ratio of virion concentration in the jet to the well-mixed background. For speaking at 1 m, this factor exceeds 10^3; at 0.5 m, it surpasses 10^4, indicating that proximity dramatically increases inhalation dose. Enhancement decays with distance but remains above 10 at 2 m for vigorous events. The enhancement is particle-size sensitive: small particles (<5 µm) disperse broadly, while larger ones (>10 µm) create a concentrated near-field peak. Enhanced ventilation reduces absolute concentration but not the gradient, so proximity remains dominant even with high ventilation. Face coverings lower the enhancement factor tenfold but still allow significant close-range transmission. Humidity alters size distribution via evaporation, changing enhancement patterns. These findings highlight that near-field effects are critical for risk assessment. Well-mixed models underestimate exposure by 10^3–10^5 in the first meter. Our quadrature-based approach offers a computationally efficient tool for real-time risk evaluation, informing spatial distancing guidelines that consider activity type and directionality, and localized ventilation strategies. It also bridges aerosol science and epidemiology by quantifying infection probability from near-field exposure.
