title: MVGrasp: Real-Time Multi-View 3D Object Grasping in Highly Cluttered Environments
text_ai: Nowadays robots play an increasingly important role in our daily life. In human-centered environments, robots often encounter piles of objects, packed items, or isolated objects. Therefore, a robot must be able to grasp and manipulate different objects in various situations to help humans with daily tasks. To address this challenge, we propose MVGrasp, a novel framework that leverages multi-view observations to achieve real-time, robust grasp planning in highly cluttered scenes. By capturing RGB-D images from multiple viewpoints, our method constructs a complete 3D scene representation, overcoming occlusions that plague single-view approaches. We introduce a multi-view fusion mechanism that effectively aggregates geometric and semantic features across views, followed by a lightweight neural network that processes the fused point cloud to predict high-quality grasp configurations efficiently. The system operates at over 30 Hz on standard hardware, enabling reactive grasping in dynamic environments. Extensive experiments on synthetic and real-world datasets demonstrate that MVGrasp outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both grasp success rate and computational speed. Our approach significantly advances robotic manipulation in cluttered settings, providing a practical solution for seamless integration into human-centric applications.

title: Early-life gut dysbiosis linked to juvenile mortality in ostriches.
text_ai: Imbalances in the gut microbial community (dysbiosis) of vertebrates have been associated with several gastrointestinal and autoimmune diseases. However, it is unclear which taxa are associated with gut dysbiosis, and if particular gut regions or specific time periods during ontogeny are more susceptible. To address these gaps, we conducted a longitudinal study on 120 farmed ostriches (Struthio camelus) from three cohorts, sampled from hatching to 90 days post-hatch—a period of high juvenile mortality. We profiled the gut microbiota via 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing across four intestinal regions (small intestine, cecum, large intestine, and cloaca) at six developmental time points. We identified two distinct microbial states: a healthy state dominated by Firmicutes and Bacteroidetes, and a dysbiotic state characterized by overgrowth of Proteobacteria (particularly Escherichia-Shigella and Clostridium sensu stricto) and depletion of beneficial commensals such as Lactobacillus and Ruminococcaceae. Dysbiosis was most prevalent in the cecum during the first two weeks post-hatch, coinciding with peak mortality. Birds that developed dysbiosis within the first week had a 3.5-fold higher risk of mortality by day 90 compared to those with stable microbiota (Cox proportional hazards model, p < 0.001). Dysbiosis was also spatially heterogeneous: the cecum showed earlier and more pronounced shifts than other regions, suggesting it is a critical hub for microbial imbalance. Furthermore, early-life dysbiosis was preceded by reduced microbial diversity and loss of specific anaerobes (e.g., Faecalibacterium) as early as day 3, indicating a predictive signature for subsequent mortality. Our results demonstrate that gut dysbiosis in ostriches is region-specific and time-dependent, with the cecum and early ontogeny representing a vulnerable window. The identified taxa associated with dysbiosis—particularly the expansion of pathobionts—provide biomarkers for health monitoring and targets for probiotic interventions. These findings have implications for reducing juvenile mortality in ostrich farming and highlight the importance of considering spatial and temporal dynamics in gut dysbiosis studies. Future work should investigate causal mechanisms and the efficacy of early-life microbial manipulation in preventing mortality.

title: Computational analysis of flow structures in turbulent ventricular blood flow associated with mitral valve intervention
text_ai: Cardiac disease and clinical intervention may both lead to an increased risk for thrombosis events due to modified blood flow in the heart, and thereby a change in the mechanical stimuli of blood cells passing through the chambers of the heart. In this study, we employ high-fidelity computational fluid dynamics to investigate the hemodynamic consequences of mitral valve intervention—specifically, edge-to-edge repair and prosthetic replacement—on left ventricular flow structures under physiologically relevant conditions. A patient-specific left ventricle geometry is reconstructed from clinical imaging, and a validated fluid–structure interaction framework is used to capture the complex interplay between the moving valve leaflets, the ventricular wall, and the blood flow. To model the transitional and turbulent flow regimes that arise post-intervention, we adopt a scale-resolving hybrid RANS-LES method, enabling detailed resolution of vortical structures and energy dissipation patterns. Our analysis focuses on quantifying the turbulent kinetic energy (TKE), Reynolds shear stresses, and the formation and evolution of the intraventricular vortex ring during diastole. Results reveal that both repair and replacement induce pronounced alterations in the vortex dynamics: the normally coherent ring becomes fragmented and asymmetric, leading to elevated TKE levels—up to 40% higher than in healthy controls—particularly near the mitral inflow and the apical region. These augmented turbulent stresses are associated with enhanced viscous shear on blood cells, as computed by the scalar shear stress index. Furthermore, we identify sustained vortical structures that persist into systole, disrupting the normal flow redirection toward the aortic outflow tract. The modified washout pattern increases the residence time of blood elements in the ventricle, a known pro-thrombotic factor. A parametric analysis across different intervention types and degrees of regurgitation indicates that the intensity and spatial extent of turbulent flow are strongly correlated with the geometric mismatch introduced by the prosthetic or repaired valve. The findings underscore that even successful mitral valve interventions can create hemodynamic environments conducive to platelet activation and thrombus formation, independent of the underlying disease. This computational framework provides a mechanistic link between intervention-induced flow disturbances and thromboembolic risk, offering a quantitative tool for optimizing valve design and surgical planning to minimize adverse outcomes.

title: Beyond Uncertainty: Evidential Deep Learning for Robust Video Temporal Grounding
text_ai: Existing Video Temporal Grounding (VTG) models excel in accuracy but often overlook open-world challenges posed by open-vocabulary queries and untrimmed videos. This leads to unreliable predictions for noisy, corrupted, and out-of-distribution data. Adapting VTG models to dynamically estimate uncertainties based on user input can address this issue. To this end, we propose Evidential VTG, a novel framework that integrates evidential deep learning into temporal grounding to quantify both epistemic and aleatoric uncertainty. By parameterizing a Dirichlet prior over the model’s predictions, our approach naturally captures prediction confidence without requiring extensive Monte Carlo sampling. This enables the model to reliably abstain when faced with ambiguous or irrelevant video content, while still delivering high-quality grounding for clear, in-distribution queries. We further introduce a temperature-scaled evidential loss that balances learning from clean versus noisy examples. Extensive experiments on Charades-STA, ActivityNet Captions, and QVHighlights demonstrate that Evidential VTG not only retains competitive accuracy under standard conditions but also significantly outperforms existing methods under video corruptions, distribution shifts, and open-vocabulary settings. The learned uncertainty estimates directly correlate with grounding quality, providing a practical, interpretable mechanism for trust-aware deployment in real-world applications.

title: Current irritability robustly related to current and prior anxiety in bipolar disorder.
text_ai: Although current irritability and current/prior anxiety have been associated in unipolar depression, these relationships are less well understood in bipolar disorder (BD). We investigated relationships between current irritability and current/prior anxiety as well as other current emotions and BD illness characteristics. Participants (N = 218) with DSM-5 bipolar I or II disorder completed the Irritability Questionnaire (IRQ) and the State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI) to index current irritability and anxiety. Current and prior anxiety disorders were assessed via the Structured Clinical Interview for DSM-5 (SCID-5). Current mood symptoms (depression, mania) and illness characteristics (age at onset, episode count, rapid cycling) were also evaluated. In bivariate analyses, current irritability was significantly associated with current anxiety (STAI-state; r = .44, p < .001) and with lifetime anxiety disorders, particularly generalized anxiety disorder (r = .28, p < .001) and panic disorder (r = .22, p = .001). Hierarchical multiple regression revealed that current anxiety (β = .32, p < .001) and number of prior anxiety disorders (β = .14, p = .02) uniquely predicted current irritability after controlling for current depression, mania, and demographic covariates. Among illness characteristics, rapid cycling (β = .18, p = .004) and more lifetime mood episodes (β = .16, p = .01) also contributed to the model, but their effects were partially mediated by current anxiety. No significant interaction emerged between bipolar subtype and anxiety predictors. These findings indicate that in BD, current irritability is robustly related to both concurrent and historical anxiety, extending the pattern observed in unipolar depression. The results underscore the importance of assessing and treating anxiety in bipolar patients presenting with irritability, as anxiety may represent a modifiable risk factor for irritability-related impairment. Future longitudinal work should examine temporal dynamics and potential causal pathways.

title: An exact relation between number of black box computations required to solve an oracle problem quantumly and quantum retrocausality
text_ai: We investigate the reason for the quantum speedup -- quantum algorithms requiring fewer computation steps than their classical counterparts. We extend their representation to the process of setting the problem. The initial measurement selects a setting at random, Bob (the problem setter) unitarily changes it into the desired one. We show that this retrocausal process reduces the number of black box queries needed. An exact relation emerges: \(Q = \frac{C}{1 - R}\), where \(Q\) is the number of quantum queries, \(C\) is the classical query complexity, and \(R\) is a measure of retrocausality defined as the fidelity between the initial random setting and the final desired setting after Bob's unitary transformation. For zero retrocausality (\(R = 0\)), \(Q = C\); for perfect retrocausality (\(R = 1\)), \(Q\) is the minimal constant, independent of problem size. This relation is applied to standard oracle problems, including Deutsch-Jozsa and Grover search, demonstrating that their respective speedups correspond to specific values of \(R\) (e.g., \(R = 0.5\) for Deutsch-Jozsa, \(R = 1 - 1/\sqrt{2}\) for Grover). The relation holds universally, as it derives from the time-symmetric structure of quantum mechanics, where the measurement at the algorithm's end retrocausally influences the initial setting selection. By reinterpreting the algorithm timeline, we treat the oracle as a retrocausal channel that transmits information from future to past, effectively reducing the number of required computations. This framework separates the role of the problem setter (Bob) from the algorithm itself, clarifying that the speedup originates from the overlap between initial randomness and final determinism. The exact relation provides a unified foundation for quantum speedup, grounding it in the foundational principle of quantum retrocausality rather than algorithmic specifics. It also implies a bound: the minimal number of quantum queries is inversely related to the retrocausal strength, which is ultimately constrained by the physical process of setting the problem. Our results offer insights for complexity theory, suggesting that the quantum-classical separation is inherently linked to retrocausal effects. Future work may extend this relation to other computational models, such as adiabatic quantum computing, and explore experimental tests via delayed-choice experiments. This work bridges quantum foundations and computational complexity, providing an exact, measurable link between oracle query counts and retrocausality.

title: International clinical practice recommendations on the definition, diagnosis, assessment, intervention, and psychosocial aspects of developmental coordination disorder.
text_ai: These international clinical practice recommendations (CPR) for developmental coordination disorder (DCD), initiated by the European Academy of Childhood Disability (EACD), aim to address key questions on the definition, diagnosis, assessment, intervention, and psychosocial aspects of DCD relevant for clinical practice. Key questions in five areas were considered through literature reviews and formal expert consensus. A systematic literature review was conducted for each of the five domains, supplemented by a Delphi consensus process involving an international, multidisciplinary panel of 80 experts including clinicians, researchers, and individuals with lived experience of DCD. Consensus was defined as ≥80% agreement on a four-point Likert scale. The recommendations were graded according to the Scottish Intercollegiate Guidelines Network (SIGN) methodology where applicable, and where evidence was insufficient, expert opinion informed the final statements. For definition, the recommendations reaffirm the use of the DSM-5 criteria, with specific guidance on operationalising the requirement that motor skills are substantially below that expected given chronological age and opportunity for learning. In diagnosis, a clear diagnostic algorithm is provided, emphasising the necessity of a comprehensive motor assessment using standardised, norm-referenced tools (e.g., the Movement Assessment Battery for Children-2), along with a detailed developmental and medical history to rule out other conditions. In assessment, the recommendations advocate for a multi-dimensional evaluation that includes not only motor proficiency but also cognitive, sensory, and emotional functioning, and highlight the importance of assessing functional impact in everyday contexts. In the intervention domain, the recommendations endorse task-oriented and cognitive approaches as first-line treatments, with strong evidence for task-specific training and cognitive orientation to daily occupational performance (CO-OP). The need for sufficient dosage and intensity is emphasised. For psychosocial aspects, the recommendations stress that DCD confers increased risk for anxiety, depression, and low self-esteem, and thus routine screening for psychosocial difficulties should be integrated into clinical care. Family-centred care and peer support are also recommended. These CPRs provide an up-to-date, evidence-based framework to guide clinical practice internationally. They highlight persistent gaps in knowledge, particularly in the areas of long-term outcomes and interventions for adolescents, and call for further research to strengthen the evidence base. Implementation strategies and dissemination plans are discussed to enhance global uptake.

title: SensatUrban: Learning Semantics from Urban-Scale Photogrammetric Point Clouds
text_ai: With the recent availability and affordability of commercial depth sensors and 3D scanners, an increasing number of 3D (i.e., RGBD, point cloud) datasets have been publicized to facilitate research in 3D computer vision. However, existing datasets either cover relatively small areas or have limited semantic annotations. We present SensatUrban, a large-scale photogrammetric point cloud dataset covering 7.6 km² of three distinct UK cities, densely annotated with 26 semantic classes including buildings, roads, vegetation, and vehicles. Unlike existing datasets that rely on laser scanning or small indoor/outdoor scenes, SensatUrban is reconstructed from high-resolution aerial imagery, capturing fine geometric and color details across urban landscapes. The dataset contains over 3.4 billion points and is split into training, validation, and test sets to facilitate rigorous evaluation. We benchmark state-of-the-art 3D semantic segmentation methods, including PointNet++, KPConv, and RandLA-Net, demonstrating that the increased scale and class diversity pose significant challenges for current approaches. Our analysis reveals performance disparities across object categories and highlights the importance of contextual reasoning in urban environments. SensatUrban serves as a realistic testbed for learning robust representations from large-scale point clouds, enabling advances in autonomous navigation, city modeling, and infrastructure monitoring. The dataset and evaluation protocols are publicly released to foster further research in urban-scale 3D scene understanding. We believe that SensatUrban will drive progress toward models capable of generalization across diverse cities and sensor modalities.

title: Deriving approximation tolerance constraints from verification runs
text_ai: Approximate computing (AC) is an emerging paradigm for energy-efficient computation. The basic idea of AC is to sacrifice high precision for low energy by allowing for hardware which only carries out "approximately correct" calculations. For software verification, this challenges the validity of verification results for programs run on approximate hardware. Such computations can produce results that deviate from the exact specification, complicating the task of verifying software correctness. Traditional verification techniques assume exact hardware behavior, yet when deployed on approximate systems, verified properties may no longer hold. To address this gap, we propose a method to automatically derive approximation tolerance constraints from verification runs. Our approach leverages the observation that verification runs—whether from model checking, symbolic execution, or testing—implicitly encode the precise operations and control flow of the program. By analyzing these runs, we can identify which arithmetic operations and data dependencies are most critical to maintaining correctness under approximation. We then synthesize constraints on the allowed error per operation (e.g., maximum relative or absolute deviation) such that the overall verification result remains valid. These constraints form a region of acceptable approximation that can guide hardware design or software mapping decisions. We implement a prototype based on symbolic execution with off-the-shelf SMT solvers and evaluate it on several benchmark programs from the embedded systems and signal processing domains. Results show that our technique can generate tight, sound tolerance bounds that significantly reduce energy consumption compared to conservative uniform approximation, while preserving the verified properties.

title: Neuropeptidase activity in the frontal cortex of Wistar-Kyoto and spontaneously hypertensive rats treated with vasoactive drugs: a bilateral study.
text_ai: Hypertension can lead to mood disorders that may worsen or ameliorate depending on the type of antihypertensive prescribed. Depression is associated with modifications in basal brain asymmetry particularly that of the frontal cortex, which is involved in blood pressure control. Furthermore, different vasoactive drugs may change the brain's asymmetry in a manner that contributes to cognition status. Here we examined whether chronic administration of the vasoactive drugs enalapril (10 mg/kg/day) and nifedipine (20 mg/kg/day) for 28 days alters the bilateral activity of three key neuropeptidases—aminopeptidase A, neprilysin, and angiotensin-converting enzyme—in the frontal cortex of adult male Wistar-Kyoto (WKY) normotensive rats and spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHR). Following drug treatment, rats were sacrificed, and frontal cortex tissue from left and right hemispheres was separately homogenized and assayed for enzymatic activity using specific fluorogenic substrates. Our results revealed a pronounced hemispheric asymmetry in SHR under vehicle treatment: the right frontal cortex exhibited significantly higher neuropeptidase activity than the left, particularly for aminopeptidase A and neprilysin, suggesting that hypertension itself predisposes to right‑sided dominance. In contrast, WKY rats showed symmetrical activity across hemispheres. Chronic enalapril treatment reversed this asymmetry in SHR by selectively increasing left‑hemisphere peptidase activity while decreasing right‑hemisphere levels, effectively restoring a bilateral balance similar to WKY patterns. Nifedipine, however, exacerbated the right‑hemisphere dominance, especially for angiotensin‑converting enzyme, intensifying the lateralized profile. No significant drug effects were observed in WKY rats, indicating that these neuropeptidase responses depend on the hypertensive background. The bilateral shifts in frontal cortex peptide processing align with the known mood‑modulating profiles of these vasoactive drugs: enalapril’s normalizing effect on asymmetry may underlie its neutral or beneficial impact on depressive symptoms, whereas nifedipine’s accentuation of asymmetry could parallel adverse cognitive and affective outcomes reported in clinical trials. These findings provide molecular evidence linking vasoactive drug treatment to frontal cortex lateralization via neuropeptidase activity, offering a potential mechanism by which antihypertensive therapy influences mood and cognition. Further studies should explore whether these enzymatic changes correlate with behavioral measures and whether other classes of vasoactive drugs produce analogous bilateral effects. Ultimately, this work underscores the importance of considering brain asymmetry when evaluating the neuropsychiatric consequences of hypertension and its pharmacological management.
prefix: Hypertension can lead to mood disorders that may worsen or ameliorate depending on the type of antihypertensive prescribed. Depression is associated with modifications in basal brain asymmetry particularly that of the frontal cortex, which is involved in blood pressure control. Furthermore, different vasoactive drugs may change the brain's asymmetry in a manner that contributes to cognition status.

title: The Community In-reach Rehabilitation and Care Transition (CIRACT) clinical and cost-effectiveness randomisation controlled trial in older people admitted to hospital as an acute medical emergency.
text_ai: To compare the clinical and cost-effectiveness of a Community In-reach Rehabilitation and Care Transition (CIRACT) service with the traditional hospital-based rehabilitation (THB-Rehab) service. Pragmatic randomised controlled trial with an integral health economic study. Large UK teaching hospital, with community follow-up. Frail older people aged 70 years and older admitted to hospital as an acute medical emergency. Three hundred and twenty participants (mean age 84.3 years, 58% female) were randomised to CIRACT (n=160) or THB-Rehab (n=160) between January 2020 and December 2022. The CIRACT intervention comprised early supported discharge with a multidisciplinary community rehabilitation team providing up to six weeks of goal-oriented therapy at home, while THB-Rehab provided inpatient rehabilitation followed by standard community services. The primary outcome was the Barthel Index at six months; secondary outcomes included length of index hospital stay, unplanned readmission within 90 days, health-related quality of life (EQ-5D-5L), and total NHS and social care costs over 12 months. Analysis was by intention-to-treat, with multiple imputation for missing data. At six months, the mean Barthel Index was 14.8 (SD 4.2) in the CIRACT group and 14.6 (SD 4.5) in the THB-Rehab group (adjusted difference 0.2, 95% CI –0.9 to 1.3; p=0.71), meeting the predefined non-inferiority margin. Median length of stay was 7 days (IQR 4–12) for CIRACT versus 11 days (IQR 6–18) for THB-Rehab (p<0.001). Readmission within 90 days occurred in 22% of CIRACT participants and 31% of THB-Rehab participants (odds ratio 0.63, 95% CI 0.42 to 0.95; p=0.03). The cost-effectiveness analysis, based on 12-month data, showed that CIRACT was associated with lower mean total costs (difference –£2,140, 95% CI –£3,450 to –£830) and marginally higher QALYs (difference 0.02, 95% CI –0.01 to 0.05), yielding a 94% probability of being cost-effective at the £20,000 per QALY threshold. Subgroup analyses revealed consistent benefits across age and frailty strata. No serious adverse events were attributed to either intervention. In conclusion, for frail older medical emergencies, the CIRACT model achieves similar functional recovery to traditional hospital-based rehabilitation while substantially reducing hospital stay, readmission rates, and overall healthcare costs. These findings support the wider implementation of community in-reach models as a clinically effective and cost-saving alternative for acute care transitions.

title: The Association between Reasons for a Rapid Response Team Alert and Immediate Patient Management in Total Hip Arthroplasty Patients.
text_ai: The purpose of this study is to evaluate the value and efficacy of rapid response teams (RRTs) for different triggering events in total hip arthroplasty (THA) patients. A retrospective review of all RRT events at a single, tertiary referral center from 2014 to 2016 was performed. The cohort comprised 1,847 primary THA patients, among whom 112 RRT activations occurred (6.1% incidence). Triggering events were categorized into five domains: respiratory (35.7%), cardiovascular (28.6%), neurological (16.1%), metabolic (11.6%), and other (8.0%). Immediate patient management was documented as oxygen supplementation, intravenous fluid bolus, medication administration (e.g., antihypertensives, antiemetics), transfer to a higher level of care (step-down unit or intensive care unit), or no intervention beyond monitoring. Multivariable logistic regression assessed the association between reason for alert and each management outcome, adjusting for age, sex, body mass index, Charlson Comorbidity Index, and time from surgery to RRT activation. Results revealed that respiratory triggers were significantly associated with oxygen administration (odds ratio [OR] 4.2, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.1–8.3, p<0.001) and transfer to higher level of care (OR 3.1, 95% CI 1.5–6.4, p=0.002). Cardiovascular triggers were most often managed with intravenous fluid bolus (OR 2.8, 95% CI 1.3–5.9, p=0.007) and medication administration (OR 3.5, 95% CI 1.6–7.6, p=0.001). Neurological triggers—primarily altered mental status or seizure—were strongly linked to intensive care unit admission (OR 5.1, 95% CI 2.2–11.9, p<0.001) but less frequently to specific pharmacological interventions. Metabolic triggers (e.g., hypoglycemia, electrolyte disturbances) were associated with targeted medication therapies (OR 4.0, 95% CI 1.5–10.6, p=0.005) and rarely required escalation of care. Only 8.0% of activations resulted in no intervention beyond observation, predominantly among “other” triggers. These findings suggest that RRT activation reasons in THA patients are meaningfully associated with distinct immediate management patterns. Respiratory and neurological alerts prompted the most resource-intensive responses, while cardiovascular and metabolic events were managed with targeted, often less acute interventions. The data support the value of reason-specific RRT protocols and education for frontline staff to streamline care and reduce unnecessary activations. Limitations include the single-center design, potential documentation variability, and lack of long-term outcomes. Future prospective studies should validate these associations and assess impact on patient safety and hospital resource utilization. Overall, understanding the trigger–management link can enhance the efficiency and clinical effectiveness of RRT programs in postoperative THA populations.

title: Moist convection is most vigorous at intermediate atmospheric humidity
text_ai: In Earth's current climate, moist convective updraft speeds increase with surface warming. This trend suggests that very vigorous convection might be the norm in extremely hot and humid atmospheres, such as those undergoing a runaway greenhouse transition. However, this inference overlooks the crucial role of entrainment and precipitation efficiency in modulating convective intensity. Using an ensemble of cloud-resolving simulations spanning a wide range of surface temperatures and relative humidities, we demonstrate that the vigor of moist convection—measured by maximum updraft velocity and mass flux—peaks not at extreme saturation, but at intermediate atmospheric humidity. As humidity increases from dry conditions, entrainment of dry air weakens, allowing updrafts to accelerate via latent heating. Yet above a threshold of near-surface relative humidity (~70–80%), the enhanced precipitation loading and increased prevalence of stratiform anvils suppress buoyancy and reduce updraft speeds. This non-monotonic behavior is robust across different radiative-convective equilibrium states and is reproduced by a simple entraining plume model. We further show that the same mechanism operates in simulations of high-CO₂ atmospheres and early Venus-like conditions: runaway greenhouse states actually exhibit weaker convective cores than moderately moist climates because the near-surface air is so close to saturation that precipitation-driven downdrafts stifle convective organization. Our results revise the conventional view linking convective vigor solely to surface warming and humidity, implying that extremely hot, moist atmospheres may be less dynamically active than previously assumed. This has implications for cloud feedbacks, atmospheric circulation, and the potential for habitable conditions on exoplanets. The intermediate humidity optimum suggests a fundamental constraint on convective energy transport, with maximum updraft speeds occurring in climates where both buoyancy generation and precipitation efficiency are balanced.

title: Nonlinear fractional waves at elastic interfaces
text_ai: We derive the nonlinear fractional surface wave equation that governs compression waves at an interface that is coupled to a viscous bulk medium. The fractional character of the differential equation comes from the fact that the effective thickness of the bulk layer that is coupled to the interface is frequency dependent. We show that the resulting equation takes the form of a nonlinear integro-differential equation with a fractional Laplacian operator acting on the displacement. The order of the fractional derivative is determined by the rheology of the bulk medium and the geometry of the interface. In the linear regime, the dispersion relation exhibits a power-law dependence on wavenumber, leading to anomalous attenuation characteristics. For large amplitude waves, the nonlinear terms, which arise from the finite deformation of the interface, compete with the fractional dissipation, giving rise to the possibility of solitary wave solutions. We analyze the conditions for the existence of such waves and derive approximate analytical solutions using a multiple-scale expansion. The results are compared with direct numerical simulations of the full equation. The derived model provides a framework for understanding wave propagation in a variety of soft materials and biological tissues where interfaces are in contact with viscous fluids.

The fractional character of the differential equation comes from the fact that the effective thickness of the bulk layer that is coupled to the interface is frequency dependent.

title: Exploiting Qubit Reuse through Mid-circuit Measurement and Reset
text_ai: Quantum measurement is important to quantum computing as it extracts the outcome of the circuit at the end of the computation. Previously, all measurements have to be done at the end of the circuit. Otherwise, it will incur significant errors. But it is not the case now. With advances in quantum hardware, mid-circuit measurement and reset have become feasible, enabling qubit reuse during a computation. This technique reduces the total qubit count required for a given algorithm by allowing a single physical qubit to represent multiple logical qubits sequentially. However, mid-circuit operations introduce additional errors and latency. We propose a systematic methodology to analyze the trade-offs between qubit savings and error accumulation. Through simulations on near-term quantum processors, we demonstrate that, for circuits with high qubit demands but moderate depth, qubit reuse can reduce the required resources by up to 40% without compromising fidelity. Key challenges include optimizing reset protocols and scheduling measurements to minimize crosstalk. Our results indicate that mid-circuit measurement and reset are a practical tool for scaling quantum algorithms on current hardware, offering a path toward larger computations within limited qubit counts. This work establishes guidelines for when and how to exploit qubit reuse effectively.

title: Ten-Year Evaluation of the TOYOTA Prehospital Stroke Scale for Tissue Plasminogen Activator Intravenous Therapy in the Real World.
text_ai: Emergency medical services are an important part of acute stroke management. We devised a prehospital stroke scale, the TOYOTA prehospital stroke scale for tissue plasminogen activator (t-PA) intravenous therapy (TOPSPIN) for triaging patients with ischemic stroke and especial indications for intravenous t-PA therapy in December 2006; this scale comprises 5 items including consciousness, atrial fibrillation, language disorder, disturbance of the upper extremities, and disturbance of the lower extremities. Here, we report the results of a 10-year prospective, observational, multicenter study evaluating the diagnostic accuracy and real-world utility of the TOPSPIN scale. From January 2007 to December 2016, consecutive patients with suspected acute stroke transported by emergency medical services to 12 participating hospitals were assessed using TOPSPIN upon arrival. The primary outcome was the scale’s ability to identify patients who received intravenous t-PA within 4.5 hours of symptom onset, as determined by subsequent clinical and imaging confirmation. Secondary outcomes included comparison with the Cincinnati Prehospital Stroke Scale and the Los Angeles Prehospital Stroke Screen, as well as analysis of over- and under-triage rates. Among 8,452 eligible patients, 1,204 (14.2%) received t-PA. TOPSPIN demonstrated a sensitivity of 84.7% (95% CI, 82.4–86.8), specificity of 78.3% (95% CI, 77.2–79.4), positive predictive value of 49.5%, and negative predictive value of 95.2% for t-PA administration. The scale performed consistently across subgroups defined by age, sex, and onset-to-door time. Notably, the inclusion of atrial fibrillation and consciousness items improved discrimination of t-PA-eligible patients compared to scales that rely solely on motor and language deficits. Over-triage occurred in 21.7% of non-t-PA patients, largely due to stroke mimics; under-triage was observed in 15.3% of t-PA recipients, often attributable to mild or rapidly improving symptoms. These findings confirm that the TOPSPIN scale, designed specifically for t-PA eligibility, provides a pragmatic and reliable tool for prehospital triage in real-world settings, facilitating faster treatment decisions and potentially improving outcomes.

title: A probabilistic reduced-order modeling framework for patient-specific cardio-mechanical analysis
text_ai: Cardio-mechanical models can be used to support clinical decision-making. Unfortunately, the substantial computational effort involved in many cardiac models hinders their application in the clinic, despite the fact that they may provide valuable information. In this work, we present a probabilistic reduced-order modeling (ROM) framework to dramatically reduce the computational effort of such models while providing a credibility interval. Specifically, the framework integrates proper orthogonal decomposition with a Gaussian process regression surrogate to construct a low-dimensional representation of the high-fidelity model’s output. A Bayesian inference step then quantifies parametric uncertainty and propagates it through the reduced-order model, yielding a credibility interval around the predicted quantities of interest. To ensure physiological relevance, we embed cardiovascular system constraints and employ a multi-fidelity training strategy that leverages a small number of full-order simulations. The framework is demonstrated on a patient-specific left ventricular model derived from clinical imaging data. Despite reducing computational cost by over two orders of magnitude, the probabilistic ROM maintains high accuracy in key hemodynamic metrics, with mean relative errors below 5% for ejection fraction, stroke volume, and peak pressure. Moreover, the credibility intervals effectively capture the true solution in more than 90% of test cases, indicating reliable uncertainty quantification. This work thus provides a practical pathway for integrating detailed cardio-mechanical analyses into time-constrained clinical workflows, enabling personalized risk stratification and treatment planning without sacrificing the rigor of physics-based modeling. Future extensions will incorporate active learning to adaptively refine the ROM in regions of high uncertainty and extend the framework to multi-chamber cardiac mechanics.

title: Quasar Photometric Redshifts and Candidate Selection: A New Algorithm Based on Optical and Mid-Infrared Photometric Data
text_ai: We present a new algorithm to estimate quasar photometric redshifts (photo-$z$s), by considering the asymmetries in the relative flux distributions of quasars. The relative flux models are built with multivariate Skew-t distributions in the multi-dimensional space of relative fluxes as a function of redshift and magnitude. The models are trained on a spectroscopic sample of quasars drawn from the Sloan Digital Sky Survey (SDSS) and the Wide-field Infrared Survey Explorer (WISE), using the optical $ugriz$ and mid-infrared $W1$ and $W2$ bands. By explicitly modeling the skewed and heavy-tailed nature of quasar relative flux distributions—which arise from redshift-dependent spectral features, dust extinction, and intrinsic variability—the Skew-$t$ framework yields substantially more accurate photo-$z$s than traditional Gaussian-based methods, particularly at $z>2.5$ where Ly$\alpha$ emission introduces pronounced asymmetries. We further exploit the probabilistic formulation to provide robust uncertainty estimates and to identify catastrophic outliers via a formal outlier probability. Extending the algorithm to candidate selection, we compute a likelihood ratio between the quasar model and a comparable stellar (or galaxy) model, enabling efficient rejection of contaminants without resorting to ad hoc color cuts. On a held-out spectroscopic test set, our method achieves a normalized median absolute deviation $\sigma_{\rm NMAD}=0.12$ in photo-$z$ and an outlier fraction ($|\Delta z|>0.15$) below 5%, outperforming both template-fitting and nearest-neighbor approaches, while maintaining a quasar completeness exceeding 95% over a wide magnitude range. The algorithm is computationally scalable to the billions of sources expected from surveys such as LSST and Euclid, and the resulting public catalog of photometric redshifts and quasar probabilities will facilitate robust statistical studies of the high-redshift quasar population and its evolution.

The relative flux models are built with multivariate Skew-t distributions in the multi-dimensional space of relative fluxes as a function of redshift and magnitude.

title: A 52 hours VLT/FORS2 spectrum of a bright z~7 HUDF galaxy: no Ly-alpha emission
text_ai: We aim to determine the redshift of GDS-1408, the most solid z~7 galaxy candidate lying in the Hubble Ultra Deep Field. We have used all the VLT spectra of GDS-1408 collected by us and two other groups with FORS2 at VLT in the last five years, for a total integration time of 52hr. The spectra cover the wavelength range 7500–10200 Å, encompassing the expected Lyα emission at z∼7. We reduce and coadd all available data using a dedicated pipeline, reaching a 3σ limiting flux of ∼ 5 × 10⁻¹⁸ erg s⁻¹ cm⁻² over a 1000 km s⁻¹ window, which is among the deepest Lyα searches at this epoch. No emission line is detected at the position of GDS-1408. From the non-detection we derive a 1σ upper limit on the Lyα rest-frame equivalent width of < 2.6 Å, assuming a systemic redshift set by the Lyman break (z ∼ 7.1). This limit places GDS-1408 firmly in the regime of Lyα–faint galaxies at z>6.5. The absence of Lyα is consistent with either a high neutral hydrogen fraction in the intergalactic medium (IGM) at this redshift or intrinsic properties of the galaxy. We compare our result with other recent studies of Lyα emitters and non-detections at z∼7. The deep non-detection suggests that GDS-1408, despite its bright rest-frame ultraviolet continuum (MUV ∼ −21.4), is unlikely to be a Lyα emitter. The tight upper limit also implies that the surrounding IGM may be significantly neutral, with x_HI > 0.4 at the 68% confidence level, under standard assumptions about the intrinsic Lyα escape fraction. However, an alternative explanation is a low covering fraction of ionized gas or a high outflow velocity. Our 52 hr combined spectrum provides the most stringent Lyα constraint for a single Lyman-break galaxy at this redshift, strengthening the evidence for a rapid evolution in the Lyα equivalent width distribution between z∼6 and z∼7. This result underscores the utility of ultra-deep spectroscopy for probing the ionization state of the early Universe and highlights the need for further characterization of faint galaxies during the epoch of reionization.

title: An Oka principle for equivariant isomorphisms
text_ai: Let $G$ be a reductive complex Lie group acting holomorphically on normal Stein spaces $X$ and $Y$, which are locally $G$-biholomorphic over a common categorical quotient $Q$. When is there a global $G$-biholomorphism $X\to Y$? We answer this question by proving an equivariant Oka principle: the inclusion of the space of holomorphic G-biholomorphisms into the space of continuous G-biholomorphisms is a weak homotopy equivalence. Consequently, a continuous G-biholomorphism can be deformed to a holomorphic one, and a local holomorphic G-biholomorphism can be globalized provided a continuous lifting exists. More precisely, we show that if X and Y are locally G-biholomorphic over Q, then the obstruction to patching local biholomorphisms lies in H^1(Q, Aut_q), where Aut_q is the sheaf of germs of automorphisms of the common fiber. Using the Stein property of Q and the reductivity of G, we prove that this cohomology group vanishes. The proof relies on a parametrized version of Luna's slice theorem, the Cartan–Remmert reduction, and Grauert's Oka principle, showing in particular that Aut_q is a coherent sheaf of groups whose cohomology vanishes because the fibers are homogeneous spaces for G. As a corollary, two Stein G-spaces with the same categorical quotient are G-biholomorphic if and only if they are topologically G-homeomorphic respecting the quotient map, generalizing the classical result for free actions and providing a new perspective on the classification of reductive group actions on Stein spaces. Our method also yields a parametrix construction for the equivariant Oka principle, analogous to the Grauert–Ramspott theorem.

title: A natural killer T-cell subset that protects against airway hyperreactivity.
text_ai: Infection of suckling mice with influenza virus expands a CD4 - CD8 - double-negative (DN) natural killer T (NKT) cell subpopulation that protects the mice as adults against allergen-induced airway hyperreactivity (AHR). However, this NKT cell subset has not been characterized, and the underlying mechanisms of protection remain unknown. Here, we identify this protective DN NKT cell subset as CD1d-restricted and expressing the invariant Vα14-Jα18 T-cell receptor, along with elevated levels of NK1.1, CD69, and the activation marker CD44, but lacking expression of CD62L. Transcriptomic profiling reveals a distinct gene signature enriched for anti-inflammatory cytokines, including interleukin-10 (IL-10) and transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β), as well as the immunoregulatory receptors LAG-3 and PD-1. Adoptive transfer experiments confirm that these cells confer protection against AHR in naive recipients, an effect abrogated by neutralization of IL-10 or TGF-β. Mechanistically, the DN NKT cells suppress dendritic cell-mediated activation of allergen-specific CD4⁺ T cells, promoting instead the expansion of Foxp3⁺ regulatory T cells in the lung-draining lymph nodes. Furthermore, the protection is dependent on sustained signaling via the aryl hydrocarbon receptor, which is required for the maintenance of the anti-inflammatory phenotype. These findings establish that a unique, long-lived DN NKT cell subset induced by neonatal viral infection functions as a critical regulator of airway allergic inflammation. Targeting this pathway may offer novel strategies for preventing asthma and other allergic airway diseases.

title: Context-Dependent Diffusion Network for Visual Relationship Detection
text_ai: Visual relationship detection can bridge the gap between computer vision and natural language for scene understanding of images. Different from pure object recognition tasks, the relation triplets of subject-predicate-object lie on an extreme diversity space, such as \textit{person-behind-person} and \textit{car-behind-building}, while suffering from the problem of combinatorial explosion. To address these challenges, we propose a Context-Dependent Diffusion Network (CDDN) that models visual relationships as iterative message passing over a dynamic graph. Unlike prior methods that treat subject and object independently, CDDN jointly refines their features and the predicate representation through a diffusion process conditioned on the global and local visual context. Specifically, a context-aware attention module computes pairwise affinity scores between all region proposals, guiding the diffusion to propagate relational information selectively. The network then decodes relation triplets by integrating the diffused features with linguistic priors from a pre-trained word embedding space. We further introduce a balanced sampling strategy to mitigate the long-tail distribution of predicates. Experiments on the Visual Genome and VRD benchmarks demonstrate that CDDN achieves state-of-the-art performance, particularly for rare and ambiguous relationships, while reducing the search space by over 40% compared to exhaustive pairing. Qualitative analyses confirm that the context-dependent diffusion effectively resolves spatial and semantic ambiguities, such as distinguishing “person-behind-person” from “person-beside-person.”

title: On Asteroid Retrieval Missions Enabled by Invariant Manifold Dynamics
text_ai: In recent years, the retrieval of entire asteroids has received significant attention, with many approaches leveraging the invariant manifolds of the Circular-Restricted Three-body Problem to capture an asteroid into a periodic orbit about the $L_1$ or $L_2$ points of the Sun-Earth system. While such approaches are promising, they typically assume a pre-existing accurate model of the target asteroid’s heliocentric orbit and rely on impulsive maneuvers at manifold insertion points, limiting their applicability to poorly characterized objects. This paper presents a systematic framework for designing retrieval missions without requiring precise initial orbital knowledge. We show that the stable and unstable manifolds of planar Lyapunov orbits about Sun–Earth L₁ and L₂ naturally intersect the near-Earth asteroid population, forming low-energy transport channels. By leveraging these dynamical pathways, a spacecraft can rendezvous with an asteroid using minimal deterministic ΔV and then guide it onto a manifold that delivers the object to a halo orbit for long-term storage or resource extraction. A survey of the known near-Earth asteroid catalog identifies several candidates for which the required ΔV for capture is less than 100 m/s. Furthermore, we demonstrate that the retrieved asteroid can be retained indefinitely using small, periodic station-keeping maneuvers that exploit the manifold’s hyperbolic structure. The analysis includes robustness to ephemeris uncertainties and perturbations from lunar and solar radiation pressure, confirming feasibility within current propulsion technology. Our results indicate that invariant manifold dynamics enable a new class of affordable asteroid retrieval missions, offering a viable pathway for in-situ resource utilization and planetary defense.

title: Prospects for constraining the spin of the massive black hole at the Galactic center via the relativistic motion of a surrounding star
text_ai: In this paper, we investigate the quality of constraining the spin of the massive black hole (MBH) at the Galactic center (GC) by using full general relativistic simulations of the motion of a surrounding star. We simulate the relativistic motion of a star on a bound orbit around the MBH, incorporating all spin-induced effects, including frame dragging and quadrupole moment precessions, up to post-Newtonian order consistent with full geodesic integration. The star is assumed to be monitored astrometrically and spectroscopically with future instruments, such as the next-generation Very Large Telescope Interferometer, providing microarcsecond positional accuracy and km s⁻¹ radial velocity precision. We systematically explore the parameter space of orbital semimajor axis, eccentricity, inclination relative to the MBH spin axis, and observer line of sight, while also varying the MBH spin magnitude (a) and orientation. For each configuration, we compute the Fisher information matrix to forecast the attainable precision on a and on the spin direction angles, under the assumption of a 10-year observational campaign covering at least one full orbital period for orbits of a few hundred gravitational radii. Our simulations reveal that the constraining power is highly sensitive to the orbital geometry. Orbits that are nearly polar or that precess significantly through the cumulative Lense-Thirring effect yield the tightest constraints on spin magnitude—potentially reaching uncertainties of δa ≲ 0.1 for favorable cases with a ≳ 0.5. Conversely, face-on orbits or those with negligible precession provide weak constraints. The spin orientation, particularly the position angle on the plane of the sky, can be determined to within a few degrees when the precession pattern is clearly detected. We also find that degeneracies between spin magnitude and orbital inclination can be partially broken by combining astrometric and radial velocity data. These results demonstrate that a carefully chosen stellar target—ideally on a short-period, moderately inclined orbit—could, with next-generation instrumentation, reveal the MBH spin at the Galactic center with unprecedented precision, thereby enabling tests of general relativity in the strong-field regime.
prefix: In this paper, we investigate the quality of constraining the spin of the massive black hole (MBH) at the Galactic center (GC) by using full general relativistic simulations of the motion of a surrounding star.

title: Effectiveness of Bone Conduction Stimulation Applied Directly to the Otic Capsule Measured at Promontory: Assessment in Cadavers.
text_ai: The aims of this study included: (a) to develop a method of direct acoustic bone conduction (BC) stimulation applied directly to the otic capsule, (b) to investigate the effect of different stimulation sites on the promontory displacement amplitude, and (c) to find the best stimulation site (among 2 located directly on the otic capsule and 1 standard site approved for clinical use) that provides the greatest transmission of vibratory energy. To address these aims, experiments were performed on 10 fresh-frozen cadaveric temporal bones. A custom-designed bone conduction transducer delivered vibration directly to two otic capsule sites (the cochlear promontory and the lateral semicircular canal) and to a standard clinical site on the mastoid. Promontory displacement amplitude, measured via laser Doppler vibrometry across 0.5–8 kHz, served as the outcome metric. Results revealed that direct otic capsule stimulation produced consistently higher displacement amplitudes than mastoid stimulation, with the cochlear promontory site yielding the greatest enhancement—particularly at low frequencies. At 0.5 kHz, the mean displacement was 20 dB higher than the mastoid site, and at 1 kHz, 15 dB higher. The lateral canal site also exceeded the mastoid but to a lesser degree. These findings indicate that direct otic capsule application of bone conduction stimulation can significantly improve vibratory energy transmission to the cochlea, with the promontory site being optimal. This technique holds promise for advancing bone conduction hearing devices, especially for patients with conductive or mixed hearing loss where conventional stimulation is insufficient. Further investigations in living subjects are necessary to confirm clinical feasibility and safety.

title: A formal implementation of Behavior Trees to act in robotics
text_ai: Behavior Trees (BT) are becoming quite popular as an Acting component of autonomous robotic systems. We propose to define a formal semantics to BT by translating them to a formal language which enables us to perform verification of programs written with BT, as well as runtime verification while these BT execute. that enables both offline verification and runtime monitoring. By mapping BT constructs—such as sequences, selectors, and condition nodes—to the primitives of this language, we obtain an unambiguous, executable model of the acting behavior. Our translation preserves the hierarchical structure and tick-based execution, allowing us to reason about properties like safety, liveness, and resource bounds using existing model checkers. For runtime verification, we instrument the formal model to generate monitors that detect violations during execution, enabling corrective actions on the fly. We illustrate the approach with a robot navigation case study, verifying that a BT-controlled robot never enters unsafe states and always achieves its goal under timing constraints. The formal semantics also facilitates modular analysis, composition of subtrees, and automatic synthesis of corrective conditions. Our work provides a rigorous foundation for using BT in safety-critical robotic applications, bridging the gap between the intuitive control flow of BT and the formal guarantees demanded by autonomous systems.

We propose to define a formal semantics to BT by translating them to a formal language which enables us to perform verification of programs written with BT, as well as runtime verification while these BT execute.

title: Beyond the Meta: Leveraging Game Design Parameters for Patch-Agnostic Esport Analytics
text_ai: Esport games comprise a sizeable fraction of the global games market, and is the fastest growing segment in games. This has given rise to the domain of esports analytics, which uses telemetry data from games to inform players, coaches, broadcasters and other stakeholders. A key challenge in this domain is the frequent patching of esport titles, which invalidates models trained on historical match data and forces analysts to rebuild their tools from scratch after every update. Prior work has focused on the "meta"—the prevailing strategies and character picks—but this approach is inherently ephemeral, as patches deliberately shift the meta to keep the game fresh. We argue that a more robust foundation lies in the game's underlying design parameters: attributes such as ability cooldowns, damage values, movement speeds, and resource costs. These parameters are not only documented in patch notes but also directly govern player behavior and matchup outcomes. By learning a mapping from raw game design parameters to features of optimal play, we can construct predictive models that remain valid across patches without retraining on new match data. We demonstrate this principle using data from two popular multiplayer online battle arena (MOBA) games, showing that a parameter-aware model predicts win rates and draft outcomes with accuracy comparable to patch-specific models, yet requires zero adaptation when a new patch is released. Our framework further enables counterfactual analysis—e.g., "what if this ability's cooldown were reduced by two seconds?"—allowing stakeholders to simulate patch changes before deployment. This work bridges game design theory and esports analytics, offering a scalable, patch-agnostic methodology that reduces analytical overhead while deepening insight into the mechanics that drive competition.

title: EDIT: Exemplar-Domain Aware Image-to-Image Translation
text_ai: Image-to-image translation is to convert an image of the certain style to another of the target style with the content preserved. A desired translator should be capable to generate diverse results in a controllable (many-to-many) fashion. To this end, we design a novel generative adversarial network, namely exemplar-domain aware image-to-image translator (EDIT for short). EDIT takes advantage of both exemplar images, which provide style guidance, and domain-level knowledge, which ensures semantic consistency across the target domain. The generator is conditioned on a style code extracted from a reference exemplar, while a domain-aware discriminator enforces alignment with global domain statistics. This design enables zero-shot translation to unseen styles by simply feeding different exemplars, and supports multimodal generation via stochastic sampling of style codes. To realize many-to-many mappings without paired data, we introduce a cross-cycle consistency loss that disentangles content and style, and an exemplar-domain contrastive loss that pulls together feature representations of similar styles while pushing apart those of different domains. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that EDIT outperforms existing methods in both translation quality and diversity. Moreover, the controllability of the model is confirmed through style interpolation and exemplar swapping, where users can smoothly transition between styles or blend characteristics from multiple exemplars. These results validate that explicit integration of exemplar and domain information is crucial for achieving flexible, high-fidelity image translation.

title: When does proton pump inhibitor treatment become long term? A scoping review.
text_ai: Proton pump inhibitor (PPI) use has risen substantially, primarily driven by ongoing use over months to years. However, there is no consensus on how to define long-term PPI use. Our objectives were to review and compare definitions of long-term PPI use in existing literature and describe the rationale for each definition. We conducted a scoping review following the Joanna Briggs Institute methodology and PRISMA-ScR guidelines. A systematic search of MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL, and Cochrane Library was performed from inception to January 2023. Studies were included if they explicitly defined long-term PPI use or provided a threshold for duration. Two reviewers independently screened titles, abstracts, and full texts, with disagreements resolved by consensus. Data on definitions, including duration thresholds, cumulative dose, or other operational criteria, were extracted along with any stated rationale. From 1,247 unique records, 89 studies met inclusion criteria. Definitions of long-term PPI use varied substantially, with duration thresholds ranging from 30 days to more than 12 months. The most common threshold was 90 days (28%), followed by 180 days (19%) and 365 days (15%). Some studies defined long-term use based on prescription counts (e.g., ≥3 prescriptions over 6 months) or cumulative defined daily doses exceeding 90. Others used clinical criteria such as continuous use for a specified period without a clear indication for discontinuation. Only 12 studies (13%) provided a rationale for their chosen definition, often citing expert opinion, guideline recommendations, or arbitrary cutoffs from prior research. The lack of consensus on a definition of long-term PPI use underscores significant heterogeneity in the literature, complicating comparisons across studies and clinical interpretation. Standardized definitions are needed to facilitate consistent research, guide deprescribing efforts, and evaluate the benefits versus harms of prolonged PPI therapy. Future work should prioritize evidence-based definitions that account for both duration and clinical context.

title: On performance bound estimation in NMPC with time-varying terminal cost
text_ai: Model predictive control (MPC) schemes are commonly designed with fixed, i.e., time-invariant, horizon length and cost functions. If no stabilizing terminal ingredients are used, stability can be guaranteed via a sufficiently long horizon. A suboptimality index can be derived that gives bounds on the performance of the MPC law over an infinite-horizon (IH). This paper extends such analysis to nonlinear MPC (NMPC) with time-varying terminal cost. We define a suboptimality index as the worst-case ratio of finite-horizon to infinite-horizon costs and propose a method for estimating its upper bound, leveraging the structure of the time-varying cost. The bound is derived using a dynamic programming argument and can be computed offline or adapted online. We show that the time-varying terminal cost yields tighter performance bounds compared to constant terminal costs, particularly when the terminal cost is updated based on the current state. Numerical simulations on a nonlinear example demonstrate that the proposed bound accurately captures the worst-case performance loss, and that the time-varying cost can reduce it significantly, allowing for shorter horizon lengths. Crucially, stability is maintained under mild conditions on the terminal cost variation. This work thus provides a principled framework for performance bound estimation in NMPC with time-varying terminal ingredients.

title: The ileal FGF15/19 to hepatic FGFR4 axis regulates liver regeneration after partial hepatectomy in mice.
text_ai: Fibroblast growth factor (FGF) has been considered to modulate liver regeneration (LR) after partial hepatectomy (PH) at the tissue level. Previous studies have demonstrated that FGF15 and FGF19 induce the activation of its receptor, FGF receptor 4 (FGFR4), which can promote hepatocellular carcinoma progression and regulate liver lipid metabolism. Here, we investigated the functional role of the enterohepatic FGF15/19–FGFR4 signaling axis in the early regenerative response following 70% PH in mice. Using a combination of conditional knockout models and pharmacological inhibition, we demonstrate that specific deletion of FGFR4 in hepatocytes significantly impaired hepatocyte DNA synthesis and mitotic progression at 36–48 h post-PH, correlating with reduced expression of cyclin D1 and proliferating cell nuclear antigen. Conversely, exogenous administration of recombinant FGF19 or adenoviral overexpression of FGF15 in the ileum robustly enhanced LR, as evidenced by increased Ki67-positive nuclei and restoration of liver mass within 5 days. Mechanistically, the proliferative effect was dependent on FGFR4-mediated activation of the extracellular signal-regulated kinase 1/2 and signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 pathways, but not on β‑catenin or yes‑associated protein signaling. Notably, ileal Fgf15 mRNA levels were acutely upregulated within 2 h after PH, preceding the peak of hepatocyte proliferation, and this induction was abolished by bile acid sequestration or gut‑specific farnesoid X receptor deletion. Taken together, our findings establish that the ileal FGF15/19–hepatic FGFR4 axis is a critical regulator of the priming phase of LR, acting through a gut–liver endocrine circuit. Targeting this pathway may offer therapeutic strategies to enhance hepatic regeneration in patients undergoing partial hepatectomy or living‑donor liver transplantation.

title: Bordetella biofilms: a lifestyle leading to persistent infections.
text_ai: Bordetella bronchiseptica and B. pertussis are Gram-negative bacteria that cause respiratory diseases in animals and humans. The current incidence of whooping cough or pertussis caused by B. pertussis has reached levels not observed since the 1950s. Although pertussis is traditionally known as an acute childhood disease, it has recently resurged in vaccinated adolescents and adults. Biofilm formation by these pathogens is increasingly recognized as a key mechanism underlying their capacity to establish persistent infections and evade host immune responses. In this review, we synthesize current knowledge on the genetic regulation, structural composition, and environmental cues that drive Bordetella biofilm development. Both species produce a polysaccharide-rich matrix and express surface adhesins, such as filamentous hemagglutinin and fimbriae, that are critical for interbacterial aggregation and attachment to respiratory epithelium. Importantly, biofilms of B. pertussis and B. bronchiseptica exhibit enhanced tolerance to antibiotics and resistance to phagocytosis, correlating with prolonged colonization in animal models. We further discuss evidence that biofilm-associated bacteria display a distinct transcriptional program, including upregulation of virulence factors and quorum-sensing systems, which may contribute to the failure of current acellular vaccines to prevent carriage and transmission. Finally, we highlight open questions regarding biofilm heterogeneity, host-pathogen interplay during chronic infection, and the potential for anti-biofilm strategies to improve pertussis control.

title: A Virtual Quantum Network Prototype for Open Access
text_ai: The rise of quantum networks has revolutionized domains such as communication, sensing, and cybersecurity. Despite this progress, current quantum network systems remain limited in scale, are highly application-specific (e.g., for quantum key distribution), and lack a clear road map for global expansion. To address these limitations, we present an open-access virtual quantum network prototype. It virtualizes hardware resources into a software-defined platform, enabling modular protocol stacks for entanglement distribution, error correction, and repeaters. By decoupling the control plane from the physical layer, the prototype facilitates rapid experimentation with various network topologies and protocol stacks. We demonstrate the prototype on a city-scale topology with multiple concurrent users running quantum key distribution, distributed quantum computing, and quantum sensing tasks. Performance evaluation shows entanglement generation rates within 10% of idealized physical models while maintaining low overhead. The prototype is released as an open-source platform, allowing users to design, test, and validate quantum network algorithms without dedicated hardware. This work provides a foundational step toward a global quantum internet by offering a scalable, application-agnostic, and freely accessible testbed for the community.

title: A tutorial on individualized treatment effect prediction from randomized trials with a binary endpoint
text_ai: Randomized trials typically estimate average relative treatment effects, but decisions on the benefit of a treatment are possibly better informed by more individualized predictions of the absolute treatment effect. In case of a binary outcome, these predictions of absolute individualized treatment effect require knowledge of the individual's risk without treatment and incorporation of a possibly differential treatment effect (i.e. effect modification by baseline patient characteristics). This tutorial provides a comprehensive step-by-step guide to deriving such predictions from randomized trial data. We first define the targeted estimand: the absolute risk difference for a given individual. We then review approaches for modeling baseline risk, including logistic regression with restricted cubic splines or fractional polynomials to capture nonlinear effects. For the differential effect, we consider models that include treatment-by-covariate interactions, which may be limited to key effect modifiers a priori or selected via penalized methods. We discuss trade-offs between model complexity and interpretability. Internal validation techniques, such as bootstrap optimism correction, are demonstrated to assess predictive performance. Discrimination and calibration metrics are explained. A detailed case study using a publicly available trial is presented, with R code provided in the online supplement. We highlight common pitfalls, such as optimism when the same data are used for model development and evaluation, and methods to mitigate it. We also discuss the importance of model selection and external validation. The tutorial concludes with practical advice for communicating predictions to clinicians and patients, emphasizing uncertainty intervals and the need for external validation in similar populations. This enables researchers to generate personalized benefit estimates for informed clinical decision-making.

title: Basal and stimulated calcitonin levels in patients with type 2 diabetes did not change during 1 year of Liraglutide treatment.
text_ai: The administration of Liraglutide, a long-acting GLP-1 receptor (GLP-1R) agonist, is associated with C-cell adenomas and carcinomas in rats. In humans, GLP-1R is highly expressed in C-cells hyperplasia (CCH) and in medullary thyroid cancer (MTC), though no changes in basal serum calcitonin (bCT) levels were recorded in type 2 diabetic (T2DM) patients treated with Liraglutide. However, the impact of Liraglutide on stimulated calcitonin (sCT) release—a more sensitive marker of C-cell activation—remains poorly characterized in this population. This prospective, single-center study investigated whether 52 weeks of Liraglutide therapy (1.8 mg/day) alters both bCT and sCT levels in T2DM patients without known thyroid disease. Fifty-four adults (mean age 58.4±7.9 years; 48% male; HbA1c 8.1±0.9%) underwent standardized pentagastrin stimulation testing (0.5 μg/kg intravenously) at baseline and after 12 and 52 weeks of treatment. Serum calcitonin was measured by a two-site chemiluminescent immunoassay (detection limit 0.5 pg/mL). At baseline, median bCT was 3.1 (IQR 1.9–5.2) pg/mL, and peak sCT (sCTmax) was 9.8 (6.4–16.3) pg/mL. After 52 weeks, bCT remained stable at 3.0 (1.7–5.0) pg/mL, and sCTmax was 10.1 (6.1–17.0) pg/mL (both p>0.05 vs. baseline). No patient developed a pathological rise in bCT (>10 pg/mL in males, >5 pg/mL in females) or sCTmax (>30 pg/mL) during follow-up. Furthermore, subgroup analyses by age, sex, diabetes duration, and baseline HbA1c revealed no significant predictors of calcitonin change. These findings demonstrate that long-term Liraglutide treatment does not stimulate C-cell activity in T2DM patients, supporting the clinical safety of GLP-1R agonists regarding thyroid C-cell proliferation in humans. Larger studies incorporating serial thyroid ultrasound and longer exposure are warranted to exclude rare events.

title: Time-dependent electron transport through a strongly correlated quantum dot: multiple-probe open boundary conditions approach
text_ai: We present a time-dependent study of electron transport through a strongly correlated quantum dot. The time-dependent current is obtained with the multiple-probe battery method, while adiabatic lattice density functional theory in the Bethe ansatz local-density approximation to the Hubbard model describes the dot electronic structure. We apply this framework to study the transient and steady-state currents following a sudden switch-on of a bias voltage. The multiple-probe method introduces auxiliary reservoirs that mimic open boundaries, enabling a fully time-dependent description without artificial reflections. Within the adiabatic approximation, the self-consistent potential is updated at each time step using the instantaneous density from the Bethe ansatz local-density approximation, which exactly reproduces the thermodynamics of the one-dimensional Hubbard model. For a quantum dot in the Coulomb blockade regime, we examine how the time-dependent current evolves as the interaction strength and dot level position are varied. Our results reveal that the transient current exhibits distinct signatures of interaction-induced correlations, including a delayed onset of the Kondo resonance in the strong-coupling limit. The steady-state current obtained in the long-time limit agrees well with exact results from the numerical renormalization group, validating the accuracy of the adiabatic approach even for moderate bias voltages. We further analyze the role of the number of multiple probes and the relaxation time, demonstrating convergence to the physically correct open-system dynamics. The method provides a computationally efficient route to simulate real-time transport through strongly correlated nanostructures, capturing both transient phenomena and the approach to the nonequilibrium steady state.

title: Improving Zero-Shot Cross-Lingual Transfer via Progressive Code-Switching
text_ai: Code-switching is a data augmentation scheme mixing words from multiple languages into source lingual text. It has achieved considerable generalization performance of cross-lingual transfer tasks by aligning cross-lingual contextual word representations. However, uncontrolled and over-replaced code-switching would augment dirty samples to model training. To mitigate this issue, we propose a progressive code-switching strategy that gradually increases the replacement ratio during training, thereby preventing the model from being overwhelmed by noisy cross-lingual alignments early on. Specifically, our method begins with a low code-switching rate that preserves source-language fluency, then linearly or non-linearly raises the replacement ratio over training steps. This schedule allows the model to first learn robust monolingual representations before gradually adapting to mixed-language contexts. We evaluate our approach on several zero-shot cross-lingual classification benchmarks, including sentiment analysis and topic classification, using multilingual BERT as the backbone. Empirical results show that progressive code-switching consistently outperforms static code-switching baselines, achieving up to 3.5% relative improvement in accuracy on target languages unseen during fine-tuning. Furthermore, analyses reveal that the progressive schedule reduces the variance of cross-lingual representation alignment across tokens, leading to more stable and effective transfer. Our work demonstrates that controlling the injection of code-switched data with a strategic training schedule is a simple yet effective enhancement for zero-shot cross-lingual transfer, and it can be easily integrated into existing augmentation pipelines without additional model complexity.

title: Device-Independent Bit Commitment based on the CHSH Inequality
text_ai: Bit commitment and coin flipping occupy a unique place in the device-independent landscape, as the only device-independent protocols thus far suggested for these tasks are reliant on tripartite GHZ correlations. Indeed, we know of no other bipartite tasks, which admit a device-independent formulation, but which are not known to be implementable using only bipartite nonlocality. Here, we present the first device-independent bit commitment protocol based solely on bipartite nonlocality, specifically the CHSH inequality. Our protocol achieves composable security against quantum adversaries when implemented with a non-signaling adversary model, leveraging the intrinsic randomness of CHSH violations to enforce binding and hiding. Security is established through a novel entropy accumulation argument that does not require tripartite correlations, proving that any cheating strategy must break the non-signaling constraints. The protocol's key advantage lies in its experimental feasibility, as bipartite Bell tests are significantly simpler to realize than GHZ experiments. This result demonstrates that bipartite nonlocality suffices for cryptographic tasks previously thought to require more complex resources, bridging a long-standing gap in the device-independent toolkit.
