title: Fractal Profit Landscape of the Stock Market
text_ai: We investigate the structure of the profit landscape obtained from the most basic, fluctuation based, trading strategy applied for the daily stock price data. The strategy is parameterized by only two variables, p and q. Stocks are sold and bought if the log return is bigger than p and less than -q, respectively. We analyze the resulting profit as a function of p and q using daily stock data from major exchanges over several years. The profit landscape exhibits a rich multiscale structure characterized by fractal scaling and self-similarity. In particular, we observe that the profit function displays power-law behavior over a range of thresholds, with exponents that vary across stocks and time periods. Using multifractal analysis, we quantify the degree of complexity and identify regimes where profit is robust or sensitive to parameter choices. The fractal nature of the landscape suggests that no single optimal parameter set exists; rather, profitable regions are interconnected across scales. This has implications for the design of adaptive trading strategies. Our findings provide a novel geometric perspective on market microstructure and the limits of simple trading rules.

title: A Trust and Reputation System for IoT Exploiting Distributed Ledger Technology
text_ai: The advent of Bitcoin, and consequently Blockchain, has ushered in a new era of decentralization. Blockchain enables mutually distrusting entities to work collaboratively to attain a common objective. However, current Blockchain technologies lack scalability, which limits their use in Internet of Things (IoT) applications. To address these limitations, we propose a lightweight trust and reputation framework built upon a directed acyclic graph (DAG)-based distributed ledger, specifically tailored for resource-constrained IoT environments. By replacing energy-intensive consensus mechanisms with a more efficient, layered validation process, our system achieves near-instant finality and linear scalability as the network grows. Each IoT device maintains and propagates trust scores derived from direct interactions and aggregated peer endorsements, which are immutably recorded on the ledger without requiring full-chain replication. The reputation model incorporates decay factors and Sybil attack resilience, ensuring robustness against malicious behaviors. Simulation results demonstrate that our approach reduces latency by over 60% compared to conventional blockchain-based solutions while maintaining trust accuracy above 95% under adversarial conditions. Furthermore, the system’s modular design allows seamless integration with existing IoT protocols. This work bridges the gap between decentralized security and practical IoT deployment, enabling trustworthy autonomous interactions among heterogeneous devices.

title: YouTube as a source of patient information for stroke: A content-quality and an audience engagement analysis.
text_ai: Stroke is the second leading cause of death worldwide following ischemic heart disease, and the fifth in the United States. The video-sharing database, YouTube, is the second most popular visited website with more than 2 billion users, thus it's increasingly being used as a medium for delivering health information. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of the 100 most-viewed YouTube videos on stroke, retrieved using the keywords “stroke,” “stroke symptoms,” and “stroke treatment.” Two independent reviewers assessed each video for medical accuracy, completeness, and reliability using the modified DISCERN instrument and the Journal of the American Medical Association (JAMA) benchmarks. Audience engagement was measured through view count, likes, dislikes, comments, and the Video Power Index (VPI). Videos were categorized by source: academic/medical institutions, health information websites, independent users, and commercial entities. Of the 100 videos, only 34% were deemed medically accurate and 22% adhered to all JAMA criteria. Academic sources, though less numerous (12%), scored highest in quality (mean DISCERN 4.2/5) but attracted only 18% of total views. Conversely, user-generated and commercial videos accrued the highest engagement (mean VPI 89.4) yet frequently contained incomplete or misleading information. A moderate inverse correlation was observed between video popularity and content reliability (Spearman’s ρ = −0.31, p < 0.01). These findings highlight a critical gap: the most-watched YouTube content on stroke often lacks evidence-based rigor, potentially endangering public health. Future interventions should consider promoting reliable, engaging video formats from credible sources, and integrating platform-level quality indicators.

title: Local Decorrelation For Improved Detection
text_ai: Even with the advent of more sophisticated, data-hungry methods, boosted decision trees remain extraordinarily successful for fast rigid object detection, achieving top accuracy on numerous datasets. While effective, most boosted detectors use decision trees with orthogonal (single feature) splits, and the topology of the resulting decision boundary may not be well matched to the natural topology of the data. We introduce a local decorrelation transform that is applied to the feature space prior to each split in the tree. This transform linearly remaps the local data distribution to a canonical coordinate system where the axes are uncorrelated, thereby allowing subsequent orthogonal splits to better approximate the natural, often oblique, decision boundaries present in the data. The transform is learned rapidly from the sample covariance within the current node and adds negligible overhead during both training and testing. On standard face and pedestrian detection benchmarks, the proposed Local Decorrelated Boosted Trees consistently outperform conventional orthogonal-split boosting, achieving higher average precision with fewer weak learners. Moreover, the method complements modern deep-learning pipelines as a fast, interpretable alternative for resource-constrained applications. Our experiments demonstrate that simple orthogonal splits, when augmented with local decorrelation, become remarkably effective at capturing the underlying manifold structure of visual object classes.

title: Space of initial conditions and universality in nonequilibrium quantum dynamics
text_ai: We study analytically the role of initial conditions in nonequilibrium quantum dynamics considering the one-dimensional ferromagnets in the regime of spontaneously broken symmetry. We analyze the expectation value of local operators for the infinite-dimensional space of initial conditions of domain wall type, generally intended as initial conditions spatially interpolating between two different ground states. We derive exact expressions for the time evolution of the order parameter using a combination of Bethe ansatz and hydrodynamic projection techniques. The results reveal a remarkable universality: despite the infinite-dimensional nature of the initial space, the late-time dynamics is governed by a single scaling function of the ray variable x/t, independent of the detailed shape of the domain wall. This universality is traced to the fact that only the net topological charge and a single width parameter survive in the scaling limit, with all other details washed out by ballistic transport. Our analysis further demonstrates that the approach to the scaling regime is controlled by power-law corrections with universal exponents, providing a complete classification of the space of initial conditions under renormalization-group flow. These findings establish a deep connection between integrability, topological conservation, and universality in far-from-equilibrium quantum systems.

title: Extracting black-hole rotational energy: The generalized Penrose process
text_ai: In the case involving particles the necessary and sufficient condition for the Penrose process to extract energy from a rotating black hole is absorption of particles with negative energies and angular momenta. No torque at the black-hole horizon occurs. However, this particle-based mechanism is limited to discrete events where negative-energy particles must be created within the ergosphere. The generalized Penrose process extends this to classical and quantum fields, enabling continuous energy extraction via superradiant scattering. Incident waves with appropriate frequencies and angular momenta are amplified upon reflection from the black hole, drawing rotational energy from the ergosphere. The condition for amplification mirrors the particle case: the incident mode must have frequency ω less than mΩ, where m is the azimuthal quantum number and Ω the black hole's angular velocity. No net torque is exerted on the horizon, as angular momentum extracted is balanced by the field's flux. This process offers a robust mechanism for energy extraction in astrophysical contexts, such as accretion disks or magnetospheres. It connects to fundamental physics, including black hole thermodynamics and the no-hair theorem. Studies show efficiency up to 20% in converting rotational energy into radiation. This abstract highlights that absorption of negative-energy objects, whether particles or waves, is key to extracting black-hole rotational energy, with torque-free horizon preserved across formulations. Implications for astrophysical observation and experimental verification are discussed, for gamma-ray bursts and active galactic nuclei.

title: The Quest for Omnioculars: Embedded Visualization for Augmenting Basketball Game Viewing Experiences
text_ai: Sports game data is becoming increasingly complex, often consisting of multivariate data such as player performance stats, historical team records, and athletes' positional tracking information. While numerous visual analytics systems have been developed for sports analysts to derive insights, few tools target fans to improve their understanding and engagement of sports data during live games. We propose Omnioculars, a novel embedded visualization system that overlays real-time, contextually relevant game data directly onto the live broadcast or augmented reality view of basketball games. By integrating multivariate player statistics, play-by-play events, and spatial tracking data into the visual field, the system enables fans to access insights without disrupting their natural viewing experience. The design was iteratively developed through participatory workshops with both casual and avid basketball followers, leading to a set of visual encodings and interaction techniques that prioritize readability, minimal cognitive load, and seamless blending with the game action. A controlled experiment with 30 participants compared Omnioculars against a conventional game dashboard and a no-augmentation baseline. Results indicate significant improvements in fans’ ability to recall and reason about player performance, team dynamics, and strategic patterns, while maintaining high levels of engagement and enjoyment. Subjective feedback also highlighted the system’s potential to deepen narrative understanding and foster social discussions during live viewing. We discuss design implications for embedded sports visualization, including trade-offs between information density and visual clutter, as well as the role of personalization in adapting to varying levels of fan expertise. Omnioculars represents a step toward making complex sports analytics accessible and intuitive for the broad audience of live spectators.

title: Green Segment Routing for Improved Sustainability of Backbone Networks
text_ai: Improving the energy efficiency of Internet Service Provider (ISP) backbone networks is an important objective for ISP operators. In these networks, the overall traffic load throughout the day can vary drastically, resulting in many backbone networks being highly overprovisioned during periods of lower traffic volume. Despite this overprovisioning, current routing protocols often maintain all network elements fully active, leading to unnecessary energy consumption. This paper proposes a green routing framework based on Segment Routing (SR) that dynamically adapts the network’s active topology to current traffic demands while preserving robust forwarding and fast failure recovery. We formulate the energy-aware traffic engineering problem as an optimization that minimizes the number of powered-on line cards and routers, subject to capacity, fairness, and resilience constraints. Using realistic traffic matrices from a major European ISP and a detailed power model of modern router hardware, we evaluate our approach via extensive simulations. Results show that our SR-based scheme reduces network energy consumption by up to 30% during low-traffic periods compared to conventional per-destination shortest-path routing. Crucially, these savings are achieved without degrading quality of service or violating service-level agreements. The work demonstrates that Segment Routing provides the necessary flexibility and programmability to realize sustainable backbone operations, offering a practical path toward greener ISP networks.

title: Impact of QCD jets and heavy-quark production in cosmic-ray proton atmospheric showers up to 10$^{20}$ eV
text_ai: The PYTHIA 6 Monte Carlo (MC) event generator, commonly used in collider physics, is interfaced for the first time with a fast transport simulation of a hydrogen atmosphere, with the same density as air, in order to study the properties of extended atmospheric showers (EAS) produced by cosmic ray protons with energies E$_{CR}\approx 10^{14}$--$10^{20}$ eV. We present the first detailed investigation of how QCD jets and heavy-quark production influence the development of extensive air showers from cosmic-ray protons. By interfacing PYTHIA 6 with a custom one-dimensional transport code for a hydrogen-equivalent atmosphere, we simulate showers from 10^14 to 10^20 eV. Our analysis reveals that heavy-flavor decays, particularly from bottom and charm quarks, significantly enhance the muon component at large lateral distances, with muon numbers increasing by up to 30% at 1000 m from the core. Jet fragmentation shifts the depth of shower maximum (Xmax) deeper by approximately 20 g/cm^2 and increases event-by-event fluctuations relative to simulations without jet substructure. These effects become pronounced above 10^18 eV, where heavy-flavor processes dominate muon production. We benchmark our results against standard models (QGSJET, EPOS-LHC) and find that PYTHIA 6 predicts a higher muon content, partially addressing the muon deficit observed in ultra-high-energy cosmic-ray experiments. The interface also enables studies of parton distribution function and renormalization scale uncertainties. This work bridges collider and cosmic-ray physics, demonstrating that QCD-based generators are essential for accurate air shower modeling and for interpreting data from observatories like the Pierre Auger Observatory. Future work will extend this analysis to nuclear primaries and include detector effects.

title: Semi-Interpenetrating Cooperative Localization in Connected Vehicle Networks
text_ai: We proposed a fusion mechanism for the distributed cooperative map matching (CMM) within the vehicular ad-hoc network. This mechanism makes the information from each node reachable within the network by other nodes without direct communication, thus improving the overall localization accuracy and robustness. By leveraging a semi-interpenetrating network architecture, the proposed fusion mechanism enables layered information propagation across overlapping subnetworks, effectively reducing latency and communication overhead. Each node maintains a local map of road geometry and infrastructure features, which is iteratively fused with decentralized peer measurements from neighboring vehicles via a consensus-based algorithm. This approach mitigates the reliance on fixed infrastructure and addresses the challenge of intermittent connectivity inherent in vehicular ad-hoc networks. The semi-interpenetrating structure ensures that even partially connected clusters can share critical location updates through bridging nodes, thereby preventing localization divergence during network fragmentation. Simulation results under realistic urban mobility scenarios demonstrate a notable improvement in positioning accuracy—up to 35% compared to conventional decentralized CMM methods—while maintaining robustness against GPS outages and sensor noise. Furthermore, the fusion mechanism adapts dynamically to varying vehicle densities and traffic speeds, ensuring scalability without compromising real-time performance.

title: Successful intra-class switching among IL-17 antagonists: a multicentre, multinational, retrospective study.
text_ai: IL-17 blockers are among the newer anti-psoriatic treatment options and little is known about the interclass switching. We have thus initiated a multi-center, multi-national, retrospective study to assess the treatment response of patients who were switched from one IL-17 blocker to another. Data were collected from 12 dermatology departments across five European and North American countries. Inclusion criteria required adult patients with moderate-to-severe plaque psoriasis who had been switched from one IL-17 blocker (secukinumab, ixekizumab, or brodalumab) to another due to primary or secondary failure, or adverse events. Efficacy was assessed by PASI at baseline, 12–16 weeks post-switch, and last follow-up. The primary endpoint was PASI90 at week 16; secondary endpoints included PASI75, PASI100, and drug survival. Safety was monitored. A total of 147 patients were identified. Mean age was 45 years, 60% male. The most common first-line IL-17 blocker was secukinumab (55%); the most common switch was from secukinumab to ixekizumab (42%). At week 16, 68% achieved PASI90 and 82% achieved PASI75. At last follow-up (mean 9 months), 85% of initial responders maintained PASI90. Drug survival at 6 months was 81%. Adverse events were mild and led to discontinuation in only 4% of cases. These real-world data demonstrate that interclass switching among IL-17 blockers is a successful strategy. The high response rates suggest that differential binding profiles may confer clinical benefit even after failure of a first IL-17 antagonist, supporting the clinical practice of interclass switching and warranting prospective investigation.

title: Multiple single-photon generations in three-level atoms coupled to cavity with non-Markovian effects
text_ai: In this paper, we show how to generate the multiple single-photon wavepackets of arbitrary temporal shape from an optical cavity coupled with $N$ three-level atoms driven by a driving field in the non-Markovian regime. We employ a quantum trajectory approach to analyze the dynamics of the system, focusing on the non-Markovian feedback arising from the structured reservoir of the cavity. By engineering the driving field and the atom–cavity coupling, we demonstrate that multiple single-photon wavepackets can be efficiently generated with high fidelity, even in the presence of memory effects. Our method leverages the ladder-type three-level atoms to mediate controlled photon emission, where the driving field acts as a tunable source of coherence. We derive an effective master equation that accounts for the finite correlation time of the reservoir, enabling precise shaping of the temporal profiles. Numerical simulations reveal that the non-Markovian dynamics can enhance the generation rate and suppress detrimental decoherence, allowing for the creation of wavepackets with arbitrary envelopes. Furthermore, we show that the scheme is robust against parameter fluctuations and can be scaled to larger atomic ensembles. This work provides a practical pathway for deterministic on-demand sources of non-classical light, crucial for quantum information processing and communication networks. Our results bridge the gap between non-Markovian cavity QED and photonic quantum state engineering, offering new insights into controlling light–matter interactions beyond the Markovian approximation.

title: Being a real nurse: A secondary qualitative analysis of how public health nurses rework their work identities.
text_ai: Many Western nations are emphasizing the importance of population health across health care delivery organizations and education systems. Despite significant momentum to integrate population health into nursing practice, a parallel effort to examine how these efforts impact practicing nurses' views of their professional role and work identity has not occurred. This secondary qualitative analysis addresses that gap by reanalyzing 28 semi-structured interviews with public health nurses from a prior study. Using thematic analysis guided by a social constructionist framework, we examined how nurses described their professional roles and the strategies they employed to reconcile population health mandates with established clinical identities. Three identity reworking strategies emerged: anchoring in hands-on care, expanding the clinical lens, and defending the specialty. Nurses navigated tensions between institutional expectations of population health work and their own desires to maintain a sense of “real nursing” tied to direct patient contact. Findings reveal that while population health integration offers opportunities for role expansion, it simultaneously threatens nurses’ professional authenticity. These dynamics have implications for nursing education, workforce policy, and organizational support structures aimed at sustaining a robust public health nursing identity.

title: Decoding and Reconstructing the Focus of Spatial Attention from the Topography of Alpha-band Oscillations.
text_ai: Many aspects of perception and cognition are supported by activity in neural populations that are tuned to different stimulus features (e.g., orientation, spatial location, color). Goal-directed behavior, such as sustained attention, requires a mechanism for the selective prioritization of contextually appropriate representations. Here, we demonstrate that the topography of alpha-band (8-12 Hz) oscillatory activity over visual and parietal cortices contains sufficient information to decode and reconstruct the locus of covert spatial attention in humans. Using electroencephalography (EEG) recordings from participants performing a sustained spatial attention task, we applied a multivariate pattern analysis framework to alpha-band power maps across trials. We show that a linear decoder can reliably classify the attended location among four cardinal positions (left, right, upper, lower) with above-chance accuracy, achieving peak performance approximately 300–600 ms after cue onset. Moreover, we employed a forward encoding model to reconstruct the full spatial profile of the attentional focus from the distributed pattern of alpha-band topography. Reconstructed attention maps exhibited a clear peak at the cued location, with a spatial resolution on the order of several degrees of visual angle. Critically, the topography of posterior alpha power showed a contralateral decrease relative to the attended hemifield, consistent with the well-known alpha lateralization effect, yet the decoding and reconstruction benefits extended beyond this univariate signature. Our results suggest that the spatial structure of alpha-band activity reflects a continuous, graded representation of attentional priority rather than a simple binary hemifield bias. These findings provide a methodological framework for non-invasively tracking the dynamic allocation of spatial attention in real time, with potential applications in brain-computer interfaces and clinical assessments of attentional function.

title: Graphene field effect transistors as room-temperature Terahertz detectors
text_ai: The unique optoelectronic properties of graphene [1] make it an ideal platform for a variety of photonic applications [2], including fast photodetectors [3], transparent electrodes [4], optical modulators [5], and ultra-fast lasers [6]. While graphene’s broadband absorption spans from ultraviolet to terahertz (THz) frequencies, its inherently low optical cross-section in the THz range has historically limited direct photodetection efficiency. Field-effect transistors (FETs) based on graphene circumvent this limitation by exploiting the strong field dependence of the material’s charge carrier density and mobility. In such devices, incident THz radiation couples to the channel via a gate-coupled antenna or through rectification of the radiation-induced ac voltage, enabling detection via the photothermoelectric effect or bolometric response. Here, we demonstrate graphene FETs that operate as sensitive THz detectors at room temperature, achieving a responsivity exceeding 1 A/W and a noise-equivalent power below 10 nW/√Hz across the 0.3–3 THz band. The devices leverage a high-mobility chemical vapor deposition (CVD) graphene channel on a high-κ dielectric substrate, combined with an integrated log-periodic antenna to efficiently couple the incoming radiation. Systematic characterization reveals that the detector performance scales with both the carrier mobility and the asymmetry of the contact work functions, with optimal operation achieved near the charge neutrality point. These results position graphene FETs as a viable, scalable platform for uncooled THz sensing in applications ranging from security imaging to non-destructive testing.

title: When Prompt Engineering Meets Software Engineering: CNL-P as Natural and Robust "APIs'' for Human-AI Interaction
text_ai: With the growing capabilities of large language models (LLMs), they are increasingly applied in areas like intelligent customer service, code generation, and knowledge management. Natural language (NL) prompts act as the ``APIs'' for human-LLM interaction. To improve prompt quality, best practices for prompt engineering (PE) have been developed, including writing guidelines and templates. However, these practices often fall short when prompts must be composed by domain experts without deep AI knowledge, or when they need to be robust across diverse LLM versions and contexts. In software engineering, APIs provide clear, structured contracts between components; we argue that prompt engineering similarly requires a systematic, contract-based approach. This paper introduces Controlled Natural Language for Prompts (CNL-P), a formalism that treats prompts as well-defined interfaces with syntactic and semantic constraints. CNL-P offers a limited yet expressive vocabulary and grammar, enabling domain experts to construct prompts that are both natural for humans and machine-parsable for LLMs. By defining prompt templates as reusable components with explicit input/output specifications, CNL-P mitigates fragility caused by ad-hoc wording and reduces reliance on iterative trial-and-error. We evaluate CNL-P across three tasks: customer intent classification, code summarization, and knowledge retrieval. Results show that CNL-P-based prompts achieve higher accuracy and consistency compared to free-form prompts and conventional templates, while also reducing the number of required revisions. Moreover, CNL-P exhibits superior robustness when subjected to paraphrasing attacks and model updates. Our findings suggest that adopting CNL-P as a standard interface can bridge the gap between prompt engineering and software engineering, promoting the development of reliable, maintainable, and composable human-AI interaction systems.

title: REPOSE: Distributed Top-k Trajectory Similarity Search with Local Reference Point Tries
text_ai: Trajectory similarity computation is a fundamental component in a variety of real-world applications, such as ridesharing, road planning, and transportation optimization. Recent advances in mobile devices have enabled an unprecedented increase in the amount of available trajectory data such that efficient query processing can no longer be supported by a single machine. To address this scalability challenge, we propose REPOSE, a distributed framework for top-k trajectory similarity search. At its core, REPOSE introduces a novel index structure, the Local Reference Point Trie (LRPT), which partitions trajectories across a distributed cluster by mapping each trajectory to a fixed set of reference points and organizing them in compact tries. This design enables efficient local pruning and candidate generation without global data shuffling. The query processing follows a two-phase approach: each node independently computes its local top-k candidates using LRPT, and then a coordinator merges these results to derive the global top-k answers. Extensive experiments on real-world trajectory datasets show that REPOSE outperforms existing distributed methods by up to 10× in query latency while achieving high accuracy. Furthermore, it exhibits linear scalability with both data size and cluster scale, making it suitable for large-scale trajectory analytics.
prefix: Trajectory similarity computation is a fundamental component in a variety of real-world applications, such as ridesharing, road planning, and transportation optimization. Recent advances in mobile devices have enabled an unprecedented increase in the amount of available trajectory data such that efficient query processing can no longer be supported by a single machine.

title: Current Predictive Indices and Nomograms To Enable Personalization of Radiation Therapy for Patients With Secondary Malignant Neoplasms of the Central Nervous System: A Review.
text_ai: The proper treatment of brain metastases continues to be a challenge for oncologists given the variability of individual patients' prognoses and the variety of treatment options available to address brain metasteses. There have been efforts since the 1990s to develop prognostic indices and nomograms to help clinicians determine the best approach for individuals with secondary malignant neoplasms of the central nervous system. This review examines the development, validation, and clinical utility of such indices, including the recursive partitioning analysis (RPA), graded prognostic assessment (GPA), and their disease-specific iterations, as well as nomograms incorporating molecular and genomic markers. We evaluate their performance in stratifying patients by survival, guiding selection of stereotactic radiosurgery, whole-brain radiotherapy, or combined modalities, and enabling personalized treatment plans. Recent advances integrating imaging biomarkers and machine learning are discussed. Despite progress, challenges remain in accounting for extracranial disease control and novel systemic therapies. The review underscores the need for dynamic, multifactorial models that adapt to modern treatment paradigms to optimize outcomes for this heterogeneous patient population.

title: DIViS: Domain Invariant Visual Servoing for Collision-Free Goal Reaching
text_ai: Robots should understand both semantics and physics to be functional in the real world. While robot platforms provide means for interacting with the physical world they cannot autonomously acquire object-level semantics without needing human. In this paper, we investigate how to minimize human effort and intervention to teach robots perform real world tasks that incorporate semantics. We propose DIViS, a Domain Invariant Visual Servoing framework that enables robots to reach semantic goals while avoiding collisions, all without requiring task-specific human demonstrations or reward engineering. Our key insight is to decouple semantic understanding from low-level control by learning a domain-invariant latent representation that maps visual observations from varied environments—simulated, real, or even with different object appearances—to a shared action space. This representation is trained via a self-supervised objective that encourages consistency across domains, using only a small set of unlabeled robot interaction episodes. For collision avoidance, we equip DIViS with a learned potential field that encodes obstacle geometry in the same latent space, allowing the servoing policy to naturally steer away from collisions while progressing toward the goal. The resulting controller operates in a closed-loop fashion, processing current camera images to predict next motor commands without explicit object detection or manual annotation. We evaluate DIViS in both simulated and real-world tabletop manipulation tasks, where the robot must reach diverse target objects (e.g., a cup, a toy block) while avoiding static and dynamic obstacles. Despite being trained solely on simulation data with random object textures and layouts, DIViS successfully transfers zero-shot to a real robot with a different camera and lighting, achieving over 90% goal-reaching success with zero collisions. These results demonstrate that our method minimizes human effort for semantic task specification, requiring only a brief, autonomous data collection phase and no human-labeled semantic labels or task-specific programming.

title: On the disappearance of a cold molecular torus around the low-luminosity active galactic nucleus of NGC 1097
text_ai: We used the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) to map the CO(3-2) and the underlying continuum emissions around the type 1 low-luminosity active galactic nucleus (LLAGN; bolometric luminosity $\lesssim 10^{42}$ erg~s$^{-1}$) of NGC 1097 at $\sim 10$ pc resolution. These observations revealed a detailed cold gas distribution within a $\sim 100$ pc of this LLAGN. The high angular resolution allowed us to disentangle the molecular gas kinematics and morphology. We find that the previously reported compact molecular torus—a key signature of the unified model for AGN—is absent in this LLAGN. Instead, the CO(3-2) emission is distributed in a diffuse, filamentary structure extending over tens of parsecs, with no evidence for a dense, rotating circumnuclear disk on scales below $20$ pc. The continuum emission at $0.9$ mm reveals a weak, unresolved core with a flux density consistent with a radiatively inefficient accretion flow. The missing molecular torus suggests a transition in the nuclear environment at low accretion rates. The cold gas reservoir within the sphere of influence of the supermassive black hole is insufficient to sustain a dusty torus, likely due to feedback from the weak jet or nuclear outflows. This challenges the universality of the torus in the unified model and implies that the covering factor decreases with decreasing AGN luminosity. Our results support a scenario where the torus disappears in LLAGNs, transitioning to a naked accretion flow. This demands a revision of the unified model for low-luminosity AGNs and motivates further high-resolution surveys.

title: FedNST: Federated Noisy Student Training for Automatic Speech Recognition
text_ai: Federated Learning (FL) enables training state-of-the-art Automatic Speech Recognition (ASR) models on user devices (clients) in distributed systems, hence preventing transmission of raw user data to a central server. A key challenge facing practical adoption of FL for ASR is obtaining ground-truth labels on the clients. Furthermore, the reliance on human annotation for each client's local data is often impractical due to privacy concerns and resource constraints. To address this, we propose Federated Noisy Student Training (FedNST), a semi-supervised learning framework that leverages abundant unlabeled speech data residing on client devices. In FedNST, a central server first trains a teacher ASR model on a small, centrally-labeled dataset. This teacher is then distributed to clients, where it generates soft pseudo-labels for their local unlabeled utterances. Clients subsequently train a student model on these pseudo-labeled samples while injecting noise (e.g., SpecAugment and dropout) to enforce consistency and robustness. Crucially, to handle the non-i.i.d. distribution of speech across clients and the inherent noise in pseudo-labels, we introduce a confidence-based filtering mechanism and a dynamic aggregation strategy on the server. Experiments on public benchmarks demonstrate that FedNST substantially outperforms standard FL baselines, achieving word error rates close to those of centrally-supervised models while maintaining data privacy. Our work establishes a practical pathway for deploying ASR in real-world, label-scarce federated environments.

title: Can Large Language Models Match Tutoring System Adaptivity? A Benchmarking Study
text_ai: Large Language Models (LLMs) hold promise as dynamic instructional aids. Yet, it remains unclear whether LLMs can replicate the adaptivity of intelligent tutoring systems (ITS)--where student knowledge and pedagogical strategies are explicitly modeled. We propose a prompt variation framework to assess LLM-generated instructional moves' adaptivity and pedagogical soundness across 75 real-world tutoring scenarios from an ITS. The framework systematically varies the prompt information provided to the LLM across three conditions: minimal (student's last answer only), partial (skill mastery probabilities), and full (complete student model and tutor policy). For each of the 75 scenarios, we generate LLM instructional moves and compare them to the ITS's original action using both automated metrics (e.g., next-step correctness, hint specificity) and expert human ratings of pedagogical quality. Our analysis reveals that LLMs exhibit modest adaptivity even with minimal information, often generating plausible next steps. However, their adaptivity significantly improves with full student model information, approaching but not surpassing ITS performance in some domains. Critically, pedagogical soundness—measured by alignment with theory-based scaffolding principles—remains a weakness: LLMs frequently provide direct answers or overly generic hints rather than targeted feedback. We also find that LLM adaptivity degrades rapidly in scenarios requiring multi-step reasoning sequencing or handling of common misconceptions. The results demonstrate that while LLMs can leverage student models to improve responsiveness, they rarely match the deliberate, structured adaptivity of expert-designed ITS policies. This benchmarking study provides a rigorous methodology for evaluating LLM-based tutoring and highlights fundamental gaps that must be addressed before LLMs can serve as autonomous adaptive tutors. We conclude by outlining key challenges for future research, including integrating explicit pedagogical models and improving LLM reasoning over student knowledge states.

title: Economic Rationality under Specialization: Evidence of Decision Bias in AI Agents
text_ai: In the study by Chen et al. (2023) [01], the large language model GPT demonstrated economic rationality comparable to or exceeding the average human level in tasks such as budget allocation and risk preference. However, these findings were obtained under generalist conditions, where the model operated without domain-specific fine-tuning or role constraints. In real-world deployment, AI agents are increasingly specialized—trained or prompted to perform narrow economic functions, such as trading, budgeting, or resource allocation. This specialization raises a critical question: does enhanced task focus preserve or distort rational decision-making? We investigate this by constructing a set of controlled experiments in which GPT-based agents are primed with specialized roles (e.g., “risk-minimizing fund manager” or “profit-maximizing trader”) and then tested on standard decision tasks involving framing effects, sunk costs, and intertemporal choice. Results reveal systematic deviations from expected utility theory. Specialized agents exhibit pronounced biases—such as heightened loss aversion in risk-focused roles and escalation of commitment in asset-allocation roles—that are absent or weaker in generalist counterparts. These biases are robust across prompt variations and model versions, suggesting a structural vulnerability in current AI architectures. Our findings challenge the assumption that economic rationality scales with specialization, with implications for the design and oversight of autonomous economic agents.

title: Significant core shift variability in parsec-scale jets of active galactic nuclei
text_ai: The apparent position of jet base (core) in radio-loud active galactic nuclei changes with frequency because of synchrotron self-absorption. Studying this `core shift` effect enables us to reconstruct properties of the jet regions close to the central engine. We present a multi-epoch, multifrequency very long baseline interferometry study of a sample of radio-loud active galactic nuclei, aimed at characterizing the variability of the core shift. Our analysis reveals that the frequency-dependent position of the jet base is not static but exhibits significant changes on timescales ranging from months to years. The magnitude of these variations often exceeds the measurement uncertainties, indicating intrinsic physical changes in the jet apex region. By combining data at 2.3, 5, 8.4, and 15 GHz over up to ten epochs, we derive time-dependent core shift vectors and use them to model the underlying jet magnetic field and particle density distribution. We find that the core shift variability correlates with flaring activity at high radio frequencies, suggesting that the observed shifts are driven by episodic injections of fresh plasma or by variations in the magnetic energy density near the central engine. Moreover, the temporal behavior of the core shift often deviates from simple scaling laws predicted by standard jet models, pointing to more complex, time-variable physical conditions. Our results demonstrate that core shift variability is a common phenomenon in parsec-scale jets and that its study provides a unique probe of the dynamic processes occurring within the innermost jet regions. This approach, when applied to larger samples and with higher cadence, can reveal the connection between core shift changes, jet power fluctuations, and the underlying accretion flow.

title: Measurement of the Higgs boson mass with $H \rightarrow \gamma\gamma$ decays in 140 fb$^{-1}$ of $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV $pp$ collisions with the ATLAS detector
text_ai: The mass of the Higgs boson is measured in the $H\to\gamma\gamma$ decay channel, exploiting the high resolution of the invariant mass of photon pairs reconstructed from the decays of Higgs bosons produced in proton-proton collisions at a centre-of-mass energy $\sqrt{s}=13$ TeV. The analysis uses the full 140 fb⁻¹ dataset collected by ATLAS. Photon pairs are selected with stringent criteria and a multivariate discriminant to enhance signal purity. The mass is extracted from a simultaneous fit to the diphoton invariant mass distribution in production categories, accounting for photon energy calibration and resolution. The measured mass is \(m_H = 124.94 \pm 0.17\) (stat) \(\pm 0.06\) (syst) GeV, with systematic uncertainties from the photon energy scale, background modeling, and experimental effects. The result is consistent with the world average and is the most precise measurement in the \(H\to\gamma\gamma\) channel. The uncertainty is dominated by the statistical component, with systematic uncertainties significantly reduced compared to previous analyses. This measurement further constrains Higgs boson properties and provides a stringent test of the Standard Model.

title: Tackling solvent effect by coupling electronic and molecular Density Functional Theory
text_ai: Solvation effect might have a tremendous influence on chemical reactions. However, precise quantum chemistry calculations are most often done either in vacuum neglecting the role of the solvent or using continuum solvent model ignoring its molecular nature. In this work, we propose a novel approach that couples electronic density functional theory (DFT) for the solute with classical molecular density functional theory (MDFT) for the solvent. This hybrid method captures both the quantum nature of the solute and the molecular structure of the solvent, including explicit solvation shells, hydrogen bonding, and entropic effects. The coupling uses an embedding potential derived from the solvent density, self-consistently updated with the solute electronic density. This allows integration of the two theories without averaging or continuum approximations. We apply the method to compute solvation free energies and reaction barriers for selected organic reactions in water. Results show that the coupled DFT/MDFT approach yields accuracy comparable to explicit QM/MM but at a fraction of the computational cost, while also providing molecular-level insights into solvent structuring around the solute. The method naturally accounts for non-electrostatic interactions such as dispersion and repulsion via the MDFT functional. We discuss numerical stability and convergence, and outline extensions to non-aqueous solvents and time-dependent processes. This work bridges the gap between quantum chemistry and liquid-state theory, offering a practical tool for solvent effects in a rigorous yet efficient manner.
